rawFindings.title: Telegram is still a login channel: passwordless session via bot, survives logout-all
rawFindings.rootCause: POST /api/auth/telegram/start (no auth) plus /poll call telegramLogin(), which issues access and refresh tokens for whichever account the chat is linked to, with no password. SocialLogin renders the Telegram button on /login. The FAQ (uz/ru/en) tells users to recover access by 'signing in with Telegram'. revokeUserSessions only bumps tokenVersion and never clears telegramChatId.
rawFindings.impact: Violates Rule A. Anyone holding a 15-min access token (XSS, shared PC) can POST /api/telegram/link with their own Telegram and keep permanent passwordless login. Logout-all and block/unblock do not remove it. The flow bypasses the email-based login-guard counter and shows the account email inside Telegram.
rawFindings.evidence: auth.routes.ts:137-158; auth.service.ts:176-181 (issueTokens, no password), :166-173 (revoke only bumps version); telegram.service.ts:123-190, 284-321; SocialLogin.tsx:90-116,145-154; login/+Page.tsx:97 (showTelegram default true); messages.en.ts:459, messages.uz.ts:465, messages.ru.ts:467; README.md:92,137.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Delete /api/auth/telegram/start and /poll, telegramLogin, loginTokens, handleLoginStart and the lgok/lgno callbacks, the SocialLogin Telegram button, the login.tg* strings and the README/FAQ text. Keep deep-link infrastructure only for verification, recovery and linking. Ship the Telegram recovery flow first so users relying on Telegram login are not locked out.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-010 (FIXED: confirm button only); ISSUE-122 (NOT FIXED, no test); D-039
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low code risk. UX risk for users who never set or forgot a password until recovery exists.

rawFindings.title: Link deep-link has no confirmation or binding: attacker account gets victim's verified phone, victim silently unlinked
rawFindings.rootCause: The link token is a bearer token bound only to userId. handleStart links on the first /start from any Telegram user, without showing which site account and without a confirm step. It then runs updateMany to detach that chat from any other account and immediately shows the contact-share keyboard.
rawFindings.impact: An attacker mints a link for their own account and sends it to a victim. The victim taps Start and shares a contact. The attacker account becomes isPhoneVerified with the victim's real phone, bypassing the anti-spam gate, and employers see the victim's number. The victim's own account silently loses its Telegram link and notifications. Once recovery is built on Telegram, this becomes a takeover primitive.
rawFindings.evidence: telegram.service.ts:93-101 (token -> userId only), :262-266, :269-273 (silent updateMany unlink, then link), :275-280 (generic 'Hisobingiz bog'landi!' plus CONTACT_KEYBOARD), :339-343. ISSUES.md ISSUE-010 impact names this 'link-token varianti', but its fix only touched login.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Two-step link. The bot shows the masked account (u***@mail.uz) and a short code also shown on the site, with Confirm/Cancel callbacks checked against from.id. Refuse if the Telegram user is already linked to another account instead of re-linking silently. Notify both accounts and write an audit event. Store telegramUserId (from.id) unique.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low; one extra bot step and i18n strings.

rawFindings.title: Phone uniqueness not enforced: one Telegram/SIM verifies unlimited accounts
rawFindings.rootCause: User.phone has no unique index, and handleContact never checks whether the phone is already verified on another account. Re-linking clears telegramChatId on the old account but leaves its phone and isPhoneVerified=true. DELETE /api/telegram/link also keeps the verification.
rawFindings.impact: Violates Rules E and F. Repeating link(A), share, link(B), share yields any number of verified seeker or employer accounts from one phone. That defeats requirePhoneVerified, the anti-spam control for apply, vacancy post, chat start and reviews. Duplicate phones also make future phone-based recovery ambiguous.
rawFindings.evidence: schema.prisma:163 `phone String?` (no @unique), :172-176 (uniqueness 'enforced by code', chat only); telegram.service.ts:269-273, 339-343; telegram.routes.ts:38-44; auth-guard.ts:90-103; applications.routes.ts:43; vacancies.routes.ts:156; chat.routes.ts:294; reviews.routes.ts:19.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Store the E.164 verified phone and telegramUserId with unique partial indexes (or a PhoneVerification collection with a unique phone). In handleContact, reject a phone already verified elsewhere with a generic reply that points to manual recovery. On re-link or unlink, reset the old account's verification or refuse the re-link.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: existing duplicate phones must be deduplicated before a unique index; demo seed uses sequential unique phones.

rawFindings.title: Phone change is a silent overwrite: no re-auth, notice, audit or session invalidation
rawFindings.rootCause: Any contact share from the linked chat overwrites User.phone. Switching Telegram accounts only needs an access token (POST link, or DELETE then POST). There is no password re-entry, no message to the previous chat or phone, no tokenVersion bump and no security event.
rawFindings.impact: Violates Rule G. A short-lived stolen access token lets an attacker permanently swap the account's verified phone and Telegram to their own. The owner is not told, and employers see the attacker's number. Combined with any future Telegram-based recovery, this is persistent takeover.
rawFindings.evidence: telegram.service.ts:323-350 (update phone and isPhoneVerified, previous value ignored); telegram.routes.ts:25-35 (link: requireAuth only), :38-44 (unlink); no revokeUserSessions call in the telegram module; profile.routes.ts:59-67 blocks only the site-side edit.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Dedicated phone-change flow: recent password re-auth, Telegram verification of the new number via a one-time payload, notice to the old chat, audit event, tokenVersion bump per the risk model, and a cooling-off period before the new phone can be used for recovery.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium; new endpoints and bot state.

rawFindings.title: Telegram password recovery (Rules B/I/J) not implemented; UI routes to /support and Telegram login
rawFindings.rootCause: No forgot, reset or change-password endpoints and no recovery-token model exist. 'Parolni unutdingizmi?' and the settings password row link to /support. The FAQ in all three languages suggests Telegram login instead. Google-created users get a random hash with a comment promising a later reset flow.
rawFindings.impact: Users who forget their password cannot recover. Google-only users can never set a password. The only self-service path is the Telegram login that Rule A forbids. Nothing invalidates sessions or challenges after a reset because none exists.
rawFindings.evidence: login/+Page.tsx:82-87; AccountSettings.tsx:87-88; auth.routes.ts:63-181 (register/login/refresh/logout/me/telegram/google only); schema.prisma model list has no token/recovery model; auth.service.ts:233-235; messages.uz.ts:465, messages.en.ts:459; docs/audit/DECISIONS.md D-010.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: RecoveryChallenge collection (sha256 tokenHash, purpose, userId, expiresAt ≤10 min with TTL index, usedAt, attempts). recovery/start {phone} always returns the same generic response plus a t.me link with a random 32-byte payload. The bot checks from.id against the stored telegramUserId and phone, then sends a one-time site return link. recovery/complete sets the password, bumps tokenVersion and deletes all challenges. Rate-limit by IP, phone and Telegram id. Emit audit events.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: new model, bot state machine, 2 pages x 3 languages.

rawFindings.title: No manual recovery request or admin verified phone reset (Rule H)
rawFindings.rootCause: No ManualRecoveryRequest model, user form, admin queue or admin action to reset a verified phone or Telegram. The admin API and UI support only list users, block and change role.
rawFindings.impact: A user who lost password, phone and Telegram has no path. Support can only edit the DB by hand, with no ownership check workflow, no forced session invalidation and no audit trail.
rawFindings.evidence: admin.routes.ts:136 (GET users), :190-215 (block), :217-225 (role), no other user mutations; admin/users/+Page.tsx:14 imports only fetchAdminUsers/setUserBlocked/setUserRole; AccountSettings.tsx:88 -> /support.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add a request form and admin queue with statuses. Admin action 'reset verified phone/Telegram' clears phone, telegramUserId and verification, bumps tokenVersion and revokes challenges. It must never set or show a password or token. Write audit entries with the admin id.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium; additive.

rawFindings.title: No security audit log for phone, Telegram, recovery or admin events (Rule L)
rawFindings.rootCause: No AuditLog or SecurityEvent model exists. Phone verification, Telegram link, silent re-link and unlink, and admin block and role changes only update the entity row.
rawFindings.impact: Takeover patterns (link CSRF, silent phone swap, one phone on many accounts) cannot be investigated or detected, and future manual recovery decisions cannot be proven. None of the Rule L events are recorded.
rawFindings.evidence: schema.prisma models 160-794 (no audit model); telegram.service.ts:269-273, 340-343; telegram.routes.ts:38-44; admin.routes.ts:190-225 (no event write).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: SecurityEvent collection {userId, actorId, type enum, ip, uaHash, meta with masked phone (last 4), createdAt} with a retention TTL. Write it from auth, phone, Telegram, recovery and admin actions. Add an admin read-only view. Use an allowlisted meta schema so tokens and passwords cannot be stored.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low; additive writes.

rawFindings.title: Phone gate depends on Telegram, but TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN is documented optional: core flows blocked without it
rawFindings.rootCause: requirePhoneVerified is unconditional, and the only writer of isPhoneVerified=true is the bot contact handler. env.ts makes the token optional with no production check. README says the project works fully without these services.
rawFindings.impact: If the token is missing, invalid or revoked, or Telegram is down for a long time, every unverified user is blocked from applying, posting vacancies, starting chats and reviewing. The UI only shows the gate at click time. Rule K requires an 'unavailable' state.
rawFindings.evidence: auth-guard.ts:90-103; grep `isPhoneVerified: true` finds only telegram.service.ts:342; gated routes applications.routes.ts:43, vacancies.routes.ts:156, chat.routes.ts:294, reviews.routes.ts:19; env.ts:57-58; README.md:130-137; .env.example:4-5,62.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Fail or loudly warn at boot in production when the token is empty. Document Telegram as required. Expose a verification-availability flag in /api/telegram/status and gate UIs with an i18n 'temporarily unavailable' message. No email fallback, per Rule K.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Bot availability is a one-time getMe flag; failing polling (401/409/network) still hands out links
rawFindings.rootCause: botUsername is set once after getMe and never cleared. getUpdates failures just pause 5 s and log. The link endpoint returns 503 only when botUsername is null. TelegramConnect ignores status.botUsername and shows the raw Uzbek server message.
rawFindings.impact: Users follow deep links that nobody processes (revoked token, second replica 409, outage) and wait with no feedback. A warn log is written every 5 s during a conflict. ru/en users see Uzbek text. Rule K is only partly met.
rawFindings.evidence: telegram.service.ts:436-461 (`if (!updates) { await pause(5000); continue; }`); telegram.routes.ts:20, 25-35; TelegramConnect.tsx:80-86 (err.message); lib/api.ts:920-927; DEPLOY.md:242-243.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Track lastPollOkAt and consecutive failures; mark the bot offline on repeated failures or 401/409 and stop the loop on 401. Return 503 TELEGRAM_UNAVAILABLE from link, verification and recovery endpoints. The UI maps the error code to i18n text and disables the actions. Rate-limit the warning logs.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Account identity keyed by chat.id with no private-chat check: group chats can be linked and verified
rawFindings.rootCause: handleStart, handleContact, handleLoginStart and handleCallbackQuery use msg.chat.id as the identity. They never check chat.type==='private' or use from.id. The callback check compares chat id, not the presser. `/start@Bot x` is parsed as payload '@Bot x'.
rawFindings.impact: If /start <token> is sent in a group (bots may join groups by default), the account is linked to the group. Any member who shares their own contact (as a reply) becomes that account's verified phone, and any member can press login confirm. Private chat previews and notifications then post into the group. This last part is an inference about Telegram group delivery under privacy mode.
rawFindings.evidence: telegram.service.ts:214-221 (TgMessage has no chat.type), :243-273 (chatId = msg.chat.id), :291-294 (entry.chatId === chatId), :328-343 (contact.user_id vs from.id, then lookup by chat), :397 (text.slice(6)); chat.routes.ts:84-89.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Ignore non-private chats for all account flows (generic reply). Store telegramUserId=from.id (unique) separately from chat id and compare from.id in callbacks and contacts. Disable 'Allow Groups' in BotFather as defense in depth.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Support relay: #u routing tag spoofable via first_name; no per-chat throttle; failures reported as success
rawFindings.rootCause: handleAdminReply routes to the FIRST /#u(-?\d+)/ in the replied text. The header places the sender's first_name (HTML-escaped only) before the real tag. There is no stored message_id-to-chat mapping. Every text from any Telegram user is relayed with no rate limit, send results are ignored, and the 4096-char limit is not considered.
rawFindings.impact: An attacker sets first_name to '#u<victimId>', so the admin's reply goes to the victim as an official 'Support javobi' (misdelivery or phishing). Anyone can flood the admin chat; the resulting 429 sleeps up to 30 s inside the single polling loop and stalls linking and verification for everyone. Long messages are dropped while the user is told 'qabul qilindi' and the admin 'Javob yuborildi'.
rawFindings.evidence: telegram.service.ts:365-373 (who = first_name, then #u tag), :377-386 (first match, result unchecked), :411 (all text relayed), :54-63 (retry_after sleep ≤30 s), :452-459 (sequential loop); support.routes.ts:121-123 (5/min per IP, spoofable with TRUST_PROXY=true by default).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Persist adminMessageId-to-chatId with a TTL and route by reply_to_message.message_id. Strip '#' from display names. Add a per-chat rate limit with a silent drop, truncate to fit 4096, and check send results. Move 429 retries to a send queue off the polling loop.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Deep-link tokens in unbounded in-memory Maps: weak rate limits, O(n) sweep, lost on restart, plaintext
rawFindings.rootCause: linkTokens (30-min TTL) and loginTokens are process Maps holding raw tokens. POST /api/telegram/link has only the global 600/min limit; /api/auth/telegram/start is unauthenticated at 10/min per IP, spoofable when TRUST_PROXY=true. Every create iterates the whole Map. The polling offset starts at 0 on boot.
rawFindings.impact: One account can hold ~18k live tokens per IP per 30 min, and spoofed IPs make growth unbounded, putting CPU and memory pressure on the single replica. Every deploy invalidates in-flight links. Restart re-delivers unconfirmed updates, duplicating support relays. The design does not meet Rule D/I needs (hashed, durable, atomic one-time use) for recovery payloads.
rawFindings.evidence: telegram.service.ts:90-110, 131-143 (Map plus full sweep), :439 (`let offset = 0`); telegram.routes.ts:25 (no rateLimit config); auth.routes.ts:59-61,137; env.ts:113-123 (TRUST_PROXY default true); server.ts:129-139.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: DB DeepLinkChallenge {payloadHash, purpose, userId?, telegramUserId?, expiresAt with a 10-min TTL index, usedAt}, consumed atomically with findOneAndUpdate. Payload is 32 random bytes in base64url. Cap active challenges per user, add per-route limits keyed by user and IP, and set TRUST_PROXY=1 on Railway.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium; new collection.

rawFindings.title: No way to unlink Telegram in UI; private chat previews sent to Telegram regardless of preferences
rawFindings.rootCause: DELETE /api/telegram/link has no web caller. deliverMessage calls notifyUserViaTelegram directly instead of notify(), and NotificationType has no message type, so the Telegram channel toggle never applies to chat messages.
rawFindings.impact: Phone verification effectively forces a Telegram link. After that a user cannot stop the first 200 chars of private messages going to Telegram, and cannot detach a lost or compromised Telegram from the site. The 'Telegram unlinked' flow in Rule L is unreachable.
rawFindings.evidence: lib/api.ts:909-927 (status and link POST only; grep 'telegram/link' finds one hit); telegram.routes.ts:38-44; chat.routes.ts:84-89; schema.prisma NotificationType enum (new_application, application_status_changed, new_vacancy_match, system); notifications.service.ts:52-61,87-90.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add an unlink action with re-auth, a message to the Telegram chat and an audit event. Route chat notifications through notify() with a message type or check the Telegram preference. Send 'new message' without the body preview by default.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Backup phone (Rule F) is unverified, non-unique free text; unverified primary phone accepts any string
rawFindings.rootCause: additionalPhone is a JobSeekerProfile string (max 30, no format, no verification, no uniqueness), and employers have no equivalent. Before verification, the primary phone PATCH saves an arbitrary string with no normalisation.
rawFindings.impact: Rule F (verified, unique backup phone usable for recovery) is not met. If recovery is later wired to this field, a stolen access token could set an attacker number as the backup. Rated P2 because recovery does not exist yet.
rawFindings.evidence: schema.prisma:217; profile.routes.ts:15-16, 59-67, 69-87; PersonalInfo.tsx:191-200.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Separate backupPhone on User, verified through the Telegram challenge, under the same uniqueness index as the primary phone, with an audit event and a notice to the primary channel. Never recover via an unverified number. Normalise to E.164 server-side.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low; data migration for existing additionalPhone values.

rawFindings.title: Plain /start sends no site link; /myid exposes config hint; bot texts Uzbek-only
rawFindings.rootCause: The welcome message gives instructions but no WEB_ORIGIN link. /myid and /id answer anyone with their chat id and mention '.env TELEGRAM_ADMIN_CHAT_ID'. All bot replies are hardcoded Uzbek, and from.language_code is ignored.
rawFindings.impact: Rule C not met. Minor disclosure of deployment internals. ru/en users get Uzbek messages. The invalid-payload reply is generic and safe (OK).
rawFindings.evidence: telegram.service.ts:252-259 (welcome, no URL), :263-265 (generic invalid-payload reply), :398-403 (/myid).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Welcome message with an inline URL button to env.WEB_ORIGIN, localised by language_code. Remove /myid or allow it only when TELEGRAM_ADMIN_CHAT_ID is unset.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Very low.

rawFindings.title: TRUST_PROXY trusts every proxy by default, so a spoofed X-Forwarded-For bypasses every per-IP rate limit
rawFindings.rootCause: TRUST_PROXY defaults to "true" (env.ts:113-123) and goes straight into Fastify trustProxy (server.ts:77). req.ip therefore comes from the client-controlled X-Forwarded-For header, and @fastify/rate-limit keys on req.ip (server.ts:129-139). Operators are only advised to set "1" after checking hops (.env.example:49-52, DEPLOY.md:70). The earlier audit probe found Railway does not strip client X-Forwarded-For (D-007); not re-verified here.
rawFindings.impact: Rotating X-Forwarded-For bypasses the register limit (10/min), /api/auth/telegram/start, /api/auth/google, /refresh and the global 600/min limit. That allows mass signups, unlimited Telegram token creation and request floods. Rule I needs working rate limits on recovery request, Telegram verification and password reset, and any limiter keyed on req.ip inherits this bypass. Only login has an email-keyed fallback.
rawFindings.evidence: env.ts:116 .default("true"); env.ts:119 "true" becomes true; server.ts:77 trustProxy: env.TRUST_PROXY; server.ts:129-131 rateLimit with default req.ip key; auth.routes.ts:59-61,64,137,164 strictRateLimit; .env.example:52 TRUST_PROXY=true; D-007 probe: 12 different X-Forwarded-For values produced no 429.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Log req.ips once on Railway to measure the hop count, then set TRUST_PROXY=1 (or the proxy CIDR) for production. Refuse to start in production when TRUST_PROXY=true. Key auth and recovery limits on normalized phone/email plus IP, stored persistently.
rawFindings.fixRisk: A wrong hop count puts every user behind the proxy IP and 429s the whole site. Verify with a canary deploy.

rawFindings.title: Unauthenticated /api/auth/telegram/start grows an uncapped in-memory Map and sweeps all of it on every call (CPU DoS)
rawFindings.rootCause: createLoginToken loops over the entire loginTokens Map on every call to evict expired entries, and the Map has no size cap (telegram.service.ts:131-143). The only guard is strictRateLimit, 10/min per req.ip (auth.routes.ts:137), which spoofed X-Forwarded-For bypasses under the default TRUST_PROXY. Entries live 5 minutes, and the API runs as one instance (railway.json:13).
rawFindings.impact: About 1k req/s with rotating X-Forwarded-For keeps roughly 300k live entries, so every new request walks 300k entries on the event loop. That can stall the only API process for all users (the numbers are an estimate). The endpoint also keeps Telegram as a login channel, which rule A forbids; .env.example:61 still advertises 'Telegram orqali kirish'.
rawFindings.evidence: telegram.service.ts:131 const loginTokens = new Map; :136-139 for (const [k,v] of loginTokens) deletes expired entries on each create; :141 set() with no limit; auth.routes.ts:137-147 route needs no auth, only that the bot is online; linkTokens uses the same pattern (:90-102) but requires auth; server.ts:77 trustProxy.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Remove the Telegram login endpoints (rule A). Build the replacement verification/recovery challenges as Mongo rows: hashed random token, TTL index for expiry (no manual sweep), atomic consume, and a cap on pending challenges per phone and IP. Fix TRUST_PROXY as well.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-010 (FIXED: confirm step only), ISSUE-079 (FIXED: shutdown only), ISSUE-011
rawFindings.fixRisk: The web SocialLogin Telegram button (SocialLogin.tsx:90-116) must be removed in the same change.

rawFindings.title: ADMIN_EMAIL bootstrap promotes any existing account with that email to admin on every boot
rawFindings.rootCause: ensureAdminUser runs on every start (server.ts:271). If a user with ADMIN_EMAIL already exists and is not admin, it sets role=admin without checking who created the account or whether the email was verified (ensure-admin.ts:23-29). Registration never verifies email ownership: registerUser leaves isEmailVerified false (auth.service.ts:37-73; ISSUE-042).
rawFindings.impact: Whoever registers the address first (e.g. admin@<domain>), before the operator puts it in ADMIN_EMAIL, becomes admin with their own password at the next deploy. That grants every user's data, moderation, and the planned manual recovery powers (rule H). Demoting the account via PATCH /api/admin/users/:id/role (admin.routes.ts:217-225) is silently undone on the next restart.
rawFindings.evidence: ensure-admin.ts:23 findUnique({ where: { email } }); :25-27 if role !== 'admin' then update to admin; server.ts:271 await ensureAdminUser(app.log) runs in bootstrap on every boot; auth.service.ts:37-73 registerUser has no email verification; .env.example:54-57 says an existing user is promoted.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Only create the admin when no user with that email exists; never promote an existing account automatically (log a warning instead). Handle deliberate promotion through a one-off CLI script, and emit an audit event.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-096 (PARTIAL, covers only password length), ISSUE-042 (PARTIAL)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low. Operators who relied on auto-promotion must use the script instead.

rawFindings.title: Email-keyed login lockout lets anyone block password login for any known email (violates rule I)
rawFindings.rootCause: After 10 failures for an email within 15 minutes, assertLoginAllowed throws 429 before the password is even checked (login-guard.ts:12-36; auth.service.ts:93). The counter is global per email, ignores IP and client, and counts failures from anyone.
rawFindings.impact: An unauthenticated attacker sends 10 bad logins every 15 minutes and the victim (any known employer or admin email) cannot log in; the correct password also gets 429. No password recovery exists yet, so the victim has no way back in. This is the easy account-denial model rule I forbids. The counter is also in memory and resets on restart.
rawFindings.evidence: login-guard.ts:13 MAX_FAILURES = 10; :27-35 throws TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS once count >= 10; auth.service.ts:93 assertLoginAllowed(normalized) runs before findUnique/argon2.verify; :97 and :103 recordLoginFailure for unknown user and wrong password; D-007 Risk section already names the lockout DoS and leaves it for an owner decision.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Key failures on email plus IP/subnet, with a looser global per-email ceiling that adds delay or a challenge instead of a hard block. Let a login from a known-good device through. Persist counters in Mongo with a TTL, and log a security event when a threshold trips.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Needs the TRUST_PROXY fix at the same time, or IP rotation defeats the per-IP part.

rawFindings.title: The refresh session depends on a third-party cookie, which Safari/iOS and Brave block in the documented Vercel+Railway setup
rawFindings.rootCause: The API on *.up.railway.app sets the refresh cookie with SameSite=None; Secure (auth.routes.ts:41-46). The web app on another origin reads it through a credentialed cross-site fetch (session.ts:118-125). vercel.app and up.railway.app are separate sites (both are on the Public Suffix List), so this is a third-party cookie. DEPLOY.md documents exactly this setup (3-15, 51, 63) and only mentions a custom domain for the web app (146-151).
rawFindings.impact: Safari (third-party cookie blocking since 13.1), Brave and Chrome Incognito never store or send the cookie. After login, the access token in localStorage (session.ts:96-104) lasts at most 15 minutes; then refresh returns null and the user drops to guest. The 30-day session is effectively broken for iOS/Safari users. This follows documented browser behaviour and was not browser-tested here.
rawFindings.evidence: auth.routes.ts:43 sameSite: isProd ? "none" : "lax"; :45 path "/api/auth"; session.ts:120-125 fetch(`${API_URL}/api/auth/refresh`, {credentials:"include"}); jwt.ts:36 access token expiresIn 15m; DEPLOY.md:51 Generate Domain for the API; apps/web/.env.example:3 VITE_API_URL=https://ishbor-api.up.railway.app; e2e-check.mjs:212-218 only asserts SameSite=None.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Put the API on a same-site subdomain (api.<domain>) next to the web app on <domain>, document it as required, then switch the cookie to SameSite=Lax/Strict. Alternatively, proxy /api through the web origin so the cookie is first-party.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: none (ISSUE-097 covers only the CSRF angle of this cookie)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Domain change means updating WEB_ORIGIN, VITE_API_URL and CORS lists, and every user re-logs in once.

rawFindings.title: prestart runs prisma db push on every boot; the unique indexes needed for the new phone/Telegram rules will crash-loop the API
rawFindings.rootCause: npm start runs prestart `prisma db push --skip-generate` before node starts (package.json:14, railway.json:8), and there is no separate release step. Rules E/F require unique primary phone, backup phone and Telegram identity. User.phone is not unique and the bot writes it without a duplicate check (telegram.service.ts:339-343). The schema itself notes that a Mongo unique index treats all nulls as equal (schema.prisma:172-176).
rawFindings.impact: Once @unique is added to phone or telegramChatId, db push fails on existing duplicates or multiple nulls. npm start then exits, Railway retries 10 times (railway.json:11-12), and the only instance stays down. Index builds on collections with hundreds of thousands of rows also run before listen, inside the 120s healthcheck window. Any schema edit reaches production unreviewed.
rawFindings.evidence: package.json:14 "prestart": "prisma db push --skip-generate"; railway.json:8-13 npm run start, healthcheckTimeout 120, ON_FAILURE x10, numReplicas 1; schema.prisma:163 `phone String?` without @unique; schema.prisma:172-176 comment on null collisions; telegram.service.ts:340-343 sets phone and isPhoneVerified without a duplicate check; DEPLOY.md:103-106.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Remove prestart and run db push as a gated release step (Railway preDeployCommand or a manual step). Write a cleanup script for duplicate phones first. Enforce uniqueness through a separate binding collection (e.g. PhoneBinding {phoneE164 @unique, userId}) so nulls never collide.
rawFindings.fixRisk: If the manual push is forgotten, new indexes are missing. Add it to the deploy checklist.

rawFindings.title: No Content-Security-Policy on the web origin, so any XSS there means full account takeover
rawFindings.rootCause: All web delivery paths set only nosniff, X-Frame-Options, COOP and Referrer-Policy, never a CSP (vercel.json:20-33, api/ssr.js:15-20, server/index.mjs:40-45, vite.config.ts:8-13). The access token is in localStorage (session.ts:96-104), and the web origin has credentialed CORS to /api/auth/refresh. A CSP is feasible: the only inline script is the theme init (HeadDefault.tsx:57, theme.tsx:63), plus the GIS script (SocialLogin.tsx:76-77). The API CSP keeps script 'unsafe-inline' even though the API serves no HTML (server.ts:88).
rawFindings.impact: One injection in user-generated content (vacancies, companies, articles, chat; ISSUE-005 was a real case) can read the token or call refresh. That includes admins, since /admin is on the same origin. The planned password-reset page and recovery return link would also sit on this unprotected origin.
rawFindings.evidence: vercel.json:20-33 header list has no Content-Security-Policy; ssr.js:15-20; server/index.mjs:40-45; session.ts:99 localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, token); HeadDefault.tsx:57 inline script; SocialLogin.tsx:77 loads https://accounts.google.com/gsi/client; server.ts:88 scriptSrc includes 'unsafe-inline'.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Define one shared header set used by all targets. Start in Report-Only, then enforce: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'sha256-<theme script>' https://accounts.google.com/gsi/client; connect-src 'self' <API origin> wss://<API host> https://accounts.google.com/gsi/; frame-src https://accounts.google.com; img-src 'self' data: https:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'. Remove 'unsafe-inline' from the API CSP.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium. Check Vike's injected scripts in the built HTML; a wrong policy breaks theme init, GIS or WebSocket.

rawFindings.title: Auth-critical state lives only in process memory: lost on every restart and wrong with more than one instance
rawFindings.rootCause: All of these are per-process: Telegram link/login tokens (telegram.service.ts:90,131), the login failure counter (login-guard.ts:16), the rate-limit memory store (server.ts:129), the WS socket registry (realtime.ts:14), caches (cache.ts:11-13), the alert sweep 'running' flag (alerts.service.ts:107) and the getUpdates offset (telegram.service.ts:439). Correctness is assumed from numReplicas: 1 (railway.json:13, DEPLOY.md:95-101).
rawFindings.impact: Every deploy, crash or prestart retry cancels pending Telegram link/verification flows and resets brute-force counters and rate limits. The API cannot scale horizontally. The rule B/D/I recovery design (one-time, replay-protected, hashed-at-rest tokens) cannot reuse this pattern: raw tokens in a Map are not hashed, and replay protection disappears on restart.
rawFindings.evidence: telegram.service.ts:88 comment says keeping tokens in memory is enough because bot and API share one process; :90 and :131 Maps; login-guard.ts:9 assumes a single API instance; cache.ts:11-13; realtime.ts:14; alerts.service.ts:107 let running = false; railway.json:13; DEPLOY.md:97-101.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Store challenges and recovery tokens in Mongo: sha256 of the token, purpose, userId, expiresAt with a TTL index, and consumedAt set atomically via findOneAndUpdate. Persist throttles the same way. Keep caches and the WS registry in memory, but document them. Move the bot and scheduler into a single-writer worker before scaling out.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-079 (FIXED for shutdown only; the state itself was not addressed)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low to medium: adds small DB writes on auth paths.

rawFindings.title: CORS preflights are not cached, so every authenticated browser API call pays an extra OPTIONS round trip
rawFindings.rootCause: CORS is registered without maxAge (server.ts:117-127). The plugin default is null, so no Access-Control-Max-Age header is sent (@fastify/cors 9.0.1 index.js:18, 248-249), and browsers cache a preflight for only about 5s per URL. Every call with Authorization: Bearer or a JSON body needs a preflight, and the web and API are on different origins.
rawFindings.impact: Logged-in pages (dashboards, chat, notifications) make roughly double the round trips. Users in Uzbekistan reaching a Railway region pay one extra round trip per distinct URL (about 100-250 ms, estimated), and the single API instance handles extra requests.
rawFindings.evidence: server.ts:117-127 register(cors, { origin(...), credentials: true }) with no maxAge; node_modules/@fastify/cors/index.js:18 `maxAge: null`; index.js:248-249 only sends Access-Control-Max-Age when maxAge is not null; session.ts:9 all API calls carry a Bearer token.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add maxAge: 600 (Chrome caps it at 7200). Longer term, a same-site API or an /api proxy through the web origin removes preflights entirely.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: a change to the origin allowlist takes up to maxAge to reach browsers.

rawFindings.title: COOP same-origin on the web may break the Google Sign-In popup callback
rawFindings.rootCause: Every web response sends Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin (vercel.json:26, ssr.js:18, server/index.mjs:43, vite.config.ts:11). SocialLogin uses GIS initialize + renderButton with a JavaScript callback and no ux_mode, i.e. the default popup flow (SocialLogin.tsx:51-69). Google's guidance is same-origin-allow-popups for popup flows, because same-origin cuts the popup's link back to the page. This is an inference from the GIS docs and was not browser-tested.
rawFindings.impact: Google login, the only primary login besides email/password, can fail silently wherever GIS uses the popup instead of FedCM (likely non-Chromium browsers): the popup closes and the callback never runs.
rawFindings.evidence: vercel.json:26 Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin; api/ssr.js:18; server/index.mjs:43; vite.config.ts:11; SocialLogin.tsx:51-69 google.accounts.id.initialize({client_id, callback}) followed by renderButton.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Test Google login in Safari and Firefox on a preview deploy. If it fails, send same-origin-allow-popups (at least on auth pages) or enable FedCM for the button (use_fedcm_for_button).
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: same-origin-allow-popups keeps most of the isolation.

rawFindings.title: The global per-IP rate limit also throttles SSR, which reaches the API from shared Vercel egress IPs
rawFindings.rootCause: The global limit is 600/min per req.ip (server.ts:129-131, env.ts:54-56). SSR data fetches call the API directly, without forwarding the client IP or any trusted SSR identity (apps/web/src/lib/api.ts:75,339,376; 'forwarded' appears nowhere in apps/web). All SSR traffic from one egress IP therefore shares one bucket. The env.ts:54-55 comment acknowledges shared SSR IPs and only raises the limit.
rawFindings.impact: Crawling tens of thousands of vacancy and company pages, at about 3-4 API calls per SSR page, can exceed 600/min per egress IP. The API then returns 429 and SSR shows error or empty pages to users and Googlebot. Vercel egress sharing was not measured, so this is an inference. Simply forwarding X-Forwarded-For would instead let clients spoof their key while TRUST_PROXY=true.
rawFindings.evidence: server.ts:129-139 rateLimit({max: env.RATE_LIMIT_MAX}) with no allowList or keyGenerator; env.ts:54-56 comment about shared SSR IPs; apps/web/src/lib/api.ts:75 fetch(`${API_URL}${path}`) sends no client-IP headers.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Have SSR send a server-only secret header (not a VITE_ variable). The rate limiter can then allowList SSR or key on a signed client IP. Keep strict per-IP limits for browsers, and cache public responses.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low, provided the secret never reaches the client bundle.

rawFindings.title: Secret-bearing URLs get logged: the self-hosted web server logs raw invite tokens, and API redaction only knows fixed parameter names
rawFindings.rootCause: The self-hosted web server uses Fastify's default request serializer at info level, which logs the full req.url (server/index.mjs:50-51). The staff invite page carries its secret as /admin/invite?token=... (pages/admin/invite/+Page.tsx:4). The API redacts only query params named token or access_token, plus the /api/staff-invites/ path (server.ts:54-58).
rawFindings.impact: Staff invite tokens already land in self-hosted web logs. The recovery return link and Telegram verification URLs from rules B/D will be logged in plain text unless they reuse exactly those names, which breaks rule L. Vercel request logs probably include the query string too (inference).
rawFindings.evidence: server/index.mjs:50-51 logger { level: LOG_LEVEL ?? 'info' } with no serializers or redact; pages/admin/invite/+Page.tsx:4 `/admin/invite?token=...`; server.ts:54-58 redactUrl regex covers only token/access_token and /api/staff-invites/.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Strip the whole query string in both loggers by default, with an allowlist of safe params. Put recovery tokens in the URL fragment or a POST body instead of the query string, and add an e2e test that scrapes logs for tokens.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: logs carry less debugging context.

rawFindings.title: Production hardening depends only on NODE_ENV (default development), so a missing value starts prod with the public example JWT secrets
rawFindings.rootCause: NODE_ENV defaults to 'development' (env.ts:28), and the secret-length, distinct-secret and placeholder checks return early unless it is production (env.ts:138-157). The base minimum is 8 characters (env.ts:41-42), which the .env.example placeholders pass (.env.example:20-21). The same flag also controls cookie Secure/SameSite, localhost CORS origins (env.ts:182), HSTS and CSP 'unsafe-eval'. WEB_ORIGIN defaults to http://localhost:5173 and is never validated (env.ts:47).
rawFindings.impact: If NODE_ENV is unset (Nixpacks probably sets it; another builder may not), the API runs with publicly known HS256 secrets. Anyone can then mint tokens for any user id: 'v' is optional (auth-guard.ts:56) and tokens without exp are accepted. Telegram, email and future recovery links would point to localhost.
rawFindings.evidence: env.ts:28 NODE_ENV default 'development'; :41-42 min(8); :138 `if (cfg.NODE_ENV !== "production") return;`; :47 WEB_ORIGIN defaults to localhost; :182 localhost origins added when not production; .env.example:20-21 placeholder secrets; auth-guard.ts:56 'v' optional.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Reject placeholder secrets and anything shorter than 32 characters regardless of NODE_ENV. When RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT or VERCEL is set, require explicit NODE_ENV=production and an https WEB_ORIGIN. Check that WEB_ORIGIN and CORS_EXTRA_ORIGINS are bare origins.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: local .env files with short secrets need new values.

rawFindings.title: Web header gaps across deploy targets: no Permissions-Policy, no HSTS when self-hosted, risky HSTS preload, duplicated header lists
rawFindings.rootCause: The security header list is copy-pasted into vite.config.ts:8-13, api/ssr.js:15-20 and server/index.mjs:40-45, with a fourth copy in vercel.json:20-33. None sets Permissions-Policy. HSTS exists only in vercel.json:28-31, with includeSubDomains and preload. api/seo.js fetches the API with no timeout (seo.js:39-41).
rawFindings.impact: Self-hosted deploys get no HSTS. Preload with includeSubDomains on a custom apex forces HTTPS on every subdomain and is hard to undo. Camera, microphone and geolocation are not restricted. The four copies drift. A hung API holds robots.txt and sitemap requests until the function times out.
rawFindings.evidence: server/index.mjs:40-45 and api/ssr.js:15-20 have no HSTS or Permissions-Policy; vercel.json:28-31 `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload`; vite.config.ts:8-13; seo.js:39-41 fetch without a signal.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Use one shared headers module (which can also carry the CSP) in every target. Add Permissions-Policy (camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()) and HSTS on the self-hosted server. Remove preload until the domain is final. Add AbortSignal.timeout to seo.js.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Shutdown skips Telegram update acknowledgement and does not wait for in-flight work; the self-hosted web shutdown has no timeout
rawFindings.rootCause: The getUpdates offset starts at 0 in memory, and Telegram only treats updates as acknowledged on the next getUpdates call (telegram.service.ts:439-459). stopTelegramBot just sets a flag, so the last processed batch is never acknowledged. The API shutdown calls prisma.$disconnect without waiting for an in-flight alert sweep (server.ts:303-311; alerts.service.ts:113-120). server/index.mjs:134-140 has no forced-exit timer or guard against a second signal.
rawFindings.impact: After each deploy or restart, Telegram re-delivers the last batch: support messages are relayed twice, /start users get 'Havola eskirgan', and contact shares are processed again. An alert sweep running during shutdown fails mid-way once Prisma disconnects. A hung web server depends on the platform's SIGKILL.
rawFindings.evidence: telegram.service.ts:439 `let offset = 0`; :442-459 offset only advances in memory; :465-467 stopTelegramBot sets stopped = true; server.ts:303-311 stop functions, then app.close, then prisma.$disconnect; alerts.service.ts:113-120 running flag with no awaitable handle; server/index.mjs:134-140.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: On stop, call getUpdates once with offset = last update_id + 1 and timeout 0 (or persist the offset). Await the running sweep, with a time bound, before disconnecting. Add the same 10s forced-exit timer to server/index.mjs.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: docker-compose publishes unauthenticated MongoDB and keyless Meilisearch on all host interfaces
rawFindings.rootCause: Mongo runs with --bind_ip_all and publishes 27017:27017 with no auth. Meilisearch runs with MEILI_ENV=development, no master key, on 7700:7700 (docker-compose.yml:19-21, 38-42). Docker publishes these ports on 0.0.0.0.
rawFindings.impact: On shared Wi-Fi, anyone on the LAN can read or write the dev database (which may hold copies of real data used in audits) and the search index. Development only.
rawFindings.evidence: docker-compose.yml:19 command ["--replSet","rs0","--bind_ip_all"]; :20-21 ports "27017:27017"; :38-42 MEILI_ENV development, no MEILI_MASTER_KEY, ports "7700:7700".
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Bind to 127.0.0.1 ("127.0.0.1:27017:27017"), set Mongo root credentials, and set MEILI_MASTER_KEY.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: local DATABASE_URL needs the credentials.

rawFindings.title: Candidate PDF resumes are unauthenticated bearer URLs: no authorization, publicly cacheable, logged, never expire
rawFindings.rootCause: fastifyStatic serves all of UPLOAD_DIR at /uploads/ with no auth (server.ts:174), including resume-<32hex>.pdf. Access control is URL secrecy only. @fastify/send defaults to 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=0' (SendStream.js:874-875), CORP is cross-origin (server.ts:103), and PDFs get no sandbox or Content-Disposition (server.ts:168). The Fastify req serializer logs the full URL (server.ts:66) and redactUrl only strips token params, so every resume fetch puts a working link in the logs.
rawFindings.impact: Anyone who ever obtains the URL can download the resume (phone, address, work history) indefinitely until the candidate replaces or deletes it. Leak paths: log viewers, shared caches or proxies, forwarded links, and employers or admins after the application is rejected. This is weaker than the rule 'candidate private data goes only to authorized employers'. There is no audit trail of who downloaded it.
rawFindings.evidence: profile.routes.ts:109 saveUpload(..., 'resume-', ['pdf']) returns public /uploads URL; applications.routes.ts:294 returns jobSeekerProfile.resumeUrl to the vacancy owner or admin; e2e-check.mjs:1602 fetches the PDF with no auth header and expects 200; D-013 Risk: 'PDF rezyume hali ham URL'ni bilgan har kimga ochiq'; server.ts:54-58 redactUrl does not cover /uploads/resume-*.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Move resumes out of the static root (a separate dir or prefix that fastifyStatic does not serve). Add GET /api/profile/resume/file for the owner and GET /api/applications/:id/resume-file for the owning employer of that application's vacancy (with the ownership check). Stream with Cache-Control: private, no-store, Content-Disposition: attachment (or inline with a cookieless download domain), and CORP same-site. Stop returning raw resumeUrl to employers. Until then, add /uploads/resume-* to log redaction and set private, no-store for .pdf.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: web ResumeFile.tsx link and any employer consumer must switch to authorized fetch (blob URL) since the anchor cannot send the Bearer token; existing resumeUrl values need backward-compatible mapping.

rawFindings.title: Uploaded PDF resume never reaches employers in the web UI; only an unused endpoint leaks its permanent link
rawFindings.rootCause: The employer UI loads GET /api/employer/applications (web lib/employer/applications/api.ts:21). Its jobSeekerProfile select (applications.routes.ts:192-204) has no resumeUrl, and the web adapter (lib/employer/applications/adapter.ts:97-172 mapResume) has no file field. Only GET /api/vacancies/:id/applications (applications.routes.ts:238-300), which the web never calls, returns resumeUrl (line 294).
rawFindings.impact: Candidates upload a PDF in the resume wizard (ResumeWizard.tsx:192, ResumeFile.tsx), but the employers they apply to cannot see it. Meanwhile, anyone calling the raw per-vacancy API gets a permanent public link. Access is both too broad (see bearer URL finding) and missing for the legitimate audience.
rawFindings.evidence: grep resumeUrl in apps/web/src: only profile components (ResumeFile.tsx:84, ProfileOverview.tsx:88, useProfileData.ts:113), none in employer components; applications.routes.ts:294 'resumeUrl: true' only in the per-vacancy endpoint.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Decide the product flow. If employers should see the PDF, expose a boolean hasResumeFile plus an authorized download endpoint scoped to the application (see bearer URL finding) and render a 'Download PDF' action in the employer ApplicationDetail. Otherwise remove resumeUrl from /api/vacancies/:id/applications.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: additive UI plus endpoint; removing the field from the unused endpoint has no web consumer.

rawFindings.title: Multipart parser buffers unlimited non-file fields before the file part (memory DoS by any logged-in user)
rawFindings.rootCause: Multipart is registered with limits {fileSize 5MB, files 1} only. @fastify/multipart 8.3.1 defaults parts to 1000 (index.js:51); @fastify/busboy defaults fieldSize to 1MB and fields to Infinity (multipart.js:56-60). onField stores every field value in the in-memory body object (index.js:326-344). req.file() (index.js:512-521) skips fields until the first file, so all preceding fields are held in heap. Fastify bodyLimit does not apply to multipart streams.
rawFindings.impact: Inference, not executed: one request to /api/profile/resume or /api/employer/company/logo carrying about 999 fields of 1MB before the file makes the API buffer about 1GB of strings. That can OOM the single Railway instance and take the platform down. The 20/min per-route rate limit does not bound per-request memory.
rawFindings.evidence: server.ts:140 `await app.register(multipart, { limits: { fileSize: 5 * 1024 * 1024, files: 1 } })`; node_modules/@fastify/multipart/index.js:51 `parts: options.limits?.parts || 1000`; node_modules/@fastify/busboy/lib/types/multipart.js:56 `fieldSize ... 1 * 1024 * 1024`, :59 `fields ... Infinity`.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Set explicit limits: { fileSize: 5MB, files: 1, fields: 5, fieldSize: 1024, parts: 6, headerPairs: 50 }. Optionally reject any non-file part in saveUpload callers.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-043 (upload limits; FIXED for rate limit/type, not for field limits)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: web upload forms send a single file part.

rawFindings.title: Web origin still has no Content-Security-Policy while the access token lives in localStorage
rawFindings.rootCause: All three header sources set only nosniff, X-Frame-Options, COOP and Referrer-Policy (plus HSTS on Vercel): vercel.json:20-33, server/index.mjs SECURITY_HEADERS, api/ssr.js:15-20, vite.config.ts:8-13. The access token is persisted in localStorage (lib/auth/session.ts:99).
rawFindings.impact: No XSS sink is currently exploitable: JsonLd is escaped, markdown and chat renderers are href-allowlisted, and nothing else uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML. But any future injection (a new renderer, a dependency bug) would run with full access to the token and API. There is no second line of defense or violation reporting.
rawFindings.evidence: vercel.json headers list has no CSP key; server/index.mjs:39-44 and api/ssr.js:15-20 identical four headers; session.ts:99 `window.localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, token)`; ISSUES.md:112 ISSUE-078 NOT FIXED.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Start with Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'sha256-<THEME_INIT_SCRIPT>' https://accounts.google.com; connect-src 'self' <API_URL> wss://<API_HOST> https://accounts.google.com; img-src 'self' data: https:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com; font-src 'self' data: https://fonts.gstatic.com; frame-src https://accounts.google.com; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'. Keep the three header sources identical, then enforce.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: a wrong policy breaks Google login, the theme init script or the Vite preload; roll out Report-Only first.

rawFindings.title: API CSP allows inline scripts on the origin that holds the refresh cookie
rawFindings.rootCause: helmet contentSecurityPolicy sets scriptSrc to ['self', 'unsafe-inline'] (plus unsafe-eval in dev) for every API response, although the API serves no HTML (only JSON, PNG, XML, text). The /uploads sandbox relies on the served Content-Type allowlist in onSend (server.ts:163-173).
rawFindings.impact: Defense-in-depth only. Any future HTML-producing route, content-type mistake or static file type outside the sandbox logic would run inline script on the API origin. There, POST /api/auth/refresh with the cookie yields an access token (the original ISSUE-002 chain).
rawFindings.evidence: server.ts:88 `scriptSrc: ["'self'", "'unsafe-inline'", ...(isProd ? [] : ["'unsafe-eval'"])]`; grep 'text/html' in apps/api/src returns nothing.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: For the API use default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none' (no script-src needed). Keep the /uploads sandbox header as is.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-078 (API part of recommendation), ISSUE-002, ISSUE-106
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: API returns no HTML; verify the dev Vite proxy does not rely on API CSP.

rawFindings.title: Orphaned upload files are never cleaned and stay publicly reachable (races, failed writes, unsaved covers, .part temps)
rawFindings.rootCause: Each upload is saved first, then the previous URL is read and replaced without atomicity (profile.routes.ts:109-119; companies.routes.ts:152-167). Two concurrent uploads both read the same previous URL, so one new file is never referenced or deleted. A DB error after saveUpload leaves the file behind. POST /api/admin/articles/cover (articles.admin.routes.ts:283-292) stores covers that are removed only when an article later references and replaces them. saveUpload streams to <prefix><id>.part inside the served dir (uploads.ts:77-85), so a crash mid-stream leaves it. There is no sweeper.
rawFindings.impact: Disk growth on the Railway volume over time. An orphaned resume PDF remains downloadable by anyone holding its URL even after the candidate deletes their resume.
rawFindings.evidence: profile.routes.ts:111 findUnique previous after saveUpload, :113 upsert, :119 removeUploadedFile(previous); companies.routes.ts:158-165 same pattern using company.logoUrl read before upload; articles.admin.routes.ts:290 returns url with no DB record; uploads.ts:77 temp path in UPLOAD_DIR.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Write temp files to a non-served dir (os.tmpdir or UPLOAD_DIR/.tmp excluded from static). On DB failure, unlink the new file. Record uploads in an Upload collection (owner, prefix, createdAt, referenced) and run a periodic sweep removing unreferenced files older than 24h. Use findOneAndUpdate-style compare-and-set when replacing.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-029, ISSUE-107, D-013 (old/demo files not deleted)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: sweeper must whitelist demo- prefix and referenced URLs.

rawFindings.title: Images are stored byte-for-byte: EXIF/GPS metadata published and no pixel-dimension limit
rawFindings.rootCause: saveUpload validates only the first 16 bytes (uploads.ts:91-103) and renames the original stream to its final name (:105-106). No decode or re-encode, metadata strip, or width/height check for png, jpg or webp.
rawFindings.impact: Inference: photos uploaded as company logos or article covers keep camera and GPS EXIF, which is served publicly and cross-origin. A 5MB PNG/WebP with extreme dimensions (a decompression bomb) is shown on public catalog and company pages and can freeze or crash visitors' browsers, especially on mobile.
rawFindings.evidence: uploads.ts:81 `pipeline(file.file, fs.createWriteStream(temp))`; :99 `detectFileKind(head...)`; :106 `fs.promises.rename(temp, ...)`; companies.routes.ts:158 and articles.admin.routes.ts:290 accept png/jpg/webp this way.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Re-encode images server-side (e.g. sharp: read metadata, reject width*height > ~25MP, resize logos to <=512px and covers to <=2000px, output WebP without metadata). The PDF path is unchanged.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium: adds a native dependency (sharp) to the Railway build; the output file extension may change (the URL is returned from the API, so it is transparent).

rawFindings.title: Telegram support reply routing trusts the first '#u<id>' in user-influenced text
rawFindings.rootCause: handleAdminReply takes the first #u(-?\d+) match in the replied-to message and sends the admin's reply there. handleSupport puts user-controlled text before the real marker (`Kimdan: ${tgEscape(who)}\n#u${chatId}`, where who is msg.from.first_name or an email). The website form relay (support.routes.ts:133-140) has no marker at all, but its name, email and message are user-controlled. tgEscape only escapes & < >.
rawFindings.impact: An unlinked Telegram user whose first_name is '#u<otherChatId>', or a website form containing '#u<chatId>', makes the admin's reply go to an attacker-chosen chat. Replies may contain account or recovery details (more relevant under the new manual-recovery rule H). This enables misdelivery and social engineering, not code execution.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Put the routing marker first on its own line and match it anchored (/^#u(-?\d+)$/m on the first line only), or keep a server-side map adminMessageId -> chatId from the sendMessage result and route by reply_to_message.message_id. Strip '#u' sequences from user text.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Email HTML escaper does not escape quotes but is used inside href attributes
rawFindings.rootCause: esc() replaces only & < > (mailer.ts:64-66), yet renderEmail places esc(ctaHref) inside a double-quoted href (mailer.ts:83). ctaHref comes from the notification url sanitized by safeInternalPath (validation.ts:29-38), which rejects control characters and backslash but allows a double quote.
rawFindings.impact: A notification url containing a double quote (reachable via the admin broadcast url, and any future caller that passes user-influenced paths) breaks out of the attribute in outgoing email HTML, allowing injected attributes or styles and phishing-style markup in official emails. Email clients do not run JS. The input is currently admin-only.
rawFindings.evidence: mailer.ts:64-66 `s.replace(/&/g, "&").replace(/</g, "<").replace(/>/g, ">")`; mailer.ts:83 `<a href="${esc(ctaHref)}"`; validation.ts:34 rejects only code<32, 127, 92.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Escape " and ' in esc() (" and '). Additionally encodeURI the path part of absoluteUrl, or reject quotes in safeInternalPath.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Employer applications list: no server pagination, 2000 hard cap hides older applications, full resume per row (3.5 s / 2.6 MB)
rawFindings.rootCause: The endpoint returns up to 2000 newest applications so the web app can filter in the client. Each row includes every Application scalar (coverLetter up to 5000 chars), statusHistory, the jobSeeker profile and the full resume with experience, education and skills. Prisma fetches these as batched `in` queries over thousands of IDs and stitches them in memory. `vacancyId $in` plus sort by createdAt has no [vacancyId, createdAt] index. count and groupBy re-scan the same set.
rawFindings.impact: An employer with more than 2000 applications cannot see, search or act on older ones in the UI: the web sends no params and the server accepts none. Every visit to Murojaatlar costs about 3.5 s and 2.6 MB for a 5,000-application employer, and payload grows with resume size.
rawFindings.evidence: applications.routes.ts:29 EMPLOYER_LIST_LIMIT = 2000; :170-220 include resume{experience,education,skills}, statusHistory, jobSeeker; :219 take 2000; :221 count + :225 groupBy on the same where; :16 coverLetter max 5000. Web lib/employer/applications/api.ts:21 fetch without query; adapter.ts filterApplications filters in the client. FINAL_AUDIT.md benchmark: p50 3,497 ms, 2,609 KB.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add `page/pageSize<=50` (or a keyset cursor), plus `vacancyId`, `status`, `period` and `q` params on the server. The list select should carry card fields only (name, headline, region, vacancy card, status, createdAt, truncated coverLetter, resume title and top skills). Add GET /api/employer/applications/:id with an ownership check for the full resume and history. Status tab counts via one groupBy by status; take total from the groupBy sum. Add @@index([vacancyId, createdAt]) or denormalize companyId onto Application with @@index([companyId, createdAt]).
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-045 (PARTIAL: two-step query and 2000 cap done, server pagination not done); ISSUE-111; D-035
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: response shape changes, and the web Murojaatlar view (client-side search over resume, skills and cover letter) must move filters to the server.

rawFindings.title: Phone and Telegram identity uniqueness not enforced in DB or code; no index for recovery-by-phone lookup
rawFindings.rootCause: User.phone is a plain optional string with no index or unique constraint, and telegramChatId is deliberately non-unique. The Telegram contact handler writes phone and isPhoneVerified=true without checking whether another account already holds that number. The profile PATCH stores arbitrary unnormalized phone text for unverified users. Chat uniqueness relies on a non-atomic updateMany followed by update.
rawFindings.impact: Violates rules E and F: two accounts can hold the same verified primary phone, and one Telegram identity can end up on two accounts under a race. The planned forgot-password flow (phone number, then account) would be ambiguous and could target the wrong account. Phone lookups would be collection scans over users.
rawFindings.evidence: schema.prisma:163 `phone String?` (no @unique or @@index); :172-176 comment: telegramChatId intentionally not unique; indexes :201-203 only telegramChatId, role, createdAt. telegram.service.ts:339-343 update phone and isPhoneVerified with no conflict check; :268-273 updateMany then update. profile.routes.ts:15 phone z.string().max(30); :65-66 stored when not verified. There is no backup phone field.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Store the verified phone normalized to E.164 in a dedicated field (e.g. verifiedPhone, and later backupPhone). Enforce uniqueness with partial unique indexes created via $runCommandRaw createIndexes (partialFilterExpression on $type string), because Prisma cannot declare partial indexes. Do the same for telegram_chat_id. On verification, reject if the number or chat is bound elsewhere (catch E11000). Keep unverified free-text phone out of the unique field.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-012 (NOT FIXED: recovery flow absent); new auth rules E/F; overlaps the auth dimension
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: existing duplicates must be detected and resolved before the unique index builds, or db push and startup fails.

rawFindings.title: Candidate search does a $lookup per profile via relation filters, plus full resumes (about 2 s at 8k candidates)
rawFindings.rootCause: `where` combines relation filters: user{role,isBlocked}, resumes.some{published}, and for text, OR with resumes.some.title and resumes.some.skills.some.skillName. The Prisma Mongo connector runs these as $lookup pipelines over job_seeker_profiles, users, resumes and resume_skills before $sort userId, skip and take, so no index serves the filter or the sort (inference, consistent with the measured 2 s and D-033). skip reaches 9,950. Each row includes the full resume sub-collections.
rawFindings.impact: The employer candidate page takes about 2 s per page or keystroke at 8,000 candidates and grows linearly with seekers. Text search adds nested skill lookups. Deep pages cost more. Payload grows with experience descriptions (up to 30 items of 2000 chars per resume).
rawFindings.evidence: candidates.routes.ts:47-63 relation and OR filters; :66-85 skip/take, orderBy userId, include resumes{skills,experience,education}; :16-17 page<=200, pageSize<=50; :96 ownedVacancyIds fan-out. FINAL_AUDIT.md:165 p50 1,972 ms at 8,000 candidates (cause unconfirmed). Web pages/employer/candidates/+Page.tsx:406-452 renders summary, experience and education inline.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Denormalize onto JobSeekerProfile: isSearchable (open to work, published resume, user not blocked, role job_seeker), publishedResumeId, resumeUpdatedAt, lowercase skillNames[] and a normalized searchText. Maintain them in resume PUT, profile PATCH and admin block/role changes, and backfill once. Add @@index([isSearchable, regionId, resumeUpdatedAt]) and keyset pagination. Return resume title, skills and a summary snippet; load experience and education on expand (or cap them in the list).
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: No tracker ID (FINAL_AUDIT.md:165/427 benchmark observation); related ISSUE-008, ISSUE-135
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: write paths must keep the flags in sync; backfill needed; the web page expects inline resume detail.

rawFindings.title: Vacancy list sorts cannot use the compound indexes because of the id tiebreaker; count runs on every request
rawFindings.rootCause: relevance sorts by [isPremium desc, publishedAt desc, id desc] and date by [publishedAt desc, id desc]. The schema indexes are [status, isPremium, publishedAt] and [status, publishedAt], without _id. MongoDB can only skip a blocking SORT when the index covers every sort key, so each page fetches all matching active vacancies and top-k sorts them in memory (inference from MongoDB sort rules; explain not run). popular and salary sorts have no index at all. count is a separate scan each time, and the salary sort adds pricedCount.
rawFindings.impact: Every public list page and home SSR reads the entire active set, so cost grows linearly with tens of thousands of active vacancies. Measured 51-93 ms p50 at 20k locally; page up to 1000 means top-k over up to 50k docs. ISSUE-053 is marked FIXED, but the added index likely does not serve the actual sort.
rawFindings.evidence: vacancies.service.ts:276-289 DATE_ORDER and SORT_ORDERS include { id: 'desc' }; :318 pricedCount; :325 orderBy [isPremium, salaryMin, id]; :401-412 findMany + count on every call. schema.prisma:440 @@index([status, publishedAt]); :442 @@index([status, isPremium, publishedAt]); no id, viewsCount or salaryMin index. vacancies.routes.ts:45 page capped at 1000.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Put id into the indexes so the sort matches the key pattern: @@index([status, isPremium, publishedAt, id]) and @@index([status, publishedAt, id]); optionally [status, viewsCount, publishedAt, id]. Verify with explain that there is no SORT stage. Consider caching total per filter key briefly, or only computing it on page 1.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-048 (PARTIAL); ISSUE-053 (FIXED, index added without id)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: index-only change; db push builds it at startup (a large collection lengthens startup).

rawFindings.title: Filtered facets run 7 uncached aggregations per request; regex text fallback scans all active vacancies
rawFindings.rootCause: computeFacets runs 5 groupBy and 2 count, each re-applying the full filter and text regex, and only the unfiltered query is cached. The MongoDB text path uses case-insensitive `contains` on title, description (up to 20k chars) and requirements for up to 6 terms, which no index can serve. The web fetches list and facets together, so each search or filter change runs list findMany, count and 7 facet scans. The companies facet groups every company, loads them all, then slices 100.
rawFindings.impact: Without Meilisearch (optional), a text search on /vacancies runs about 9 full regex scans of the active set. List-only text search already measured 306 ms at 20k; facets with text were not benchmarked and are likely several times slower (inference). Load grows with search traffic and data size.
rawFindings.evidence: vacancies.service.ts:249-273 textFilter contains on description and requirements; :438-447 seven aggregations; :452-462 findMany over all companyIds, then :493 slice(0,100); :508-530 only unfilteredFacets cached. Web pages/vacancies/+data.ts:15 and lib/vacancies/useVacancyResults.ts:32 fetch page and facets in parallel. .env.example:105-109 Meili optional.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Compute facets in one aggregateRaw: a shared $match (status active + text), then $facet branches that each add the filters excluded for their own dimension. Include the total, and limit the companies branch to the top 100 before the name lookup. Add a keyed short-TTL cache for filtered facets and list totals (like catalogCache). For production, require Meilisearch or maintain a normalized searchText field with a text or Atlas Search index.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-048 (PARTIAL: regex and per-request count remain); ISSUE-138
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: the per-dimension exclusion semantics must stay identical (e2e facet checks exist).

rawFindings.title: Global bumpDataVersion() invalidates all heavy caches on any vacancy, company or review write
rawFindings.rootCause: One process-wide version counter gates every cache: companies catalog (200 keys), unfiltered facets, home stats and the 20k-row salary dataset. It is bumped on every vacancy PUT (including drafts), status change, delete, create, company profile or logo change, review write, admin moderation or verification, and employer registration with a company.
rawFindings.impact: With thousands of employers editing vacancies, the caches rarely stay warm, so users mostly hit the cold paths: catalog 0.75 s (2 $lookup per company), facets 0.6 s, salary dataset reload 0.57 s. The TTLs give little protection (inference; production write rate not measured).
rawFindings.evidence: cache.ts:14-17 single `version`; :24-44 keyedCache checks hit.version === version; :46-58 cached() same. Bumps at vacancies.routes.ts:219, :265, :291; vacancies.service.ts:677; companies.routes.ts:122, :140, :162, :177, :260; reviews.routes.ts create and delete; admin.routes.ts:210, :312, :382, :447, :454. FINAL_AUDIT benchmark cold catalog 754 ms, facets 602 ms, salary 573 ms.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Use per-domain versions (vacancies-public, companies, reviews) and bump only when publicly visible data changes: skip draft edits, and bump the salary dataset only for active vacancy title, salary, category, region or status. Serve stale-while-revalidate instead of blocking on recompute. Long term, denormalize Company.activeVacancyCount, ratingAvg and reviewCount with indexes so the catalog needs no $lookup.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-049 (PARTIAL); ISSUE-125 (FIXED for applications only); D-034
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium: stale data windows must stay acceptable; denormalized counters need write-path sync.

rawFindings.title: GET /api/conversations is unpaginated, repeats company description per row, and fans out over all vacancy IDs; refetched on WS reconnect
rawFindings.rootCause: findMany over all of the user's conversations has no take, and the list is sorted in JS by the last message. lastMessages groups every message of every conversation. Context lookup loads all vacancy IDs of every company in the conversations into `$in`, then queries applications. Each row carries company.description (up to 2000 chars). The client reloads the full list on every WS reconnect, and the WS closes when the access token expires.
rawFindings.impact: An employer with 500 conversations measured p50 523 ms, p95 1,148 ms, 498 KB. That payload is re-downloaded at least every token lifetime per open messages tab and grows with conversation count. A seeker chatting with large companies triggers very large `$in` arrays.
rawFindings.evidence: chat.routes.ts:358-381 findMany without take, include company{description}; :122-138 aggregateRaw $match/$sort/$group over all messages; :398-405 vacancy.findMany companyId in, select id; :406-433 applications; :500 in-memory sort; :228-230 WS closes at token exp. Web lib/messages/useMessenger.ts:175 and :221 reloadList on new conversation and reconnect. FINAL_AUDIT benchmark row conversations.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Denormalize lastMessageAt, lastMessagePreview and lastSenderId on Conversation (update in deliverMessage; backfill). Add @@index([employerUserId, lastMessageAt]) and @@index([seekerUserId, lastMessageAt]), and keyset-paginate (take 30, before cursor). Drop description from list rows (the partner panel loads it). Resolve context from application.findMany({ jobSeekerId in }) with vacancy.companyId filtered in memory, or store vacancyId on the conversation.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-046 (PARTIAL: cursor pagination not done); D-035
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: backfill needed; web list merging (bump()) and unread handling must support pages.

rawFindings.title: Employer vacancies returns full documents (up to 1000) with per-row _count; edit form downloads the whole list
rawFindings.rootCause: `include` returns every Vacancy scalar (description up to 20k, requirements and conditions up to 10k, contacts, images) plus region, category, company and `_count.applications` for each row. There is no status filter or pagination, only take 1000. The edit page has no single-record endpoint, so it fetches the list and finds one record by id.
rawFindings.impact: An employer with 500 vacancies downloads 987 KB (measured) on the dashboard and again on every edit screen. Because the product has no vacancy limit, employers above 1000 vacancies cannot reach older ones in the dashboard.
rawFindings.evidence: vacancies.routes.ts:93 EMPLOYER_VACANCIES_LIMIT = 1000; :126-136 findMany include with _count, no select. Web components/employer/vacancies/VacancyFormView.tsx:79-87 fetchEmployerVacancyRecords then records.find(id); lib/employer/vacancies/api.ts:25-29. FINAL_AUDIT benchmark: 987 KB, p50 180 ms.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: List: select card fields only, applicationCount via one application.groupBy by vacancyId, `?status&page&pageSize<=50` with @@index([companyId, status, createdAt]). Add GET /api/employer/vacancies/:id (ownership-checked) returning the full record for the edit form.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-058 (PARTIAL: edit page still loads whole list)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium: web dashboard filters and counters currently computed in the client must use server params or a counts endpoint.

rawFindings.title: API serves large JSON and XML uncompressed (no compression plugin)
rawFindings.rootCause: Fastify registers helmet, cors, rate-limit, multipart, static and websocket, but no @fastify/compress, and no compression dependency exists. The browser calls the API origin directly, so JSON goes out uncompressed unless the Railway edge compresses it (not confirmed; inference).
rawFindings.impact: The multi-hundred-KB and MB payloads (employer applications 2.6 MB, employer vacancies 987 KB, conversations 498 KB, company page 113 KB, sitemap 7.2 MB) travel at full size to mobile users, which adds latency and bandwidth on top of the query cost.
rawFindings.evidence: server.ts:60-80 Fastify options; grep for 'compress' finds nothing in apps/api/src/server.ts or apps/api/package.json (dependencies list has no compression package). FINAL_AUDIT.md benchmark 'hajm' column.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Register @fastify/compress (brotli and gzip, threshold about 1 KB, skip WS upgrades and already-compressed uploads), or confirm and document that the Railway edge compresses API responses. Treat this as a complement to pagination, not a replacement.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: CPU cost per response; check streaming and static upload routes are excluded.

rawFindings.title: Conversation history capped at latest 1000 messages with no cursor; older messages unreachable
rawFindings.rootCause: GET /api/conversations/:id/messages always returns the newest 1000 messages in one response, with no before/after cursor. The client reloads the whole thread on open and on WS reconnect.
rawFindings.impact: Long conversations lose access to messages older than the newest 1000. Each open or reconnect re-downloads up to 1000 bodies (each up to 4000 chars; 252 KB measured for a 5,000-message thread).
rawFindings.evidence: chat.routes.ts:158 MESSAGES_LIMIT = 1000; :523-528 findMany orderBy createdAt desc take 1000, no cursor params; :512-515 updateMany marks read on every load. Web useMessenger.ts:222 loadThread on reconnect. FINAL_AUDIT benchmark 252 KB.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add keyset params `before=<createdAt,id>` and `limit<=50` on the existing [conversationId, createdAt] index. The client loads more on scroll, and reconnect fetches only messages after the last known id.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium: the thread view and read-marker logic need infinite-scroll support.

rawFindings.title: Notifications: no cursor beyond newest 100 and no retention; collection grows with every broadcast
rawFindings.rootCause: The list query accepts only unreadOnly and limit (at most 100), with no before or offset parameter. notify() inserts one document per in-app notification, and a broadcast inserts one per user. No deleteMany, TTL index or cleanup job exists.
rawFindings.impact: Users cannot see notifications older than the newest 100. The notifications collection grows without bound (hundreds of thousands of documents), increasing storage, index size and backup cost. Queries stay indexed.
rawFindings.evidence: notifications.routes.ts:20-23 listQuerySchema {unreadOnly, limit max 100}; :58-63 take limit ?? 30. notifications.service.ts:100-108 notification.create per notify. admin.routes.ts:563-581 broadcast loop. Web lib/notifications/api.ts:5 NOTIFICATIONS_LIMIT = 100. The only notification deleteMany is in prisma/demo-seed.ts:1582.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add a keyset `before` param on [userId, createdAt]. Add retention: a TTL index on created_at for read notifications (via $runCommandRaw createIndexes with partialFilterExpression {is_read: true}) or a daily cleanup job (e.g. read and older than 90 days).
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: retention policy is a product decision.

rawFindings.title: Unbounded vacancy-ID fan-out in polled inbox summary and other employer paths
rawFindings.rootCause: ownedVacancyIds() returns every vacancy ID of the employer (drafts and archived included, no limit), and callers pass it as `vacancyId $in`. /api/inbox/summary also loads all conversation IDs for `conversationId $in`. The web polls the summary every 20 s per tab and again on every incoming message and on window focus.
rawFindings.impact: Steady background load of about 5 queries per poll per logged-in tab, with `$in` arrays sized to the employer's full vacancy and conversation history. Measured employer summary p50 125 ms, cold 735 ms. Cost grows with employer size (no vacancy limit).
rawFindings.evidence: ownership.ts:15-20 findMany companyId in, select id, no take; chat.routes.ts:673-695 conversations findMany (all ids) + message.count + ownedVacancyIds + application.count; also candidates.routes.ts:96, chat.routes.ts:327, applications.routes.ts:167. Web lib/useInboxSummary.ts:45-49 setInterval 20000 plus INBOX_CHANGED and focus; useMessenger.ts emitInboxChanged per received message.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Denormalize companyId on Application with @@index([companyId, status]) so new applications become one indexed count. Store receiverId on Message with @@index([receiverId, isRead]), or keep an unread counter per user, to avoid the conversation fan-out. Push badge updates over the WS and poll only when the socket is down.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: backfill of the new denormalized fields.
