rawFindings.title: Duplicate or unused count queries (applications, company page, salary sort, alerts sweep)
rawFindings.rootCause: Totals are computed separately from data that already contains them. The employer list runs count plus groupBy over the same filter. The company page runs _count.reviews plus companyReview.aggregate _count. The salary sort runs pricedCount plus a total count. The alerts sweep calls listVacancies, which always runs vacancy.count, even though only items are used.
rawFindings.impact: Extra collection or index scans on hot paths. The alerts sweep executes one unnecessary count per subscription per interval.
rawFindings.evidence: applications.routes.ts:221 count({where}) and :225 groupBy({where}); companies.routes.ts:211-216 _count.reviews and :221-225 aggregate _count; vacancies.service.ts:318 pricedCount and :411 count; alerts.service.ts:195 listVacancies(query) uses only items; vacancies.service.ts:401-412 always counts.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Take total from the groupBy sum. Drop _count.reviews (use summary.count). Add a `withTotal: false` option to listVacancies for alerts. Reuse pricedCount plus an unpriced count, or cache the total per filter.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-055 (FIXED, but the per-subscription count remains); ISSUE-048
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Sitemaps uncached single files (7.2 MB vacancy sitemap); employer sitemap uses relation-filter lookups
rawFindings.rootCause: Every crawl request reads up to 50,000 vacancies and builds XML with 4 alternates per URL in memory, with no cache or Cache-Control and no chunking. The employer sitemap filters with owner.isBlocked and vacancies.some, which run $lookup for every company.
rawFindings.impact: Each crawler hit costs about 240 ms of DB and CPU plus a 7.2 MB response at 20k vacancies, growing toward the 50k-URL cap. Repeated bot hits add avoidable load.
rawFindings.evidence: seo.routes.ts:99-104 findMany status active take 50000; :114-125 company.findMany with NOT owner.isBlocked and OR vacancies.some; :150-164 buildUrlSet string; no reply.header Cache-Control. FINAL_AUDIT benchmark: sitemap-vacancy 7,189 KB, 240 ms.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Cache generated XML in memory for about 1 h and set Cache-Control public, max-age 3600. Split into 5k-10k URL chunks under the sitemap index (keyset on publishedAt/_id). For employers, precompute company IDs from vacancy distinct companyId (indexed) and blocked owner IDs instead of relation filters.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-056 (PARTIAL: origin cache and chunking not done)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Admin list search uses relation filters over whole collections; vacancy admin sort unindexed; deep skip allowed
rawFindings.rootCause: Admin vacancies text search puts company.name inside an OR, and admin users search puts jobSeekerProfile.firstName and lastName inside an OR. These relation filters run $lookup over every vacancy or user. Admin vacancies sort by createdAt, but Vacancy has no createdAt index. pageSchema allows page up to 10,000 with pageSize up to 100 (skip up to about 1M). Overview loads all 14-day application timestamps into Node to count per day.
rawFindings.impact: Admin searches and unfiltered vacancy pages scan full collections (tens of thousands of vacancies, 10k users) with lookups, which is slow for moderators. Deep pages are expensive. Admin-only, so user impact is limited.
rawFindings.evidence: admin.routes.ts:27-31 page max 10_000, pageSize max 100; :142-151 OR with jobSeekerProfile relation; :239-244 OR with company{name}; :249 orderBy createdAt; schema.prisma:440-447 has no Vacancy createdAt index; admin.routes.ts:107-113 findMany createdAt>=since select createdAt.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Pre-resolve company IDs by name and user IDs by profile name (as in D-033), then filter on indexed IDs. Add @@index([createdAt]) and [status, createdAt] on Vacancy. Cap page at about 200 or use a keyset cursor. Compute the overview chart with an aggregateRaw $group by Tashkent day.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-053 (Vacancy createdAt index not added, listed as I7 in DB_MAP); D-033
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Public vacancy cards ship full requirements text; company page returns 200 reviews and 100 cards
rawFindings.rootCause: VACANCY_CARD_SELECT includes requirements (up to 10,000 chars) only so the web can extract skill chips from it on the client. The company detail page embeds 200 reviews (with reviewer userId) and 100 cards in one response.
rawFindings.impact: List, similar, home and company page payloads scale with employer-written requirements text. Up to about 500 KB for a 50-card page and about 1 MB for the company page in the worst case; 113 KB measured with synthetic data.
rawFindings.evidence: vacancies.service.ts:70-99 VACANCY_CARD_SELECT with requirements: true (:75). Web lib/api.ts:244 extractSkills(title + requirements). vacancies.routes.ts:57 requirements max 10_000. companies.routes.ts:27-28 limits 200 and 100; :191-210 reviews select userId; FINAL_AUDIT company page 113 KB.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Denormalize a `skills: String[]` (at most 12) at vacancy write time and drop requirements from the card select, or truncate it in an aggregate projection. Page company reviews (take 20 with cursor) and vacancies (take 20; the full list already exists via /api/vacancies?company=).
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: card skill extraction moves to the server; backfill for existing vacancies.

rawFindings.title: Salary statistics silently truncated to newest 20,000 active vacancies and reloaded in full after each cache bump
rawFindings.rootCause: loadDataset reads up to MAX_ROWS=20,000 active vacancies with category and region into memory and computes medians in JS. There is no truncation flag, and the whole dataset reloads whenever the global data version changes.
rawFindings.impact: At tens of thousands of active vacancies, the public salary medians, distribution and market counts silently cover only a subset. Each reload costs about 0.57 s and holds 20k objects in the API process.
rawFindings.evidence: salary.stats.ts:76 MAX_ROWS = 20_000; :166-197 cached(5 min) findMany status active, include category/region select, take MAX_ROWS; :199-262 in-memory filtering; no `truncated` field in response. FINAL_AUDIT benchmark cold 573 ms.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Compute with aggregateRaw: $match active, UZS, salary not hidden, then $group per category, region and experience ($percentile on MongoDB 7+, or bucketed histograms). Alternatively project only numeric fields, remove the cap and expose `truncated` when capped. Combine with per-domain cache versions.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium: results must match the existing role/regex matching done in JS.

rawFindings.title: Candidate-owned lists unbounded: applications without take, favorites without per-user cap
rawFindings.rootCause: GET /api/applications returns all of a candidate's applications with statusHistory and no take. Favorites have no per-user cap, and /api/favorites/ids returns every favorited ID, fetched on list and search pages. /api/favorites filters on the vacancy.status relation, which runs a lookup per favorite (capped at 500).
rawFindings.impact: Low today (5 KB measured). A heavy user or script can grow these lists without bound, and every vacancy list page then downloads the full favorite ID list.
rawFindings.evidence: applications.routes.ts:129-155 findMany where jobSeekerId, no take; favorites.routes.ts:71-76 favorites/ids no take; :92-96 upsert with no count check; :25-31 relation filter vacancy.status with take 500.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add take (at most 200) with a cursor on /api/applications. Cap favorites per user (e.g. 1000) and return favorite membership only for the IDs on the current page (`?ids=`) instead of the full list.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: API outage during SSR returns HTTP 200: detail pages add noindex (deindex risk), list pages stay indexable with error content
rawFindings.rootCause: The +data loaders catch ApiError and return data with vacancy/company/article/page/stats set to null instead of throwing a Vike 5xx abort. api/ssr.js and server/index.mjs forward httpResponse.statusCode, which is 200. Detail heads switch to noindex on the error state; list heads always emit a canonical URL without noindex.
rawFindings.impact: If a crawler fetches a page while the API is down or slower than the 8 s SSR timeout, live vacancy, company and article URLs are served as 200 + noindex and can drop out of the index (standard crawler behaviour; inference). /vacancies, /companies and /salaries serve 200 with an error block under a canonical URL, which looks like a soft 404. Users do get a retry UI. SSR 5xx metrics never show API outages.
rawFindings.evidence: vacancies/@slug/+data.ts:14-24 turns ApiError into {vacancy:null, failed:true} with no abort; vacancies/@slug/+Head.tsx:33-36 adds noindex. Same in companies/@slug/+data.ts:14-24 + +Head.tsx:24 and articles/@slug/+data.ts:18-20 + +Head.tsx:28. Lists: vacancies/+data.ts:16 null page + vacancies/+Head.tsx:31 canonical; salaries/+data.ts:19 + +Head.tsx:9-13; companies/+data.ts:20 + +Head.tsx:8. server/index.mjs:116 and api/ssr.js copy statusCode. _error/+Page.tsx:39-44 handles only 404/500.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: When primary data fails with an ApiError during SSR (not client navigation), throw render(503) so the response is a 503 (optionally with Retry-After). Add a 503 'temporarily unavailable, retry' state to _error/+Page.tsx. Keep the null path for client-side navigation. Never emit noindex for a transient failure.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low to medium. Outage pages change HTTP status; confirm Vercel and self-hosted do not cache 5xx and that in-page retry still works on client navigation.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: None directly. ISSUE-016 (FIXED) covered only the in-page empty-vs-error state; ISSUE-069 (PARTIAL) covers SSR timeouts.

rawFindings.title: ISSUE-069 still partial: salary stats, articles and contact SSR fetchers have no timeout
rawFindings.rootCause: withServerTimeout is applied only inside lib/api.ts. fetchSalaryStats, the articles request() helper and the support request() helper call fetch with only the caller's signal, and their +data loaders pass no signal.
rawFindings.impact: When the API hangs (DB stall, cold start), SSR for /salaries, /articles, /articles/:slug and /contact hangs until the platform kills the request (Vercel function timeout, 504 or blank page). The designed 'could not load, retry' state never renders, and self-hosted SSR capacity is tied up.
rawFindings.evidence: api.ts:64-70 defines withServerTimeout (8 s); it is used only at api.ts:75,339,359,376,390,436,483,499. apiExtra.ts:352 fetch(`/api/stats/salary`, {signal}) is called from salaries/+data.ts:19. articles/api.ts:12 fetch(path, init) is called from articles/index/+data.ts:16 and articles/@slug/+data.ts:17. support/api.ts:13 is called from contact/+data.ts:9. The ISSUE-069 fix note says 'lib/articles/api.ts qamrab olinmadi'.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Pass withServerTimeout(signal) in apiExtra.fetchSalaryStats, articles/api.ts request() and support/api.ts request(). Their catch blocks already turn a TimeoutError (anything that is not an AbortError) into ApiError(0), so the loaders' null path works unchanged.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-069 (PARTIAL): api.ts is covered; apiExtra salary stats, articles and support fetchers are not.

rawFindings.title: Bot-offline state is never shown proactively: status exposes botUsername=null but the UI ignores it; users see a raw Uzbek 503 only after clicking, and phone gates still demand Telegram verification
rawFindings.rootCause: GET /api/telegram/status returns botUsername, which stays null until getMe succeeds, but no web code reads it. TelegramConnect always renders the Connect button and shows err.message from the 503 BOT_OFFLINE response. requirePhoneVerified returns 403 PHONE_NOT_VERIFIED telling users to verify via Telegram whether or not the bot is running.
rawFindings.impact: Violates Rule K. While the bot is down, the profile shows a Connect button that looks functional. After a click, ru/en users see an Uzbek server string. Apply, create vacancy and start conversation keep returning 'verify your phone via Telegram' with no 'temporarily unavailable' notice, so new users are blocked by an instruction they cannot follow. Nothing crashes (that part complies).
rawFindings.evidence: telegram.routes.ts:11-22 returns botUsername: getBotUsername(); :25-32 returns 503 BOT_OFFLINE. telegram.service.ts:443-452 sets botUsername only after getMe. The only web reference to botUsername is lib/types.ts:378. TelegramConnect.tsx:80-86 does setError(err instanceof ApiError ? err.message : ...). auth-guard.ts:97-102 has the PHONE_NOT_VERIFIED text.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add an explicit available flag to the status response. In TelegramConnect, disable the button and show a translated 'Telegram verification is temporarily unavailable' notice. Map the BOT_OFFLINE code to i18n text instead of err.message. Have the phone-gate notice check availability, or return a distinct TELEGRAM_UNAVAILABLE code while the bot is down.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: an additive response field plus UI changes.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-073 (NOT FIXED) covers raw Uzbek server text in ru/en.

rawFindings.title: Header bell mark-read, mark-all-read and delete swallow API failures after the optimistic update
rawFindings.rootCause: useNotifications updates items and count first, then awaits the request with .catch(() => undefined): no rollback and no failure signal. useNotificationCenter (the /notifications page) does roll back and returns false, so the two paths behave differently.
rawFindings.impact: 'Mark all read' in the bell zeroes the badge and shows 'all read' even when the POST failed (5xx, network, or 401 after a failed refresh). The next 45 s poll or window focus brings the unread items back, so the badge jumps back without explanation. The same fake success applies to markRead when a notification is opened.
rawFindings.evidence: useNotifications.ts:171-177 sets state, then `await markNotificationRead(token, id).catch(() => undefined)`; :181-186 markAllRead and :188-197 remove follow the same pattern. NotificationBell.tsx:61 calls markAllRead and :96 calls markRead. The poll is every 45 s (:68). Contrast useNotificationCenter.ts:76-85, 100-104, 122-130, which roll back and return false.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Reuse the center's rollback pattern (restore the previous items and count in the catch, then call refresh()). Optionally show a small inline error in the bell dropdown.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-067 (FIXED) covered poll errors and the badge dropping to 0, not mutation rollback.

rawFindings.title: Mutation fetchers don't normalize network or non-JSON failures; forms show raw browser text or an Uzbek fallback in every locale
rawFindings.rootCause: apiExtra send() and many api.ts mutations call fetch with no try/catch, so a lost connection throws a raw TypeError. A non-JSON error body falls back to the hard-coded 'Xatolik' or 'Kutilmagan xatolik'. Components render err.message as-is.
rawFindings.impact: When the connection drops or a proxy returns a 502/504 HTML page, company profile save, logo upload/remove, saved-search creation and the rating dialog show 'Failed to fetch' or 'NetworkError when attempting to fetch resource.', or Uzbek text in the ru/en UI, instead of a translated retry message.
rawFindings.evidence: apiExtra.ts:69-89 send has no try around fetch. api.ts saveMyCompany 754-764, uploadCompanyLogo 728-740, deleteCompanyLogo 742-752, createVacancy 817-827, submitConversationRating 972-986 are the same. EmployerCompanyForm.tsx:48,61,95 do `setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : ...)`; SaveSearchButton.tsx:67 does the same; RatingDialog.tsx:58 uses err.message. The normalizing code already exists but isn't shared: admin/http.ts:31-33 and apiExtra getStrict :59-61 map failures to ApiError(0,'NETWORK').
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Use one shared request helper (modelled on adminRequest) that wraps network errors as ApiError(0,'NETWORK') and non-JSON responses as ApiError(status,'BAD_RESPONSE'). In components, map error codes to i18n strings instead of rendering err.message; keep specific codes such as PHONE_NOT_VERIFIED and VACANCY_HAS_APPLICATIONS.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low to medium: many call sites; keep the existing error codes stable.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-073 (NOT FIXED) covers raw server text; ISSUE-102 (FIXED) made these helpers keep server messages.

rawFindings.title: Chat WebSocket drops rejected or failed sends silently (no error frame); the client shows a generic 'failed' after 10 s
rawFindings.rootCause: handle() returns without replying on rate limit, unknown conversation or non-participant, and DB errors are only logged via handle(raw).catch. The protocol has no nack or error message carrying the clientId, so the sender can only wait for its timeout.
rawFindings.impact: Rate-limited, forbidden or DB-failed messages stay 'pending' for 10 s, then turn 'failed' with a generic retry; retrying repeats the same silent failure, and users can't tell whether to wait, reload or give up. A second observation (inference): the WS path checks only isBlocked and tokenVersion, not isPhoneVerified, while the REST conversation start requires phone verification.
rawFindings.evidence: chat.routes.ts:257 `if (!allow()) return;`, :260 `if (!parts) return;`, :261 non-participant return; :283 `handle(raw).catch(err => req.log.warn(...))`. :203-224 the ready check reads only isBlocked/tokenVersion; :294 the REST start route uses requirePhoneVerified. useMessenger.ts:10 SEND_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000; :226-243 dispatch marks the bubble failed on timeout.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: On each early return and in the catch, send the sender {type:'error', clientId, code:'RATE_LIMITED'|'FORBIDDEN'|'SERVER_ERROR'}. On the client, map the code to i18n and don't offer retry for FORBIDDEN. If messaging is meant to be phone-gated, add isPhoneVerified to the ready query.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: the message type is additive; confirm useChatSocket ignores unknown types.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-003 (FIXED): its fix covered the crash; its impact text already noted the missing phone check on WS sends.

rawFindings.title: Lenient fetchers still in use show wrong UI on failure: saved-company hearts, push 'not configured', missing Rate action
rawFindings.rootCause: fetchSavedCompanyIds, fetchPushPublicKey and fetchConversationRating use get()/tryFetch fallbacks ({ids:[]}, {key:''}, null). The UI cannot tell these apart from 'nothing saved', 'push not configured on the server' and 'cannot rate'.
rawFindings.impact: 1) Any 401, 5xx or network error shows every company as not saved; vacancy favorites got a ready flag but saved companies did not. 2) usePush reports 'unconfigured' after a network blip, which hides the enable-push control. 3) A rating load error is stored as null and never reloaded, so the Rate action and rating summary disappear for that conversation until reload.
rawFindings.evidence: apiExtra.ts:45-49 get() returns the fallback when !res.ok; :156-159 fetchSavedCompanyIds; :237-240 fetchPushPublicKey. api.ts:949-958 fetchConversationRating: `if (!res || !res.ok) return null`. useSavedCompanies.ts:21-25. usePush.ts:52-56 and 79-83 treat an empty key as unconfigured. useMessenger.ts:288-293 stores null; :339 `if (!(activeId in ratingsRef.current))` blocks reload. ConversationHeader.tsx:39 needs rating to show Rate.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Switch these to throwing (getStrict-style) fetchers. Add a ready/error flag to useSavedCompanies, as useFavorites.ts does. Give usePush an 'error' state distinct from 'unconfigured'. On rating error, delete the ratings entry (or store 'error') so it reloads.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-022 (FIXED) covered vacancy favorite IDs only; ISSUE-068 (FIXED) stopped the rating getting stuck in loading, but an error still becomes null.

rawFindings.title: SSR loaders turn catalog and featured-list failures into [], which the page treats as loaded, so no client retry happens
rawFindings.rootCause: fetchCategories, fetchRegions and fetchFeaturedCompanies return [] on network or 5xx errors. The pages retry only when the loader value is null, and [] is not null.
rawFindings.impact: After one transient API error during SSR, /salaries keeps empty categories and regions for the whole visit, so the selected profession's category label cannot be resolved. /companies hides the 'Top companies' block until a full reload. No data loss, but the empty UI is misleading.
rawFindings.evidence: salaries/+data.ts:20-21 call fetchCategories() and fetchRegions() (api.ts:790-794, 550-555 return [] when !res.ok). useSalaryStats.ts:61-62 refetches only `if (!initialCategories)`. SelectedProfession.tsx:52 does categories.find(...). companies/+data.ts:21 calls fetchFeaturedCompanies() (api.ts:457-459 catch returns []); companies/+Page.tsx:68 refetches only `if (featured === null)`.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: In the loaders, call strict variants and add .catch(() => null) so the existing client null path retries. fetchRegionsStrict already exists at api.ts:558; add fetchCategoriesStrict and a throwing featured-companies call.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-016 (FIXED) established the null-means-failed pattern for the home page only.

rawFindings.title: Global error handler: Fastify's default 404 body, infrastructure errors all become 500, internal FST_* codes and English text pass through as 4xx
rawFindings.rootCause: setErrorHandler maps only AppError, Zod and Prisma P2002/P2025/P2023. Any other error with a 4xx statusCode is forwarded with its raw error.code and message; everything else becomes 500. No setNotFoundHandler is registered.
rawFindings.impact: Unknown routes, including billing endpoints when billing is disabled, return {message:'Route GET:/api/plans not found', error:'Not Found', statusCode:404}, so clients that read `error` as a code get 'Not Found'. A DB outage (PrismaClientInitializationError, P2024 pool timeout) or a Mongo write conflict (P2034) returns 500 INTERNAL_ERROR instead of 503/409, with no retry hint, and outages look like bugs. 413 FST_REQ_FILE_TOO_LARGE shows English text in ResumeFile.tsx:40.
rawFindings.evidence: server.ts:178-216 is the handler. :196-204 map only P2002, P2025 and P2023. :211-212 do `statusCode >= 400 && < 500` → send({error: error.code ?? 'ERROR', message: error.message}). :214-215 return 500. A grep for setNotFoundHandler in apps/api/src finds nothing. Billing routes are registered only when features.billing is on. session.ts:126 already treats >=500 as transient (correct).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add setNotFoundHandler returning {error:'NOT_FOUND', message}. Map P2024, P1001 and PrismaClientInitializationError to 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE and P2034 to 409 with a retryable code. Translate known Fastify 4xx codes to stable codes (PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, BAD_REQUEST) with messages the client can localize.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: the body shape change is additive; check e2e-check.mjs assertions on 404/500 bodies.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-073 (NOT FIXED) covers message language; nothing covers the 404 shape or 5xx classification.

rawFindings.title: POST /api/push/unsubscribe reports success when the database delete fails
rawFindings.rootCause: The route calls deleteMany(...).catch(() => undefined) and then returns {ok:true}. The client also swallows the error and sets its state to 'off'.
rawFindings.impact: If the DB write fails, the user sees push disabled while the subscription row stays in the database, so the server keeps sending web push to that endpoint. Pushes to an unsubscribed endpoint probably fail with 410; whether the server cleans those up (common/push.ts) was not verified.
rawFindings.evidence: notifications.routes.ts:208-213: `.deleteMany({ where: { endpoint, userId } }).catch(() => undefined); return { ok: true };`. usePush.ts:116-119: `await unsubscribePush(...).catch(() => undefined); await sub.unsubscribe().catch(() => undefined); setState('off')`.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Let the DB error reach the global handler (500). In usePush, show an error and keep the 'on' state when the server call fails, or retry the server unsubscribe on the next load.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Telegram bot sends no reply when a /start, contact or callback handler throws
rawFindings.rootCause: The polling loop catches handleUpdate exceptions and only logs them; the handlers have no try/catch that sends a generic reply. tg() returns null on any Telegram API or network failure, and bot callers never check that result.
rawFindings.impact: A DB error while linking an account (handleStart) or verifying a phone (handleContact) leaves the user with no answer, so they can't tell whether verification worked while the site keeps showing 'not verified'. The loop keeps running, so there is no crash. Invalid payloads do get a safe generic reply.
rawFindings.evidence: telegram.service.ts:454-458: `try { await handleUpdate(u) } catch (e) { logger.warn(...) }`. handleStart :268-272 does Prisma writes before replying; handleContact :340-343 prisma.user.update before replying; the invalid-payload branch :262-266 replies 'Havola eskirgan'. tg() returns null at :66 and :71. Among all callers, only support.routes.ts:141 checks the send result.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Wrap each handler body in a try/catch that sends a generic 'Something went wrong, please try again from the site' message with no internals, and log only the update type and error.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Strict list fetchers still turn an unparseable or wrong-shape 200 response into an empty list
rawFindings.rootCause: These fetchers throw only when !res.ok. A 2xx response with a non-JSON body (proxy or captive-portal HTML) or no items array becomes [].
rawFindings.impact: Unlikely, but when it happens the UI says there are no conversations, favorites, notifications, companies or applications instead of showing an error with retry. fetchCandidates already treats this case as an error.
rawFindings.evidence: messages/api.ts:17-25: null json gives rows []. Same pattern in favorites/api.ts:17-20 and notifications/api.ts:26-31. api.ts:443-449 fetchCompanyPage: null json gives items []. api.ts:653-654 fetchMyApplications: non-array gives []. apiExtra.ts:132-135 fetchFavoriteIdsStrict. Contrast api.ts:876-878, where fetchCandidates throws 'Kutilmagan javob'.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Throw ApiError(res.status, 'BAD_RESPONSE') when the JSON is null or items is not an array, as fetchCandidates does.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Unused 'empty on error' fetchers and module comments that describe that policy are still exported
rawFindings.rootCause: Earlier fixes added strict variants but left the fallback versions in place, and the file header comments still say 'server down → empty result' is the module policy.
rawFindings.impact: No current UI impact (these functions have zero call sites). Any new code importing them silently brings back the empty-vs-error bugs fixed in ISSUE-021, ISSUE-022 and ISSUE-067. refreshAccessToken returns null (guest) on a 5xx, which contradicts the tri-state refresh in session.ts:118-132.
rawFindings.evidence: Header comments api.ts:1-2 and apiExtra.ts:4-5; authGet at api.ts:784-788. Zero references (grep) to fetchVacancies :320, fetchCompanies :405, fetchMe :173, refreshAccessToken :161, fetchEmployerVacancies :796, fetchEmployerApplications :882, fetchInboxSummary :901, fetchConversations :936, fetchMessages :940; apiExtra fetchFavorites :118, fetchFavoriteIds :127, fetchNotifications :175, fetchUnreadCount :192, fetchSavedSearches :257. fetchPlans/fetchSubscription/fetchMyPayments are used only by /pricing, which pricing/+guard.ts:10-12 always redirects.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Delete the unused lenient exports, or rename them *OrFallback with explicit JSDoc. Update the header comments to describe the strict policy, and add a lint rule or grep check that bans tryFetch/authGet/get fallbacks in new code.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: the typecheck confirms nothing uses them.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-021, ISSUE-022, ISSUE-067 (FIXED): these are leftovers from those fixes.

rawFindings.title: Revoking sessions does not close live sockets; each caller must remember to call closeUserSockets
rawFindings.rootCause: The WS checks tokenVersion only once, at connect (chat.routes.ts:204-224). handle() never checks it again. revokeUserSessions only increments tokenVersion. Open sockets are closed only if the caller also calls closeUserSockets. Today all 4 callers do this by hand. Rule J/G/H flows (password reset, phone change, manual recovery) do not exist yet (no reset/recovery code found), so each new flow has to remember this pairing.
rawFindings.impact: If a future password-reset or phone-change flow calls only revokeUserSessions, an attacker's open socket keeps receiving private messages and notifications and can send messages until the access token expires (up to 15 min, chat.routes.ts:227-231). That breaks rule J (invalidate all active sessions).
rawFindings.evidence: auth.service.ts:166-173 (update tokenVersion only); callers that pair it by hand: auth.routes.ts:117-119, admin.routes.ts:200-201 and 223-224, team.routes.ts:211-213; chat.routes.ts:244-278 has no tokenVersion recheck; no grep hits for reset/recovery/forgot in apps/api/src.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Make closeUserSockets(userId, 4401, 'session revoked') part of revokeUserSessions, or add a single invalidateAllSessions() helper, and use it in every current and future flow. Optionally re-check tokenVersion before handling a 'message' frame (cache it for a few seconds). Add an e2e test: revoke, then the WS closes and a sent frame is rejected.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-035 / ISSUE-041 (FIXED for logout/block/role; the pairing is still by hand)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low. Clients already handle 4401 by refreshing and falling back to guest.

rawFindings.title: WS message frames skip the phone-verification requirement that REST enforces for messaging
rawFindings.rootCause: requirePhoneVerified lists messaging ('xabar') as a key action and is applied on POST /api/conversations/start. The WS connect check selects only isBlocked and tokenVersion, and the 'message' path checks only that the user is a participant. Resume publishing is not phone-gated, so an unverified seeker can be discoverable and receive a conversation started by an employer.
rawFindings.impact: A user with an unverified phone can send messages over WS in any existing conversation (for example, replying after an employer starts the chat). This defeats the anti-spam purpose of Telegram phone verification (rule E). If a phone change later resets verification, sending stays open.
rawFindings.evidence: auth-guard.ts:86-89 (doc: 'Kalit amallar (ariza, vakansiya, xabar)'); chat.routes.ts:204-205 select {isBlocked, tokenVersion}; 274-278 no isPhoneVerified check; 294 REST start uses requirePhoneVerified; requirePhoneVerified appears only in applications, conversations/start, reviews and vacancies routes (no resume route).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Load isPhoneVerified in the connect check and reject 'message' frames when it is false, returning an error frame (e.g. {type:'error',code:'PHONE_NOT_VERIFIED'}) so the UI can prompt verification. Or record an explicit product decision that replying is allowed.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-003 (its impact text already noted WS lacked requirePhoneVerified and isBlocked; only isBlocked was fixed)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low. Needs a UI state for the rejected send.

rawFindings.title: WS rate limit is per connection with no per-user socket cap; each offline-recipient message sends one Telegram alert
rawFindings.rootCause: The token bucket is created per socket. addSocket has no limit on sockets per user. The only connection limit is the global per-IP HTTP limit (RATE_LIMIT_MAX default 600/min). deliverMessage sends a Telegram message for every chat message when the receiver has no socket, with no aggregation or cooldown. A phone-verified seeker can open a conversation with any company by slug.
rawFindings.impact: One verified account can open dozens of sockets (about 2 msg/s each), flooding a target employer's chat and Telegram and growing the messages collection. Many parallel Telegram sends can hit Telegram's global rate limits, which delays other users' alerts.
rawFindings.evidence: chat.routes.ts:160-162, 233-242 (bucket per connection); realtime.ts:17-26 (no cap); env.ts:56 RATE_LIMIT_MAX default 600; chat.routes.ts:84-89 (a Telegram alert for every message); 342-347 (seeker can start a chat with any company slug).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Key the bucket by userId (shared Map), cap sockets per user (e.g. 5, closing the oldest), and debounce Telegram chat alerts per (receiver, conversation), e.g. at most one per 5-10 min with an 'N new messages' summary.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-040 (FIXED per-connection bucket; per-user and Telegram throttling not covered)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Chat-message Telegram alerts skip notification preferences and are the only out-of-site channel for chat
rawFindings.rootCause: deliverMessage calls notifyUserViaTelegram directly instead of notify(). NotificationType has no message type, so preferences cannot control it. Push, email and in-app are never used for chat. 'Offline' means no socket at all, so any open tab (for example the bell socket in a background tab) suppresses the alert. The text is fixed Uzbek and includes the first 200 characters of the message.
rawFindings.impact: Users cannot turn off chat Telegram alerts except by unlinking Telegram. Under rules B/F Telegram is also the recovery channel, so users are pushed to unlink it. Users without Telegram, or with a tab left open anywhere, get no alert for new messages. RU/EN users get Uzbek text.
rawFindings.evidence: chat.routes.ts:84-89; schema.prisma:119-124 enum NotificationType {new_application, application_status_changed, new_vacancy_match, system}; notifications.routes.ts:11-16; realtime.ts:45-47 isOnline = sockets.has(userId).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add a 'new_message' NotificationType and send through notify() with channels telegram/push (not in_app, since chat has its own badge), with a per-conversation debounce. Expose it in preferences. Base 'online' on chat activity or a visible tab rather than any socket. Localize the text.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-060 (FIXED routing of status reasons through deliverMessage); ISSUE-073
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium. Needs a Prisma enum addition (additive) and a preferences UI row.

rawFindings.title: notify() runs Telegram and email channels even when not configured; email addresses are logged for every notification
rawFindings.rootCause: use(channel) checks only wanted channels and user preferences, not features.telegram or features.email. With SMTP_HOST empty, sendUserEmail still looks up the user and sendMail logs the recipient address and subject with console.log. With TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN empty, notifyUserViaTelegram still looks up the user and tg() calls api.telegram.org/bot/sendMessage with an empty token for linked users.
rawFindings.impact: In production without SMTP (likely, since email is not a product channel), every notification writes a user's email address to stdout. A 10k broadcast writes about 10k addresses into the logs. Each notification also costs extra DB lookups and failed HTTP calls plus warning noise. Rule K asks for clean unavailability.
rawFindings.evidence: notifications.service.ts:90 use(), 131-155 (no features checks), 170-175 user lookup; mailer.ts:36-39 console.log(`[mail:o'chiq] ${input.to} — ${input.subject}`); telegram.service.ts:197-204 and 31-37 (no token check); env.ts:186-189 features; .env.example:92 SMTP_HOST="".
rawFindings.recommendedFix: In deliver(): const available = {email: features.email, telegram: features.telegram, push: features.push, in_app: true}; skip unavailable channels before any DB work. Remove the recipient address from the disabled-mail log (log the count only). Return early in tg() when there is no token.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Read receipts are sent from hidden or background tabs
rawFindings.rootCause: Incoming messages for the selected conversation are marked read immediately (socket.markRead) whether or not the document is visible or focused. A reconnect in a hidden tab calls loadThread, and its REST GET also marks messages read on the server. No visibility or focus check exists anywhere in the chat or notification client code.
rawFindings.impact: The sender sees double ticks and the receiver's unread badge clears while the /messages tab sits minimized or in the background. Because that socket keeps isOnline true, no Telegram alert is sent either, so the message can go unnoticed while appearing read.
rawFindings.evidence: useMessenger.ts:159 isActive = selected conversation; 194-197 markRead plus emitInboxChanged; 218-223 reconnect reload; chat.routes.ts:512-520 GET messages marks read; grep for visibilityState|document.hidden|hasFocus|visibilitychange in lib, components/messages, Header and pages/messages returns nothing.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Mark read only when document.visibilityState==='visible' and the window has focus. Otherwise count the message as unread and send markRead on 'visibilitychange' or 'focus'. Consider a ?markRead=false option on the history GET for silent reloads.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Reconnect backoff has no jitter; after a deploy every client reconnects and reloads at the same moment
rawFindings.rootCause: Delay is a fixed min(30s, 1000*2^attempt) in both hooks. On SIGTERM, app.close() runs @fastify/websocket's defaultPreClose, which closes all clients at once. Each client reconnects on the same 1/2/4 s schedule. Each connect runs a user findUnique, and each reopen triggers full REST reloads (conversation list, the thread's newest 1000 messages, the notification list).
rawFindings.impact: With about 10k users, every Railway deploy or restart causes a synchronized burst: up to 2 sockets per tab plus the heavy /api/conversations aggregation for every open /messages tab, all within about 1 s. The per-IP 600/min limit can also trip for users behind shared carrier NAT (inference).
rawFindings.evidence: useChatSocket.ts:50 and useNotifications.ts:93 (no Math.random); node_modules/@fastify/websocket/index.js defaultPreClose closes all server.clients; server.ts:308 app.close(); chat.routes.ts:204 lookup on every connect; useMessenger.ts:218-223 reloadList + loadThread; useNotifications.ts:110 refresh.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Use full jitter (delay = random(0, cap)), add a random 0-3 s stagger before post-reconnect reloads, and make the reload incremental (messages newer than the last known createdAt). Close with code 1012 on shutdown so clients can apply a longer randomized delay.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Conversation list and history are still unpaginated and are re-fetched in full on reconnect
rawFindings.rootCause: GET /api/conversations loads every conversation of the user with no take/cursor. The last-message aggregation groups every message of those conversations. It loads IDs of every vacancy of every counterpart company, then every matching application, and sorts in memory. History returns a fixed newest 1000 with no cursor. The client re-fetches both on every reconnect and on the first message from an unknown conversation, and its thread cache is never trimmed.
rawFindings.impact: Active employers (thousands of conversations, 100k+ messages) and seekers who chat with large companies get slow, multi-MB responses. The cost repeats on every reconnect (including the 15 min token-expiry cycle). History beyond 1000 messages cannot be reached.
rawFindings.evidence: chat.routes.ts:356-381 findMany with no take; 122-139 $group over all messages; 398-433 all vacancy IDs, then applications; 500 in-memory sort; 158 and 523-528 MESSAGES_LIMIT=1000; useMessenger.ts:50 threads cache; 173-176 and 221-222 reloads.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Cursor-paginate conversations (take 30, ordered by a denormalized lastMessageAt on Conversation, updated in deliverMessage). Paginate history with before=createdAt and take 50. Load vacancy context only for the returned page. Reconnect should fetch only changes since the last seen time. Trim the client cache to recent threads.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-046 (PARTIAL: no cursor pagination; still accurate)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium. Needs a denormalized field and UI infinite scroll.

rawFindings.title: Header polls inbox and notifications in every tab, including hidden ones, on top of up to two open sockets
rawFindings.rootCause: Header polls /api/inbox/summary every 20 s and the bell polls /api/notifications every 45 s, in every authenticated tab, with no visibility check and no slowdown while the WS is connected. The bell opens its own WS per tab and /messages opens a second one. The server sends every chat and notification payload to all sockets. Unread message counts are never pushed over WS.
rawFindings.impact: Each idle tab costs about 4 REST calls per minute. Each inbox summary call reads all of the user's conversation IDs and runs a message count, and for employers also ownedVacancyIds plus an application count. At 10k users with multiple tabs this is steady DB load and doubled WS fan-out, and it uses up the per-IP rate limit.
rawFindings.evidence: useInboxSummary.ts:45 setInterval 20000; useNotifications.ts:68 45_000 and 102 second WS; Header.tsx:163 bell on every page; useMessenger.ts:153 chat WS; realtime.ts:36-41 sends to all sockets; chat.routes.ts:673-695 summary queries.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Share one WS per tab through a context. Push unread counters (messages, new applications, notifications) as WS events. Pause polling while document.hidden, and poll only as a slow fallback (e.g. 2-5 min) while the WS is connected.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium

rawFindings.title: Backend notification texts are stored as Uzbek strings and links drop the locale prefix
rawFindings.rootCause: User has no locale field. Callers build Uzbek title/body/CTA strings, and those are saved as final text in Notification.title/body, so they cannot be re-rendered per language. The bell and center show the server strings. Telegram, email and push links are WEB_ORIGIN plus the path, with no /ru or /en prefix. The chat Telegram alert and the email CTA default ('Saytda ochish') are also Uzbek.
rawFindings.impact: RU/EN users see Uzbek in-app, Telegram, push and email notifications, and every link opens the Uzbek version of the site.
rawFindings.evidence: schema.prisma User model (no locale/lang field); applications.routes.ts:105-116 and 359-374; admin.routes.ts:315-321 and 385-391; alerts.service.ts:217-229; notifications.service.ts:92-93, 100-107, 135, 182; chat.routes.ts:87; NotificationBell.tsx renders items from the API.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add User.locale (set from UI language on login or on switch). Store the type plus structured params in payload and render titles on the client with i18n. For external channels, render with the user's locale and build locale-prefixed absolute links using a shared loc() helper.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-073 (NOT FIXED), ISSUE-103 (NOT FIXED): still accurate
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium. Needs a schema addition and client rendering by type.

rawFindings.title: 'system' notification type covers broadcasts, moderation results and payments, and users can mute it on every channel
rawFindings.rootCause: There are only 4 types. Admin broadcast, vacancy rejection, company verification and billing all use 'system'. The preferences API lets users disable 'system' on any channel, including in_app, and deliver() honours that. No non-mutable security category exists for rule G/L events (phone changed, recovery started, sessions invalidated).
rawFindings.impact: A user who mutes marketing broadcasts also stops getting vacancy-rejection and verification notices (the employer never learns why a vacancy disappeared). Future security alerts would be mutable or mixed with broadcasts.
rawFindings.evidence: schema.prisma:119-124; admin.routes.ts:574 broadcast type 'system'; 315-321 rejection 'system'; 385-391 verification 'system'; notifications.routes.ts:11-35 and 148-173 (system and in_app can be disabled); notifications.service.ts:52-61, 90, 96.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Split into 'moderation', 'broadcast' and 'security' types. Treat 'security' as mandatory (always in_app plus Telegram when linked; never disableable) and 'moderation' as in_app-mandatory. Update the preferences matrix and the web adapter categories.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium. Additive enum; existing rows stay 'system'.

rawFindings.title: A lost ack plus 'Retry' creates duplicate messages; the server has no clientId idempotency
rawFindings.rootCause: The server echoes clientId but never stores or deduplicates it. If the socket drops after the server saves the message but before the echo arrives, the client marks the bubble failed after 10 s. The reconnect reload merges server items with every local non-sent item, so the saved copy and the failed copy both show. Pressing retry saves a second copy.
rawFindings.impact: The sender sees their message twice (once sent, once failed). If they retry, the receiver gets a duplicate. This is most likely on mobile networks.
rawFindings.evidence: chat.routes.ts:62-71 and 277-278 (clientId not stored); useMessenger.ts:103-111 (local non-sent kept next to server items); 234-240 10 s timeout; 269-275 retry calls dispatch again.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Store clientId on Message (sparse unique index on [senderId, clientId]) and return the existing row on repeat. Include clientId in the history REST response so the reload can reconcile local bubbles.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low (additive field and index)

rawFindings.title: WS frames are processed concurrently, so rapid messages can be saved out of order
rawFindings.rootCause: Each 'message' event starts handle() independently. After the shared ready promise, every frame does its own participantsOf lookup and message.create, so creation order follows DB timing rather than arrival order.
rawFindings.impact: Two messages sent back to back can be stored and shown with swapped createdAt order for both sides (inference: depends on DB latency variance).
rawFindings.evidence: chat.routes.ts:281-284 ws.on('message', raw => handle(raw).catch(...)); 259 participantsOf per frame; 278 deliverMessage.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Serialize per connection with a promise chain (queue = queue.then(() => handle(raw))) and cache the participants per conversationId for the life of the connection.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: A socket is registered and receives live payloads before its session check completes
rawFindings.rootCause: addSocket runs right after signature verification. The blocked/tokenVersion lookup finishes later. Only inbound frames wait for ready; sendToUser and notify() push to the socket immediately, and isOnline becomes true.
rawFindings.impact: A token with a valid signature but a revoked session (for example stolen, used after logout) can connect repeatedly and receive live messages and notifications during each DB round trip. The same window also suppresses the Telegram fallback. Exposure is small but non-zero.
rawFindings.evidence: chat.routes.ts:197-199 addSocket before the check; 204-224 the check closes with 4403/4401; realtime.ts:36-47; D-022 describes only inbound frames waiting.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Register the socket (or mark it deliverable) only after ready resolves true. Queue outbound payloads for the few milliseconds it takes, or accept the tiny delivery delay.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Server closes every socket at token expiry, forcing a full reconnect and reload every 15 minutes
rawFindings.rootCause: The expiry timer closes with 4401 when the 15 min access token expires. The client always calls refreshSession() on 4401, even if a fresh token is already stored, then reconnects. onOpen(reconnected) triggers a full list and thread reload. Sends during the gap fail immediately.
rawFindings.impact: Every open /messages tab gets a periodic 'Yuborilmadi' risk plus a heavy reload (list aggregation and up to 1000 messages). Each bell socket also runs a notifications refresh.
rawFindings.evidence: chat.routes.ts:227-231; jwt.ts:36 expiresIn 15m; useChatSocket.ts:81-90; useMessenger.ts:218-223 and 230-233 (send returns false and the bubble fails).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Support an in-band {type:'auth', token} frame that extends expiry without reconnecting. Otherwise, on 4401 reconnect straight away with getAccessToken() when it differs from the token used, and make the post-reconnect sync incremental.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-019 (FIXED client-side token-change reconnect; server expiry close remains)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Client has no liveness check; a half-open socket still shows as connected
rawFindings.rootCause: Browsers do not expose ping/pong, and the hooks have no app-level heartbeat. A failed send ack does not force a reconnect, and there are no 'online' or 'visibilitychange' listeners, so recovery waits for the OS TCP timeout or the next scheduled backoff (up to 30 s).
rawFindings.impact: After a network switch or sleep, the UI can report connected while sends fail one by one after 10 s, and incoming messages are missed until TCP gives up.
rawFindings.evidence: useChatSocket.ts:56-107 (no heartbeat and no online listener); useMessenger.ts:234-240 (timeout only marks failed); ConversationPane.tsx:51 offline banner driven only by onclose.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add an app-level ping frame every ~25 s with a pong timeout that closes and reconnects. Reconnect right away on 'online' and 'visibilitychange'. Force a reconnect after an ack timeout.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low (needs server support for a 'ping' frame type)

rawFindings.title: WS access token still travels in the query string (outside app logs, which are already redacted)
rawFindings.rootCause: The browser WS API cannot set headers, so the 15 min access token goes in ?token=. Fastify logs are redacted, but upstream proxy or edge access logs outside the app may record full URLs (inference; not verified for Railway).
rawFindings.impact: Access tokens could persist in infrastructure logs. They are short-lived and tokenVersion-bound, so impact is limited.
rawFindings.evidence: chat.routes.ts:182-189; useChatSocket.ts:59 and useNotifications.ts:102; server.ts:54-58 redactUrl; ISSUES.md ISSUE-030 recommended a one-time ticket long term.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add POST /api/ws-ticket (requireAuth) that returns a random 30 s single-use ticket stored hashed in memory; the WS accepts ?ticket= and re-checks the user. Or send the token in the first frame.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-030 (FIXED for app logs; ticket not implemented)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium

rawFindings.title: In-memory socket registry is not listed in the single-replica deploy constraint
rawFindings.rootCause: realtime.ts keeps sockets in a process-local Map. DEPLOY.md explains numReplicas 1 only by Telegram long polling and the alerts scheduler. The obvious plan of moving those to a worker would still silently break WS delivery and isOnline across replicas.
rawFindings.impact: If the API is scaled horizontally, messages and notifications reach only sockets on the same instance, and isOnline is wrong, so Telegram fallback is skipped or sent incorrectly. No error is raised.
rawFindings.evidence: realtime.ts:14 const sockets = new Map; DEPLOY.md:95-101; railway.json numReplicas 1.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Document the WS registry as a third reason for one replica, and note that scaling needs sticky sessions plus a pub/sub fan-out (or Mongo change streams) for sendToUser and isOnline.
rawFindings.fixRisk: None (docs)

rawFindings.title: No retention for notifications; every broadcast adds one document per user
rawFindings.rootCause: There is no TTL index or cleanup job for Notification (no notification.deleteMany outside demo seed). The admin broadcast calls notify() per user, which creates one in_app row per user.
rawFindings.impact: The notifications collection grows without bound (10k rows per broadcast plus alerts), raising storage and index size. The UI only shows the newest 30-100 rows, so older rows are never read.
rawFindings.evidence: schema.prisma:614-630 (no TTL); admin.routes.ts:574 notify per user; grep found no notification.deleteMany in src except prisma/demo-seed.ts:1565 (messages).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add a scheduled cleanup (for example delete read notifications older than 90 days and all older than 180 days) in the existing scheduler, or a TTL index on created_at created with a raw command.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-053 (merged sources R109/R242 flagged retention; not implemented)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Service worker push click calls navigate() on possibly uncontrolled windows
rawFindings.rootCause: matchAll uses includeUncontrolled:true, then calls client.navigate(target) on the first same-origin window. WindowClient.navigate rejects for clients this SW does not control (for example hard-reloaded tabs), and the rejection aborts the chain before focus() or openWindow().
rawFindings.impact: Clicking a push notification sometimes does nothing when the only open tab is uncontrolled.
rawFindings.evidence: sw.js:32-40 matchAll({type:'window', includeUncontrolled:true}), client.navigate(target) then return client.focus(), with no catch or openWindow fallback.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Try navigate only on controlled clients (client.frameType plus a check that the client belongs to this SW), catch errors, and fall back to client.focus() plus postMessage, or self.clients.openWindow(target).
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Telegram login is still a working login method (/api/auth/telegram/start and /poll, button on the login page), which breaks rule A
rawFindings.rootCause: Telegram was built as a third login method. auth.routes.ts:137-158 opens a full session (telegramLogin -> issueTokens plus refresh cookie) after the user confirms in the bot. The lg<token> flow is in telegram.service.ts:112-190 and 283-321. The deep-link payload is the polling secret itself (telegram.service.ts:142 payload=`lg${token}`; auth.routes.ts:145-146). Anyone who sees the t.me URL can poll it and race the owner for the one-time result, because consumeLoginToken deletes the entry on the first read (:152).
rawFindings.impact: Violates rule A. Whoever controls the linked Telegram chat gets a 30-day session with no password and skips login-guard. That includes a stolen Telegram session or a victim tricked into pressing Confirm. The UI and FAQ point users to Telegram login as the replacement for password recovery.
rawFindings.evidence: auth.routes.ts:133-158; telegram.service.ts:12 ('5) Telegram orqali kirish'), 135-154, 156-190, 248-250, 310-315; SocialLogin.tsx:90-116, 145-154 (rendered on login/+Page.tsx:97); messages.uz.ts:362 'Telegram orqali kirish', :465 FAQ says to log in via «Telegram»; messages.en.ts:357, 459; README.md:92, 137; apps/web/DESIGN.md:184.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Remove /api/auth/telegram/start and /poll, telegramLogin(), loginTokens/handleLoginStart and the lgok/lgno callback handling. On the web side remove startTelegramLogin/pollTelegramLogin, the Telegram button and the tg*/withTelegram i18n keys in all 3 locales. Rewrite the FAQ answer and the README/DESIGN lines. Keep the bot for linking, phone verification and recovery. An unknown /start payload should get a generic safe reply. Add an e2e check that the removed routes return 404.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low, but ship the Telegram recovery flow (rule B) in the same release so users who relied on Telegram login still have a way back in.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-010 (FIXED, but the fix only added a confirm button), ISSUE-122 (NOT FIXED, no tests), D-039

rawFindings.title: No password recovery, password change or manual recovery flow exists (rules B, H, I, J)
rawFindings.rootCause: The auth API has only register, login, refresh, logout, me, google and telegram (auth.routes.ts:63-181). Grepping apps/api/src finds no reset, forgot, recovery or change-password code. The schema has no recovery token, recovery request or backup phone model (schema.prisma:160-205). 'Forgot password' links to /support (login/+Page.tsx:82-87). Google-created accounts get a random, unusable hash with a comment promising later recovery (auth.service.ts:233-235).
rawFindings.impact: A user who forgets the password has no self-service path; the only documented workaround is Telegram login, which rule A forbids. Google-only users can never set a password. A user whose password leaked cannot change it (only log out everywhere). Admins have no verified manual recovery tool, which pushes support toward ad-hoc DB edits.
rawFindings.evidence: auth.routes.ts:63-181; login/+Page.tsx:82-87; auth.service.ts:233-235; schema.prisma:160-205 (no recovery or backup-phone fields/models); messages.uz.ts:464-465 FAQ; FINAL_AUDIT.md:10, 140; DECISIONS.md D-010 (was left pending; the owner has now chosen Telegram-only).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add a PasswordRecovery model {userId, tokenHash (sha256), expiresAt of 10-15 min, usedAt, attempts}, reusing the team.routes.ts invite hashing and updateMany claim. POST recovery/start: takes a phone, always returns a generic 200, rate-limited per IP+phone, returns a random opaque deep-link payload. The bot checks the chat belongs to the verified primary or backup phone owner, then sends a one-time site link. POST recovery/complete: sets a new argon2 hash, bumps tokenVersion, revokes other recovery tokens. POST change-password requires the current password. Add a ManualRecoveryRequest model plus admin review that can only trigger a verified phone reset, never set a password. Return 503 when the bot is offline.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: a new security-sensitive flow. Needs e2e tests for replay, expiry, rate limits and session invalidation.

rawFindings.title: The per-email login lockout lets anyone keep a victim locked out indefinitely (rule I)
rawFindings.rootCause: assertLoginAllowed runs before the password check (auth.service.ts:93). After 10 failures for an email in a fixed 15-min window it returns 429 (login-guard.ts:12-14, 27-36), whatever the IP and even when the password is correct. The counter is keyed only by the victim's email. When 50k keys are reached, the oldest entries are evicted (login-guard.ts:45-49).
rawFindings.impact: Sending 10 wrong passwords every 15 minutes is well under the 10/min per-IP limit (auth.routes.ts:59-61) and keeps any known email unable to log in, permanently. With no recovery flow (ISSUE-012) the owner has no way around it. In the other direction, with spoofed X-Forwarded-For an attacker could flood 50k fake emails to evict the victim's counter and keep guessing (inference).
rawFindings.evidence: login-guard.ts:12-14, 27-36, 38-51; auth.service.ts:90-107 (the guard runs before argon2.verify); DECISIONS.md D-007 lists the risk as 'lockout DoS — MENING QARORIM KERAK' ('I need a decision'), still open; e2e [ISSUE-011] expects 429 on the 11th attempt.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Replace the hard lock with throttling that cannot deny the owner. Count failures per (email, client IP or /24). Use a softer per-email global backoff capped around 30-60 s instead of a 15-min block. Exempt devices that logged in successfully before (signed known-device cookie). Add a CAPTCHA or proof-of-work only after N failures. Prune by TTL instead of insertion order. Use a shared store if there is ever more than one replica.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium: the e2e expectation must be updated.

rawFindings.title: Google sign-in logs into any existing account with the same email, including unverified password accounts and staff/admin accounts
rawFindings.rootCause: googleLogin looks the user up by normalized email and issues tokens for whatever account it finds (auth.service.ts:222-226). Registration never verifies email; isEmailVerified stays false (auth.service.ts:44-60). User has no stored Google subject or link field (schema.prisma:160-178), so there is no notion of an explicitly linked Google identity. There is no role restriction.
rawFindings.impact: Pre-account takeover: an attacker registers victim@gmail.com with a password. Later the victim clicks 'Continue with Google' and works inside the attacker's account, which the attacker can still open with the password (CVs, applications, chats). For admin or staff accounts on Google-hosted mail, Google alone gets in, skipping the password and login-guard. Breaks the rule that Google login must not merge accounts unsafely.
rawFindings.evidence: auth.service.ts:218-226 (existing account -> issueTokens); :37-60 (no email verification); :241 isEmailVerified is set only for Google-created users; SocialLogin.tsx:53-58; DECISIONS.md D-011 kept the merge knowingly.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Store googleSub on User (unique, sparse) and log in by googleSub only. If the email belongs to an account without googleSub, return 409 ACCOUNT_EXISTS; the user logs in with the password and links Google from settings after re-entering it. Never auto-link staff or admin roles. On first Google login, backfill googleSub for accounts that were created via Google.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium: existing password users who have been signing in with Google must link once.

rawFindings.title: ensureAdminUser promotes any existing account with ADMIN_EMAIL to admin on every boot
rawFindings.rootCause: On every startup (server.ts:271 bootstrap) ensureAdminUser finds the user with ADMIN_EMAIL and, if the role is not admin, changes it to admin (ensure-admin.ts:23-29). It does not check who created the account, its password, email verification or block state. Public registration accepts any email without verification (auth.routes.ts:64-69; auth.service.ts:37-60).
rawFindings.impact: Suppose an attacker registers the ADMIN_EMAIL before the operator first boots with it or rotates to it (such emails are often guessable, e.g. admin@domain). The attacker's own password account becomes a full admin with access to all candidate data, moderation and role grants. It also silently re-promotes an account that a super admin deliberately demoted, on every restart. Requires the attacker to register first.
rawFindings.evidence: ensure-admin.ts:20-29 (if existing and role !== 'admin' -> update role to admin); auth.service.ts:37-60; DEPLOY.md:64, 210 (operator sets ADMIN_EMAIL, then logs in).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Create the admin only when the email is free. If a non-admin account already exists, log a warning and do nothing. Promotion then happens through the admin UI or a one-shot CLI command. Never re-promote on later boots. Optionally, before any promotion, require ADMIN_PASSWORD to match the existing hash.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: operators who relied on auto-promotion promote once by hand.

rawFindings.title: Telegram linking has no confirmation and moves a chat away from another account; a link sent by an attacker captures the victim's verified phone
rawFindings.rootCause: On /start <linkToken> the bot links the chat to the token's account right away (telegram.service.ts:262-273). First it unlinks the chat from any other account via updateMany (:269-272), then it asks for the contact. handleContact saves the shared phone as verified on whichever account the chat is linked to, with no uniqueness check (:333-343). The ISSUE-010 fix added confirmation only to login.
rawFindings.impact: An attacker logged in as account A sends his t.me link to a victim ('verify your account'). The victim presses Start and shares the contact, so A gets the victim's phone as verified, bypassing requirePhoneVerified anti-spam. The victim's own account silently loses its Telegram link. Rule F (one Telegram identity per account) is enforced by taking the chat, not by refusing. Once Telegram becomes the recovery channel this gets close to account takeover.
rawFindings.evidence: telegram.service.ts:262-280, 323-343; telegram.routes.ts:25-35 (link token), 38-44 (unlink, no audit); schema.prisma:172-176 (telegramChatId not unique); ISSUES.md ISSUE-010 Impact already describes the link-token variant.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: If the chat is already linked to another account, refuse with a generic reply. Otherwise show the target account (masked email) and require an inline Confirm tied to the chat id and a one-time token. Store the Telegram user id (from.id) under a unique sparse index. Reject a shared contact whose phone is already verified on another account. Record security events for link, unlink and phone verification. Hash link tokens and limit them to 10 min or less.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: changes the verification UX; needs a manual bot test.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-010 (the link-token variant was never addressed)

rawFindings.title: No security audit log: role grants, blocks, session revocations, Telegram link/unlink and phone verification leave no record (rule L)
rawFindings.rootCause: The schema has no audit or security-event model (grep finds no *Log/*Event/*Audit/*Session model), and none of the sensitive handlers record anything: admin block/role (admin.routes.ts:190-226), team role/block (team.routes.ts:168-216), logout revocation (auth.routes.ts:102-127), Telegram link/unlink (telegram.service.ts:268-273; telegram.routes.ts:38-44), phone verification (telegram.service.ts:339-343). The only trace is a pino warning when logout fails (auth.routes.ts:122).
rawFindings.impact: None of the rule L events can be produced. Admin abuse (granting admin, blocking other admins) or a hijack through Telegram cannot be investigated or shown to the user. The manual recovery flow required by rule H has no audit trail to write to.
rawFindings.evidence: schema.prisma (no security-event model); admin.routes.ts:190-226; team.routes.ts:168-216; auth.routes.ts:102-127; telegram.routes.ts:38-44; telegram.service.ts:268-273, 339-343.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add a SecurityEvent model {userId, actorUserId?, type enum (PHONE_VERIFIED, BACKUP_PHONE_ADDED, PHONE_CHANGED, RECOVERY_STARTED, RECOVERY_COMPLETED, SESSIONS_REVOKED, MANUAL_RECOVERY_APPROVED, TELEGRAM_LINKED, TELEGRAM_UNLINKED, ROLE_CHANGED, BLOCKED), ipHash?, userAgent?, meta without secrets, createdAt}, indexed on [userId, createdAt] and [type, createdAt]. Add a recordSecurityEvent() helper that rejects token and password fields, call it from these handlers, and add a read-only admin view.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: purely additive.

rawFindings.title: The documented deployment makes the refresh cookie third-party (vercel.app page, up.railway.app API); Safari/WebKit likely blocks it, so sessions end after 15 minutes
rawFindings.rootCause: Sessions depend on a cross-site SameSite=None refresh cookie (auth.routes.ts:30-46). DEPLOY and README put the site on *.vercel.app and the API on *.up.railway.app (DEPLOY.md:63, 82-85, 189; README.md:189-190). Both are public suffixes, so the API is a different site. Safari's ITP blocks all third-party cookies (this covers WebKit browsers on iOS), as do browsers with third-party cookies turned off. They ignore Set-Cookie on these fetches and never send the cookie.
rawFindings.impact: Inference; this audit did not test WebKit, and the earlier browser runs do not appear to either. On iPhone/Safari a user logs in and the 15-min access token in localStorage works. After that, refresh returns accessToken:null and the user drops to guest (AuthContext restore and the 12-min interval). Logout in these browsers cannot revoke server sessions because the cookie is never sent. A large share of mobile users would be affected.
rawFindings.evidence: auth.routes.ts:30-49 (the comment itself says web and API are on different domains); session.ts:118-132 (refresh with credentials: include); DEPLOY.md:63 WEB_ORIGIN https://ishbor.vercel.app, :82-85; README.md:189-190 ('site and API are on different domains').
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Make the cookie first-party. Preferred: proxy /api/* (at least /api/auth/*) through the web origin (Vercel rewrite to Railway, and the same in apps/web/server/index.mjs) and use SameSite=Lax. Alternative: serve the API from api.<site-domain>; Safari may cap cookies from CNAME-cloaked subdomains at 7 days, so the proxy is safer. Update DEPLOY.md and add a WebKit Playwright check for login followed by refresh.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: touches API_URL, CORS, cookie settings and the WebSocket URL; test SSR and WebSocket paths.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-097 covers the same cookie from the CSRF side; no issue covers third-party blocking

rawFindings.title: Per-IP auth rate limits can still be bypassed by default (TRUST_PROXY=true), so signup and argon2 work are effectively unthrottled
rawFindings.rootCause: TRUST_PROXY defaults to true (env.ts:113-123; .env.example:52), so req.ip comes from the client-controlled X-Forwarded-For header (server.ts:77). That makes the 10/min strictRateLimit on login, register and google (auth.routes.ts:59-61) and the 600/min global limit (server.ts:129-131) bypassable. Register has no per-email or global cap. Every login attempt, including unknown emails (dummy hash, auth.service.ts:95-96), and every register runs argon2id with m=64MiB, t=3, p=4 (argon2.cjs:31-35).
rawFindings.impact: Mass fake-account creation (no email verification, no CAPTCHA). Password spraying across many emails is still possible, since the per-email guard allows 10 guesses per email per 15 min. A flood of spoofed-IP login/register requests queues argon2 jobs on the 4-thread libuv pool and delays other threadpool work: file uploads, static files, and DNS lookups for Telegram, Google and SMTP. The threadpool effect is an inference, not load-tested.
rawFindings.evidence: env.ts:113-123; .env.example:52; server.ts:77, 129-139; auth.routes.ts:59-61; apps/api/node_modules/argon2/argon2.cjs:31-35; DEPLOY.md:70 only recommends '1'.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: In production, have env.ts reject TRUST_PROXY=true and require a hop count or CIDR (Railway: 1). Put a small semaphore around argon2 hash/verify (for example 4 concurrent, bounded queue, 429/503 when full). Add caps that do not depend on IP: a global per-minute cap on register, and an email+IP key on login.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: a wrong hop count puts all users behind one IP; check req.ip in logs after deploy.

rawFindings.title: Any admin can grant admin, or block and demote every other admin, with one call; no re-authentication and no last-admin guard
rawFindings.rootCause: PATCH /api/admin/users/:id/role accepts role 'admin', and PATCH /block accepts any target. The only check is 'not yourself' (admin.routes.ts:190-194, 217-221). The team PATCH endpoint is the same (team.routes.ts:168-184). No password re-entry, no protection for the last active admin, no notification to other admins.
rawFindings.impact: A stolen admin access token (15 min, stored in localStorage, web has no CSP) is enough to promote an attacker account to admin and block every other admin; each block also revokes that admin's sessions. Getting control back then requires DB access. The web admin page has a one-click 'make admin' button (pages/admin/users/+Page.tsx:151-153).
rawFindings.evidence: admin.routes.ts:190-226; team.routes.ts:168-216; apps/web/src/pages/admin/users/+Page.tsx:151-153.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Require re-authentication (current password, which yields a short-lived elevated token) before granting or removing admin or blocking an admin. Refuse to block or demote the last non-blocked admin. Record security events and notify the other admins.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-035 and ISSUE-108 fixed reading roles from the DB; this gap is not tracked

rawFindings.title: Refresh tokens are stateless and never rotated; a stolen refresh cookie keeps working, and keeps renewing itself, until the user logs out everywhere
rawFindings.rootCause: refreshSession checks the signature and tokenVersion, then signs a new token with the same version (auth.service.ts:131-146; jwt.ts:41-46). Old tokens stay valid until their 30-day expiry. There is no jti, no session store and no reuse detection. The only revocation is incrementing tokenVersion, which logs out every device.
rawFindings.impact: A copied cookie (from a device backup, malware or proxy logs) can be used alongside the real one indefinitely, with no detection and no 'active sessions' list. Rule J ('invalidate refresh tokens') is met only through the global version bump. The session policy allows this, but theft is invisible.
rawFindings.evidence: auth.service.ts:131-154; jwt.ts:41-46 (30d); auth.routes.ts:84-86 (cookie is re-set on every refresh).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add a RefreshSession model {jti, userId, familyId, tokenHash, expiresAt, revokedAt, lastUsedAt, userAgent} with a TTL index. Rotate on every refresh and revoke the whole family when a rotated token is reused. Keep tokenVersion for global revocation. At 10k users the collection stays small.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: parallel refreshes from several tabs need a short grace window.

rawFindings.title: JWT verification still accepts tokens without typ or v (legacy fallback); any such token would be impossible to revoke
rawFindings.rootCause: decode() accepts a missing typ (jwt.ts:53-54). verifyAccessToken omits v when it is absent (:61-62). requireAuth and the WebSocket skip the version check when v is undefined (auth-guard.ts:56; chat.routes.ts:203-214). Every token issued before the fix expired long ago (30 days at most).
rawFindings.impact: This is dead compatibility code. If any future signing path forgets typ or v, its tokens would survive logout and block. Such tokens could also be used as either access or refresh tokens when both secrets are equal, which dev allows.
rawFindings.evidence: jwt.ts:12, 53-54, 61-62; auth-guard.ts:56; chat.routes.ts:203-214.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: In decode(), require typ === expected and a numeric v. Remove the optional-v branches in auth-guard and the WebSocket handler.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Access token is stored in localStorage while the web origin has no CSP
rawFindings.rootCause: setAccessToken writes the bearer token to localStorage (session.ts:25, 96-104). vercel.json sets nosniff, X-Frame-Options, COOP, Referrer-Policy and HSTS headers but no Content-Security-Policy.
rawFindings.impact: Any XSS on the web origin can read a valid token. It can also call /api/auth/refresh with credentials, because the web origin is on the CORS allowlist. Admin tokens are exposed, which combines badly with the one-click admin grant.
rawFindings.evidence: session.ts:25, 96-104; apps/web/vercel.json headers block (no CSP).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Once the refresh cookie is first-party, keep the token in memory only and restore it with a refresh on page load. Ship a web CSP, starting in Report-Only mode.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium: CSP must allow the Google GIS script and the inline theme script.

rawFindings.title: Registration reveals whether an email is already registered (409 returned before hashing)
rawFindings.rootCause: registerUser returns 409 'Bu email bilan foydalanuvchi allaqachon mavjud' ('a user with this email already exists') before argon2 runs (auth.service.ts:39-42), so both the message and the response time differ. Login does not have this problem; it runs a dummy hash for unknown emails.
rawFindings.impact: The user base can be enumerated by email, which helps target lockouts, phishing and pre-account takeover. The per-IP limit that would slow this can be bypassed with X-Forwarded-For.
rawFindings.evidence: auth.service.ts:37-42 vs 90-99.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: If this trade-off is accepted, throttle register much harder. Otherwise return a generic response and continue through a verification step once phone/Telegram verification becomes part of signup.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Password policy only checks length (8-128); no common-password check, 8-char admin password allowed, signup field has no minLength
rawFindings.rootCause: registerSchema uses z.string().min(8).max(128) (auth.routes.ts:18). Invite accept is the same (team.routes.ts:233). ADMIN_PASSWORD is accepted at 8 characters (ensure-admin.ts:32). The signup PasswordField has no minLength, so a short password produces a raw English zod error.
rawFindings.impact: Passwords like '12345678' are accepted. With bypassable IP limits and 10 guesses per email every 15 min, spraying common passwords across many accounts is feasible.
rawFindings.evidence: auth.routes.ts:18; team.routes.ts:233; ensure-admin.ts:32-38.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Reject a small embedded list of the most common passwords and passwords equal to the email's local part. Require at least 12 characters for staff and admin. Add a localized minLength check in the client.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: The 'Remember me' checkbox on the login page does nothing
rawFindings.rootCause: The remember state is never sent or used (login/+Page.tsx:22, 73-81). The API always sets a 30-day refresh cookie (auth.routes.ts:49).
rawFindings.impact: A user on a shared computer who unchecks it still gets a 30-day session. The control is misleading on a security-relevant setting.
rawFindings.evidence: login/+Page.tsx:22, 73-81; auth.routes.ts:48-50.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Remove the checkbox, or send remember:false to /login and set the refresh cookie without maxAge (a browser-session cookie) or with a shorter lifetime.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-044 (raw finding R206 mentioned it; not fixed)

rawFindings.title: Signup, and the login page's link to signup, drop the returnTo target
rawFindings.rootCause: After signup, done() always goes to /employer or /profile (signup/+Page.tsx:34). The login page links to plain l('/signup') (login/+Page.tsx:101-102), so ?returnTo is lost. safeReturnTo itself is correct (returnTo.ts:7-16).
rawFindings.impact: A guest who hits a guarded page (for example, applying to a vacancy) and chooses to register lands on the profile instead of returning to the page. This adds friction to the core apply funnel.
rawFindings.evidence: signup/+Page.tsx:34, 143; login/+Page.tsx:101-102; returnTo.ts:27-34.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Pass returnTo through on the signup link and use returnTargetOr(fallback) in signup's done() and in its SocialLogin onDone.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Telegram is still a login channel: /api/auth/telegram/start and /poll mint sessions
