rawFindings.rootCause: The earlier audit hardened Telegram login (a confirm button, ISSUE-010) instead of removing it. /poll issues access and refresh tokens for whatever account is bound to the Telegram chat that pressed confirm.
rawFindings.impact: Violates rule A. Whoever controls a Telegram chat bound to an account can get a full session without the password; combined with the link-binding flaw below, a bound chat equals account access.
rawFindings.evidence: auth.routes.ts:137-147 creates a login token and t.me deep link. 149-158 poll calls consumeLoginToken, then telegramLogin(entry.userId), setRefreshCookie and returns accessToken. auth.service.ts:176-181 telegramLogin issues tokens with only a blocked check. telegram.service.ts:156-190 handleLoginStart finds the user by telegramChatId; 284-321 the callback sets status 'confirmed' and userId.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Delete the telegram/start and telegram/poll routes, the loginTokens map, the 'lg' prefix handling, handleLoginStart, the lgok/lgno callback, and the web 'login with Telegram' button. Reuse the confirm pattern only for the recovery, phone-change and link challenges defined in rules B, D and G.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-010 (FIXED: confirm step added, flow kept); ISSUE-122 / D-039 (untested)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low on the API. The web login page and i18n strings need updating. Telegram-only users need password or Google, and no recovery exists yet (D-010).

rawFindings.title: Telegram link deep link binds a chat to an account without confirmation and silently takes the chat from its current account
rawFindings.rootCause: handleStart trusts possession of the payload alone. It unlinks the chat from any other account and binds it to the token's user. It asks for no confirmation naming the target account and sends no notice to the previous account.
rawFindings.impact: If a user opens a link generated by another account (phishing), their Telegram gets bound to that account. The bot then asks them to share their contact, so the attacker's account receives the victim's verified phone, and the victim's own account silently loses its Telegram link. If a victim's link leaks, the opener's chat is bound to the victim's account, which today enables Telegram login and would later control the planned Telegram recovery (rule B).
rawFindings.evidence: telegram.service.ts:262-273: verifyLinkToken(payload), then updateMany({telegramChatId: chatId, id not userId}) sets it to null, then update({id: userId}, {telegramChatId}). 275-280: reply 'Hisobingiz bog'landi!' with no account identity, plus CONTACT_KEYBOARD. 90-110: tokens are stored raw in an in-memory Map. telegram.routes.ts:25-35: link creation has only requireAuth, with no route rate limit. Exploitation needs social engineering (inference).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: After /start <payload>, show confirm/deny buttons with the masked account email. Refuse to rebind a chat that is linked to another account unless that account confirms or unlinks first. Notify the old account and write a security event. Hash tokens and keep them in the DB with TTL and single use. Rate-limit link creation.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: none (ISSUE-010 added confirmation to the login flow only)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: the bot UX and web Telegram status polling change; existing links are unaffected.

rawFindings.title: Verified phone is not unique and verification survives relinking: one Telegram account can phone-verify unlimited accounts
rawFindings.rootCause: handleContact sets phone and isPhoneVerified=true with no uniqueness check. Relinking or unlinking never clears the old account's verification. User.phone has no unique index. PATCH /api/profile accepts a free-text phone and an unverified additionalPhone.
rawFindings.impact: requirePhoneVerified gates applying, posting vacancies, starting chats and reviews. One Telegram account can verify account A, relink to B, verify B, and so on, which enables fake applications, spam and self-reviews (own seeker accounts apply to own vacancy, then leave auto-approved reviews). The same 'verified' phone on many accounts makes phone-based recovery ambiguous. Employers see unverified, possibly third-party numbers as candidate contacts.
rawFindings.evidence: telegram.service.ts:339-343 update {phone, isPhoneVerified:true} with no lookup of other holders; 269-273 relink clears only telegramChatId. telegram.routes.ts:38-42 unlink keeps isPhoneVerified. schema.prisma:163 phone String? with no @unique; 217 additionalPhone. profile.routes.ts:59-67 writes phone while unverified; 74 saves additionalPhone. auth-guard.ts:90-103 checks only the boolean. applications.routes.ts:196-197 and 285-286 return phone to employers.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Normalize phone to E.164 and add a unique index on verified phones. On contact share, reject a phone already verified on another account, or run an explicit transfer flow that writes a security event. Clear isPhoneVerified when a chat is relinked or unlinked. Verify the backup phone through Telegram with the same uniqueness rule. Stop accepting a free-text phone in PATCH /api/profile.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: none (ISSUE-087 covers only where the gate is applied)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: existing duplicate phones need a migration or conflict report before the index; check demo seed data.

rawFindings.title: Admin 'archive' takedown of a vacancy is reversible by the employer (moderation bypass)
rawFindings.rootCause: The admin moderation action and the owner's own close both write status=archived with no marker of who archived it, and the owner transition table allows archived to active.
rawFindings.impact: When an admin archives an active vacancy from the admin panel (for example a scam), the employer can republish it at once with PATCH /api/vacancies/:id/status {status:'active'}; the employer UI shows an Activate button for archived rows, and the vacancy is reindexed. Rejected content can also be reposted instantly as a new vacancy, because creating a vacancy publishes it immediately.
rawFindings.evidence: vacancies.routes.ts:240-243: allowedFrom = {active:['archived','draft'], archived:['active']} for non-admins. admin.routes.ts:285-309: moderate accepts 'archived' and sets no lock. web pages/admin/vacancies/+Page.tsx:185-188: archive button on active rows. web lib/employer/vacancies/adapter.ts:101: activate when status==='archived'. vacancies.service.ts:646: createVacancy uses status ?? 'active'.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Record a moderator takedown (for example moderationLockedAt/By), or map admin archive to 'rejected' with a reason. Block owner reactivation and resubmission of locked vacancies until an admin approves. Optionally pre-moderate new posts from companies with recent rejections.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: none (context: D-015 / ISSUE-024 defined archived-to-active for owner-closed vacancies)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium: a new optional field. Existing admin-archived rows cannot be told apart from owner-closed ones and will stay unlocked.

rawFindings.title: Company keeps its admin-granted verified badge after the owner renames it or changes logo or website
rawFindings.rootCause: PUT /api/employer/company and the logo upload update identity fields but never reset isVerified or require re-review. Verification is a one-time boolean that is not tied to the identity that was verified.
rawFindings.impact: A verified employer, or someone who took over its account, can rename the company to impersonate a known brand and swap the logo and website. It keeps the badge and still appears under verified=1 filters, so candidates trust fraudulent vacancies and hand over personal data.
rawFindings.evidence: companies.routes.ts:99-119: PUT updates name, description, website, region, industry, size and year; isVerified is untouched. 146-160: logo POST updates only logoUrl. admin.routes.ts:374-381: verify sets isVerified. vacancies.service.ts:49: isVerified is in the public card; 179: the verified filter uses isVerified.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: On a verified company, reset isVerified (or set a pending re-verification state) when name, legal name, stir, website or logo change. Alternatively store a verified snapshot and show the badge only while it matches. Notify admins and write an audit event.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low; legitimate edits trigger re-verification, which adds admin workload.

rawFindings.title: Any unverified employer account can bulk-harvest names and full resumes of all open candidates; exposure is on by default
rawFindings.rootCause: Candidate search needs only the employer role and a self-created company: no phone or company verification, no per-account quota, and paging up to 200 pages of 50. Candidates are listed by default because isOpenToWork defaults to true and saving a resume always publishes it.
rawFindings.impact: A throwaway employer (email and password, then PUT /api/employer/company) can script about 10k profiles: full name, region, headline, rating and the latest resume, including summary, desired salary, work-history descriptions and education. Candidates never explicitly opted in, which conflicts with 'candidate private data only to authorized employers'.
rawFindings.evidence: candidates.routes.ts:34: preHandler [requireAuth, requireRole('employer','admin')], no requirePhoneVerified. 37: only a primaryCompany check. 13-18: page up to 200, pageSize up to 50. 71-84: includes resume experience, education and skills. 122-160: returns names and the full resume. resume.routes.ts:140: PUT sets status 'published' unconditionally. schema.prisma:219: isOpenToWork @default(true).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Require phone verification (ideally also company verification) for /api/candidates. Make employer visibility an explicit opt-in, off by default and separate from saving a resume. Add a per-account daily quota and a lower page cap. Show a reduced card (initials, title, skills) until the candidate applies or accepts contact.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-008 (FIXED: contacts hidden); ISSUE-104 (FIXED); D-012 accepted listing for all employers
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: employers see fewer candidates. Existing opt-in defaults need a migration and a 3-language UI toggle.

rawFindings.title: Google sign-in auto-merges into an existing password account that never proved it owns the email
rawFindings.rootCause: googleLogin issues tokens for any existing user with the same email. Registration never verifies email, so an attacker-created password account looks like a genuine one.
rawFindings.impact: Pre-account takeover. An attacker registers victim@gmail.com with their own password. When the victim later signs in with Google, they end up in the attacker's account, and the attacker keeps password access to the victim's resume, applications and chats. This breaks the rule that Google must not merge unsafely.
rawFindings.evidence: auth.service.ts:37-72: registerUser leaves isEmailVerified false and has no verification flow. 218-226: googleLogin does findUnique({email}), assertNotBlocked, then issueTokens for the existing user, with no isEmailVerified check. D-011 kept the merge deliberately.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: If existing.isEmailVerified is false, do not issue a session silently. Either return 409 and require password login first, then link Google explicitly; or treat the Google login as email proof: rotate passwordHash to a random value, revoke sessions, set isEmailVerified true, write a security event and notify the user.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium: some users get an extra step. With no recovery (D-010), rotating the password needs care.

rawFindings.title: Candidate resume PDFs are served from public /uploads/ with no authorization; the URL is a permanent bearer link
rawFindings.rootCause: All uploads, including resume-*.pdf, are served by @fastify/static with no access check. Protection relies only on the random file name.
rawFindings.impact: Once an employer, or anyone they forward it to, has resumeUrl, the CV stays readable indefinitely, even after the application is rejected. There is no per-viewer check and no expiry.
rawFindings.evidence: server.ts:174: register(fastifyStatic, {root: UPLOAD_DIR, prefix: '/uploads/'}) with no preHandler. profile.routes.ts:95-121: resume saved as /uploads/resume-<32hex>.pdf. applications.routes.ts:294: resumeUrl returned to the vacancy owner. ISSUE-029 PARTIAL: random names and deletion were fixed, authorization was not.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Store resumes outside the static root and serve them through an authenticated endpoint (owner, an employer with an application on one of its own vacancies, or admin), or through short-lived signed URLs. Keep static serving only for logos and covers, and migrate existing files.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: web pages that link resumeUrl must switch to the new endpoint, and the volume layout changes.

rawFindings.title: No security audit log for authorization-sensitive actions (admin role or block changes, verification, moderation, Telegram link, phone verify)
rawFindings.rootCause: There is no audit or security-event model, and no privileged or identity-changing handler records actor, target or time.
rawFindings.impact: Misuse by a compromised admin (promoting users to admin, unblocking, verifying companies, deleting reviews) and identity changes (Telegram rebinding, phone verification, session revocation) cannot be reconstructed. Manual recovery (rule H) has no ownership history to check, and rule L events are missing.
rawFindings.evidence: schema.prisma defines models User through PushSubscription with no audit collection. admin.routes.ts:190-226: block and role change call revokeUserSessions with no record. 285-309: moderate. 374-394: verify. 443-456: review status and delete. team.routes.ts:168-216: staff role and block. telegram.service.ts:269-273 relink and 340-343 phone verify. telegram.routes.ts:38-42 unlink.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add a SecurityEvent collection (type, actorUserId, targetUserId, ip, userAgent, createdAt, metadata without secrets or message bodies) with a retention policy. Write events from these handlers and future recovery and phone flows, and add a read-only admin view.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low; make sure tokens, passwords and message contents are never written.

rawFindings.title: Job seekers can open conversations with every company and learn company owners' user IDs
rawFindings.rootCause: The seeker branch of conversations/start needs only a company slug: no active-vacancy or relationship requirement and no per-account creation limit. The conversation list returns the counterpart's raw user ID.
rawFindings.impact: One phone-verified seeker (cheap to get, see the phone finding) can open chats with and message the owners of all companies. The owner's user ID, which ISSUE-032 removed from public responses, is revealed, and /api/users/:id/summary then accepts it.
rawFindings.evidence: chat.routes.ts:342-347: company found by slug, then getOrCreateConversation(company.ownerUserId, me). 462: otherUserId is the seeker ID for an employer and employerUserId for a seeker. 603-615: summary is allowed once any conversation exists. server.ts:129-139: only a global per-IP rate limit.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Cap new conversations per account per day and optionally require an active vacancy or a prior application. Return a conversation-scoped counterpart handle instead of the raw user ID and resolve the summary by conversation ID.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low; the web messages UI probably uses otherUserId for the profile modal (not verified).

rawFindings.title: Docs and code define Telegram as a login channel (violates rule A)
rawFindings.rootCause: Telegram was treated as a third login provider. ISSUE-010 and D-039 hardened it (confirm button) instead of removing it, and every doc was written for that model.
rawFindings.impact: Future work will keep or extend a session-issuing Telegram path that the owner forbids. Users are told Telegram is a way to log in, and the bot-confirmation flow remains a phishing target.
rawFindings.evidence: Docs: DESIGN.md:219-225,243-244 (Google/Apple/Telegram row); README.md:92,137; .env.example:61; tizim-arxitekturasi.md:630; ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT.md:113; API_MAP.md:41-42; ROUTE_MAP.md:34; DECISIONS.md:425-434 (D-039). Code matches: auth.routes.ts:137-158 (/api/auth/telegram/start and /poll issue access plus refresh tokens via telegramLogin); SocialLogin.tsx:145-154 (Telegram button, rendered on login/+Page.tsx:97); telegram.service.ts:12,112-190,284-321.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Remove /api/auth/telegram/start and /poll, telegramLogin, the bot's lg-token handlers, the Telegram button and its i18n keys (withTelegram, tgWaiting, tgNotLinked). Keep deep links only for linking, verification and recovery. Update README, .env.example, the DESIGN auth section, tizim section 19, ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT section 1.2 and the maps. Add a decision that supersedes D-039; mark ISSUE-010 superseded and ISSUE-122 obsolete.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Users who only log in via Telegram lose access. Ship Telegram-based password recovery (rule B) first so they can set a password.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-010 (FIXED: hardened, not removed); ISSUE-122 (NOT FIXED); D-039

rawFindings.title: Password FAQ and 'Forgot password' point to Telegram login or support; no recovery flow exists
rawFindings.rootCause: ISSUE-012 was never implemented, so the help content was written around a Telegram-login workaround.
rawFindings.impact: Users who forget their password are locked out. The FAQ (3 locales) recommends a forbidden login channel (rule A) and contradicts the decided recovery flow (rule B).
rawFindings.evidence: messages.uz.ts:465: can't self-recover; log in via «Telegram» on /login, otherwise contact us (ru/en equivalents in the id 'password' entries). DESIGN.md:184: no password-recovery flow (answer: Telegram login or /contact). DESIGN.md:284-285: no password-change API. login/+Page.tsx:82-86: forgot link goes to /support. A grep for forgot/reset/recover finds no API route; auth.routes.ts:64-180 has only register, login, refresh, logout, me, telegram and google.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Implement the rule B flow: phone number, Telegram deep link, one-time authorization, new password, tokenVersion bump. Then rewrite the 'password' FAQ in uz/ru/en, point the login link to the new page, and update the DESIGN /support facts and profile notes. Until the flow exists, remove the Telegram-login advice from the FAQ.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low for the text change. The flow itself touches auth and needs tests.

rawFindings.title: Docs call the Telegram bot optional, but Telegram-only phone verification gates core flows
rawFindings.rootCause: The optional-services table predates the requirePhoneVerified gates and the Telegram-dependent recovery rules, and was never updated.
rawFindings.impact: A production deploy without TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN makes /api/telegram/link return 503. No one can verify a phone, so apply, post or republish vacancy, start chat and review all fail, and recovery (rule B) would be impossible. The deploy checklist would not catch it. Rule K messaging is not documented anywhere.
rawFindings.evidence: README.md:132-137 (works fully without these services; Telegram row lists only login, phone verification and notifications as off). .env.example:4-5 and :61-62 (if empty these features are off). DEPLOY.md:55-64 minimum vars and :202-210 checklist have no Telegram entry. Code: requirePhoneVerified at applications.routes.ts:43, vacancies.routes.ts:156,249, chat.routes.ts:294, reviews.routes.ts:19; telegram.routes.ts:25-32 returns 503 BOT_OFFLINE.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: List TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (and TELEGRAM_ADMIN_CHAT_ID) as required for production in DEPLOY.md and .env.example. Rewrite the README table to say a bot outage makes verification and recovery temporarily unavailable and blocks gated actions. Add a checklist step to verify a phone through the bot. Document rule K UI behaviour.
rawFindings.fixRisk: None (documentation), apart from making env validation stricter if that is also changed.

rawFindings.title: Phone and Telegram identity model violates rules E/F/G; docs describe it as acceptable
rawFindings.rootCause: phone is a plain optional field that verification overwrites without a uniqueness check. additionalPhone is free text. Telegram 'uniqueness' is implemented by silently moving the chat to the new account.
rawFindings.impact: One number can be verified on many accounts, which makes phone-based recovery ambiguous or hijackable. Linking a Telegram account to account B silently removes it from account A, which loses its recovery channel with no notice or audit. Unlinking keeps the phone marked verified.
rawFindings.evidence: schema.prisma:163 `phone String?` (no unique), :217 additionalPhone. profile.routes.ts:15-16,65-66,74 set phone/additionalPhone without verification. telegram.service.ts:339-343 sets `phone, isPhoneVerified: true` with no duplicate check; :268-273 updateMany clears telegramChatId on other accounts, then links. telegram.routes.ts:38-43 unlink keeps isPhoneVerified. Docs: CHANGELOG.md:20-22 and DB_MAP.md:139 ('uniqueness enforced in code'); API_MAP.md:111,229.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Store only verified, normalized phones, with uniqueness enforced by a unique index or a separate VerifiedPhone model; mind the MongoDB unique-null caveat. Verify the backup phone via Telegram. Refuse, rather than transfer, a Telegram identity that is already linked elsewhere. Clear verification on unlink or phone change, apply session policy and write an audit event. Document the model in DB_MAP, API_MAP and a new decision.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Existing duplicate phones need conflict resolution or backfill before a unique constraint can be added; demo seed must be updated.

rawFindings.title: D-011 keeps Google auto-merge into existing email accounts, against the Google session policy
rawFindings.rootCause: Merge-by-email was kept so password users without recovery would not be locked out. There is no email verification or ownership check.
rawFindings.impact: Pre-account takeover: an attacker registers the victim's email with a password; the victim's later Google login lands in that account, and the attacker keeps password access.
rawFindings.evidence: DECISIONS.md:117-126 (D-011: merge kept, risk PARTIAL). ISSUES.md:1039-1052 (ISSUE-042 PARTIAL). FINAL_AUDIT.md:141,401. Code: auth.service.ts:222-225 finds a user by email and, if one exists, returns issueTokens(existing...) with no isEmailVerified or provider check. schema.prisma:166 isEmailVerified defaults to false and password registration never sets it; only a new Google user gets true (auth.service.ts:241).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Refuse Google sign-in into an account not created via Google (for example 409 with guidance) unless a logged-in user explicitly links Google. Once rule B recovery ships, D-011's lockout argument no longer applies. Record a superseding decision and update ISSUE-042.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Password users who currently sign in via Google get an error and must use password or recovery; needs i18n text.

rawFindings.title: No security audit log exists and no doc defines security events (rule L)
rawFindings.rootCause: Audit logging was never in scope; auth-relevant changes are only visible in request logs, if at all.
rawFindings.impact: Phone verification, Telegram link/unlink, session invalidation, and future recovery or manual-recovery approvals cannot be audited or investigated. Rule H explicitly depends on this log.
rawFindings.evidence: Case-insensitive grep for 'AuditLog|SecurityEvent' over apps (excluding node_modules) finds nothing. The schema's 28 models (DB_MAP.md:11) have no event model. telegram.service.ts:273 and :340-343, and telegram.routes.ts:38-43, change identity or phone with no event. auth.routes.ts:116-119 revokes sessions with no event. ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT, DECISIONS and FINAL_AUDIT never mention audit logging.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add a SecurityEvent model (userId, actorId, rule-L type enum, createdAt, redacted metadata; index [userId, createdAt]) and write events at those points. Document the event list and the never-log fields (passwords, tokens, bot token, message bodies) in ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT and a decision.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low; additive collection. Ensure no secrets reach metadata.

rawFindings.title: Manual recovery (rule H) is undocumented and impossible in admin tooling, yet the FAQ promises it
rawFindings.rootCause: ISSUE-012 noted that admins cannot help, but no design followed.
rawFindings.impact: Users without password, phone and Telegram have no path. Support cannot verify ownership or reset a phone safely, which invites ad-hoc DB edits that skip session invalidation and audit.
rawFindings.evidence: admin.routes.ts:136-217: user endpoints are list, block (:190) and role (:217) only. A grep for 'recovery' finds no model or route. ISSUES.md:406: support cannot do anything manually, and there is no password setting in the admin panel. messages.uz.ts:465 promises 'we will help restore your account'. The /contact form only relays to the admin Telegram chat (DESIGN.md:189).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Design a RecoveryRequest model (status, reviewer, notes) and an admin 'verified phone reset' action that clears phone and Telegram link, bumps tokenVersion and writes an audit event, and never shows or sets passwords. Document it in DESIGN (admin section) and a decision, and align the FAQ.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Social-engineering risk if ownership verification criteria are vague; document them.

rawFindings.title: Core modules and the whole docs/ tree are untracked; DEPLOY.md's deploy-from-GitHub builds a broken HEAD

rawFindings.title: Audit tracker and final report still plan email-based or undecided password recovery
rawFindings.rootCause: Written before the owner decided on Telegram-only recovery.
rawFindings.impact: An implementer following ISSUE-012 would build email reset (forbidden by rule B) and miss rules I/J: hashed one-time tokens, replay protection, invalidating recovery tokens and auth challenges, and rate limits without easy lockout.
rawFindings.evidence: ISSUES.md:408: PasswordReset model, POST /api/auth/forgot that calls sendMail, /forgot and /reset pages; :405 cites mailer.ts as the infrastructure. DECISIONS.md:112 (D-010: Telegram recovery needs a decision). FINAL_AUDIT.md:10 (channel decision needed: email or Telegram), :391, :453 (email or Telegram channel).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add D-040 recording rules A-L. Rewrite ISSUE-012's fix and test plan: random hashed tokens, short TTL, single use, tokenVersion bump, clearing the in-memory link/login token maps, per-phone and per-IP limits, generic responses. Update FINAL_AUDIT's remaining issues and recommendation 1.
rawFindings.fixRisk: None (documentation).

rawFindings.title: Email-keyed login lockout (D-007) conflicts with rule I; the IP limit is still spoofable by default
rawFindings.rootCause: A per-email hard counter was chosen because the Railway proxy hop count was never verified.
rawFindings.impact: Anyone can block password login for a known email for 15 minutes with 10 requests, and repeat it. A recovery endpoint that copies this pattern would allow recovery denial. With TRUST_PROXY=true, a spoofed X-Forwarded-For bypasses the 10/min per-IP limit.
rawFindings.evidence: DECISIONS.md:73-82 (D-007, risk listed as lockout DoS). login-guard.ts:12-13 WINDOW_MS 15 min, MAX_FAILURES 10; :27-33 returns 429 regardless of IP. env.ts:113-119 TRUST_PROXY defaults to 'true'. .env.example:52; DEPLOY.md:70; FINAL_AUDIT.md:139.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Throttle per (email, IP or subnet) with progressive delay instead of a global per-email lock. Set TRUST_PROXY to the verified hop count. Document limits for the recovery and verification endpoints in a decision. Kept P2 (not P1) because the lock is temporary and Google login is unaffected.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Weaker brute-force protection if the IP key stays spoofable; fix TRUST_PROXY first.

rawFindings.title: Plain /start in the bot does not send a link to the ISH BOR! site (rule C)
rawFindings.rootCause: The welcome text was written for the linking and support use case; no doc specifies /start behaviour.

Invalid payloads get a generic 'link expired' reply (:262-266), consistent with rule D. README, DEPLOY and tizim section 11 (:516) do not describe bot commands.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add a WEB_ORIGIN link or inline URL button to the plain /start reply, and document bot commands and payload rules in ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT or README.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: DESIGN.md says contrast is verified, but the audit measured AA failures; reduced motion is deliberately ignored

rawFindings.title: No documented test strategy for auth or Telegram flows; bot handlers cannot be unit-tested
rawFindings.rootCause: Bot logic lives inside the long-polling module with a global fetch, and e2e runs without a bot token.
rawFindings.impact: Upcoming recovery, phone-change and linking flows (rules B, D, G, I, J) would ship without regression tests for replay, expiry, wrong chat, rate limits and session invalidation.

DEPLOY.md:167-179 e2e scope has no phone verification or linking. telegram.service.ts:156,243,284: handleLoginStart, handleStart and handleCallbackQuery are module-private.

rawFindings.title: Security gaps FINAL_AUDIT lists as open are still open in code

Token: lib/auth/session.ts:99-108 reads and writes localStorage (ISSUE-083). Resume: profile.routes.ts:109 stores the PDF via saveUpload('resume-'); server.ts:174 serves /uploads/ without auth, with PDF exempt from sandbox per :143-169 (ISSUE-029).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add a CSP (hash the inline theme script) on Vercel and in the self-hosted server. Serve resumes through an authenticated endpoint that checks the applicant-employer relation. Reconsider in-memory token storage.

rawFindings.title: Vacancy and company detail pages inherit the list page +Head: duplicate, conflicting description/og:title/og:type/canonical
rawFindings.rootCause: Vike inheritance: getInheritanceRoot strips only 'pages'/'renderer', so pages/vacancies/+Head.tsx (root /vacancies) applies to /vacancies/@slug, and companies/+Head.tsx applies to /companies/@slug. vike-react Head is cumulative, so detail Head, list Head and HeadDefault all render. The same problem was fixed for articles by moving to articles/index/ (articles/index/+data.ts:11-12), but vacancies and companies were never moved. employer/+Head.tsx is likewise inherited by the private employer/* pages.
rawFindings.impact: The most valuable indexable pages ship two meta descriptions (the second is the generic 'all vacancies'/'companies catalogue' text), two og:title, og:type article/profile plus website, and duplicate og:url and canonical tags. Search snippets and social previews become ambiguous and crawler-dependent. Private employer pages also get indexable landing meta and a canonical, though noindex still wins.
rawFindings.evidence: Built entry dist/server/entries/src_pages_vacancies_-slug.mjs:2281-2308 lists Head sources in order: vacancies/@slug/+Head.tsx, vacancies/+Head.tsx, HeadDefault.tsx. src_pages_companies_-slug.mjs:1427-1454 shows the same for companies. vacancies/+Head.tsx:31 `<Seo title={meta.title} description={meta.description} canonical={canonical} />`; companies/+Head.tsx:8. vike filesystemRouting.js:36-45 (inheritance root), 73 (most specific first).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Move vacancies/{+Page,+Head,+data,+title} to pages/vacancies/index/ and companies/* to pages/companies/index/, as was done for articles. Move employer/+Head.tsx and the landing page to employer/index/ as well. Afterwards, check the built entries list exactly one page-level Head plus HeadDefault.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: routes are unchanged (index/ is ignored by routing); verify with a build that only one page Head plus HeadDefault is attached.

rawFindings.title: Detail pages return HTTP 200 + noindex when the API fails (no 503)
rawFindings.rootCause: Any ApiError from fetchVacancyDetail becomes `vacancy: null`: a network error, 8s timeout or 5xx. The page renders with 200 and +Head adds noindex. Companies and articles follow the same pattern. D-027 added only the timeout and deliberately kept 200 + noindex.
rawFindings.impact: A crawl during a brief API outage or slowdown makes Google drop active vacancy, company or article pages from the index; recrawl and reindexing take days. A 503 (optionally with Retry-After) would make the crawler retry without deindexing. With tens of thousands of vacancy URLs, one outage window can deindex many.
rawFindings.evidence: vacancies/@slug/+data.ts:17 `if (error instanceof ApiError) return { vacancy: null, failed: true };` +Head.tsx:34-35 `if (!vacancy) return <Seo ... noindex />`. companies/@slug/+data.ts:17 and +Head.tsx:23-24. articles/@slug/+data.ts:19 and +Head.tsx:27-28. api.ts:382-384: any non-404 non-ok status throws ApiError. DECISIONS.md D-027 'detail sahifada 503 qilinmadi'.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: During SSR only (typeof window === 'undefined'), throw render(503, VACANCY_UNAVAILABLE) (and COMPANY_/ARTICLE_UNAVAILABLE) on ApiError. _error then shows the existing retry state without noindex. Keep the null + retry behaviour for client-side navigation. Treat an API 404 as 404, and 5xx or timeout as 503.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: the _error page must render the retry UI for the new abortReasons; client navigation behaviour must stay unchanged.

rawFindings.title: List/home/salaries SSR returns 200 indexable error state when the API is down
rawFindings.rootCause: List hooks catch API failures as null and render an error or retry component with HTTP 200. The Head stays indexable with the normal canonical; unlike the detail pages, there isn't even a noindex. ISSUE-016 fixed the UX (error instead of zeros) but not the HTTP status.
rawFindings.impact: During an outage Googlebot sees /vacancies, /salaries and the home page as 200 pages whose main content is 'could not load'. This risks soft-404 classification and a cached thin snippet for the site's hub pages, which carry most internal linking to vacancy pages.
rawFindings.evidence: vacancies/+data.ts:16 `fetchVacancyPage(...).catch((): VacancyPage | null => null)`; vacancies/+Page.tsx:167-168 `page === null ? <VacancyErrorState/>`; vacancies/+Head.tsx:31 has no noindex. salaries/+data.ts:19 and +Page.tsx:93-94 SalaryErrorState. index/+Page.tsx:214,233 `vacancies === null`/`companies === null`. companies/+data.ts:20 `first: null`.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: During SSR, when the primary dataset fails (vacancies page, salary stats, companies first page), throw render(503) with a list-specific abortReason, or at least set the HTTP status to 503 while keeping the retry UI. Leave secondary blocks (facets, featured) as soft failures. Leave client navigation unchanged.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: needs an _error branch per list page or a shared 'service unavailable' state.

rawFindings.title: Canonical drops all query params: sitemap salary URLs contradict canonical, pagination canonical to page 1, ?q= indexable
rawFindings.rootCause: useHead builds canonical and alternates from the logical pathname only. The sitemap still publishes /salaries?category=X and /salaries?region=Y, whose canonical is /salaries. /vacancies?page=N points to page 1. /vacancies?q=<anything> puts user-supplied text into <title> and description with no noindex (articles does add noindex for q).
rawFindings.impact: The hundreds of per-category and per-region salary URLs in the sitemap are reported as 'alternate page with proper canonical' and never rank. Deep paginated vacancies are not discoverable through pagination. Arbitrary ?q= URLs give crawlers attacker-chosen titles on the site's domain, plus duplicate-canonical noise.
rawFindings.evidence: head.ts:25 `canonical: ${SITE_ORIGIN}${localizeHref(logical, locale)}`. seo.routes.ts:89-92 `/salaries?category=${c.slug}`, `/salaries?region=${r.slug}`. salaries/+Head.tsx:12 `canonical={canonical}`. vacancies/+Head.tsx:12-13,31 (no noindex). vacancies/+title.ts:8. messages.uz.ts:19-21 `${q} bo'yicha vakansiyalar | ISH BOR!`. articles/index/+Head.tsx:28 noindex on q. D-031 deferred.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add a whitelist option to useHead, e.g. canonicalParams: salaries keeps category and region (sorted); vacancies/companies/articles keep page>1. Apply the same params to the hreflang alternates. Add noindex to /vacancies and /companies when q or saved=1 is present. Otherwise, remove the salary query URLs from sitemap-static. Either way, sitemap and canonical must agree.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: meta-only; param order must match the sitemap URLs exactly.

rawFindings.title: JobPosting validThrough is effectively dead: Vacancy.expiresAt is never written or enforced by the API
rawFindings.rootCause: The schema has a real nullable Vacancy.expiresAt and the API selects it. No create, update or publish path sets it, and no job closes vacancies past it; the only writer is demo-seed (publishedAt + 30 days). Production JobPostings therefore never carry validThrough, and vacancies stay active and in the sitemap indefinitely. Demo data emits past validThrough dates on vacancies that are still active.
rawFindings.impact: Google Jobs receives postings with no expiry. Stale 'active' vacancies stay in structured data and sitemap-vacancy.xml forever, which lowers quality signals. In demo/staging, active pages declare themselves expired. Per product rules the expiry must not be invented, so this needs a product decision.
rawFindings.evidence: schema.prisma:429 `expiresAt DateTime? @map("expires_at")`. grep in apps/api/src: vacancy expiresAt appears only in vacancies.service.ts:92 (select); it is not in vacancies.routes.ts create/update schemas. demo-seed.ts:1714 `expiresAt: published ? new Date(publishedAt + 30*DAY) : null`. seo.routes.ts:99-104 lists all status active. +Head.tsx:59 `...(vacancy.expiresAt ? { validThrough } : {})`. Currency and sameAs parts of ISSUE-072 are fixed.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Product decision first. Either (a) set expiresAt on publish (e.g. a fixed duration or an employer-chosen date), with a sweep that moves expired vacancies to closed and excludes them from the sitemap and public detail; or (b) drop expiresAt from demo-seed so no fabricated past dates reach JSON-LD. Never synthesize validThrough in the web layer.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: auto-closing vacancies changes the employer workflow and notifications; needs product sign-off.

rawFindings.title: og:image points to /api/og/... on the API host, whose own robots.txt disallows /api
rawFindings.rootCause: seoRoutes and ogRoutes are registered on the same Fastify app, so API_URL/robots.txt returns 'Disallow: /api'. The vacancy og:image is `${API_URL}/api/og/vacancy/:slug`, which that robots.txt disallows.
rawFindings.impact: Robots-respecting preview crawlers skip the dynamic share image: Twitterbot documents that blocked images are not shown, and LinkedIn behaves similarly. Vacancy shares then fall back to no image, or to the logo that HeadDefault emits as a second og:image. It is an inference whether Telegram's preview bot honours robots.txt.
rawFindings.evidence: server.ts:238-239 `app.register(seoRoutes); app.register(ogRoutes);`. seo.routes.ts:46 `const lines = ["User-agent: *", "Disallow: /api"]`. og.routes.ts:7 `app.get("/api/og/vacancy/:slug"`. vacancies/@slug/+Head.tsx:121 `content={`${API_URL}/api/og/vacancy/${vacancy.slug}`}`. HeadDefault.tsx:49 global og:image logo.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: On the API host, serve a robots.txt that allows /api/og/ and /uploads/ (e.g. `Allow: /api/og/` before `Disallow: /api`), or detect the API host and skip Disallow: /api there. Alternatively, move the OG endpoint to a non-/api path such as /og/vacancy/:slug.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: OG image fonts are Latin-only: Cyrillic vacancy titles/company names render without glyphs
rawFindings.rootCause: Satori receives only space-grotesk-latin-700 and inter-latin-400/600, and no loadAdditionalAsset fallback. Space Grotesk ships no Cyrillic subset at all. Russian-language titles, company names and region names cannot be shaped.
rawFindings.impact: Uzbekistan has many Russian-language vacancies. For them the share image (Telegram, social) shows a blank or tofu title and company line, which looks broken and lowers click-through. The exact rendering of missing glyphs is an inference about satori behaviour.
rawFindings.evidence: og.service.ts:78-80 loads `space-grotesk-latin-700-normal.woff`, `inter-latin-400-normal.woff`, `inter-latin-600-normal.woff`. og.service.ts:141,169 title uses fontFamily 'Space Grotesk'. node_modules/@fontsource/inter/files contains inter-cyrillic-400/600-normal.woff; @fontsource/space-grotesk has 0 cyrillic files.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Register the inter-cyrillic 400/600 (and latin-ext) files as additional 'Inter' font entries. Use Inter bold (or another Cyrillic-capable display font) for the title when it contains Cyrillic, or list fallback fonts in fontFamily. Add a test rendering a Cyrillic title.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: slightly larger font memory.

rawFindings.title: Untranslated vacancy/company/article content published as ru/en hreflang alternates; Article inLanguage is false
rawFindings.rootCause: Every public URL is exposed under /, /ru and /en, declared as hreflang alternates in the sitemap and in HeadDefault. Only the UI template is translated; employer-written vacancy text, company profiles and articles exist in one language (Article has no locale field). The article JSON-LD sets inLanguage from the URL locale, not from the content.
rawFindings.impact: Tripled URL inventory (tens of thousands of vacancies x3) of near-duplicate pages. Google's multilingual guidance warns that translating only boilerplate on UGC pages produces duplicate results and a poor experience. It also wastes crawl budget and triples sitemap size. /ru/articles/x claims inLanguage 'ru' for Uzbek text. Severity is partly inference from Google guidance.
rawFindings.evidence: seo.routes.ts:153-157 emits alternates for each of LOCALES plus x-default for every vacancy, company and article path. HeadDefault.tsx:52-55 alternates on every page. schema.prisma:649-677 Article has no locale or language field. articles/@slug/+Head.tsx:43 `inLanguage: locale`. articles/@slug/+data.ts:13-27 never checks locale.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Store the content language (Article.locale; optionally a detected language for vacancies). Emit hreflang and sitemap alternates only for the primary locale, or canonicalize /ru and /en detail URLs to the content-language URL. Set Article inLanguage from the stored field. Keep localized alternates for truly translated static and hub pages.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: canonical changes on ru/en detail pages shift existing indexed URLs; roll out with monitoring.

rawFindings.title: Sitemaps: no origin cache, 50k-row loads per request, Mongo relation filters, silent 50k cap
rawFindings.rootCause: Each hit queries the DB directly: up to 50k vacancies and 50k companies, the latter filtered with `owner: {isBlocked}` and `vacancies: {some}` relation filters, which Prisma on MongoDB runs as $lookup aggregations. Every hit builds ~20MB+ of XML strings with 4 alternates per URL. Nothing is cached in-process. The API host is publicly reachable, bypassing Vercel's s-maxage cache, and self-hosted has no cache. There is no chunking beyond 50k.
rawFindings.impact: At the target scale (10k companies, tens of thousands of vacancies), repeated sitemap fetches by bots or anyone hitting the API domain cause heavy DB aggregation and memory spikes on the single API instance. Past 50k active vacancies, URLs are dropped silently.
rawFindings.evidence: seo.routes.ts:99-104 `findMany({ where: { status: "active" }, ... take: 50000 })`. seo.routes.ts:114-125 company filters `NOT: { owner: { isBlocked: true } }`, `vacancies: { some: { status: "active" } }`. seo.routes.ts:150-164 buildUrlSet string building. api/seo.js:50 edge cache on Vercel only. ISSUE-056 is PARTIAL: filters added, cache and chunking not done.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add an in-memory TTL cache (e.g. 30-60 min) per sitemap and set Cache-Control on the API response. Split into chunked sitemaps (e.g. 10k per file via publishedAt/id cursor) listed in the index. Precompute a company 'hasActiveVacancies' flag, or query active vacancy companyIds first and filter by id, instead of relation filters.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium: chunked file names must be added to the vercel.json rewrites (the regex in api/seo.js already allows sitemap-[a-z]+ only; digits would need a change).

rawFindings.title: Site origin for canonical/hreflang/sitemap silently falls back to localhost and comes from two env sources
rawFindings.rootCause: SITE_ORIGIN = VITE_SITE_URL || 'http://localhost:3001', with no build-time guard in vite.config.ts. The API's WEB_ORIGIN defaults to 'http://localhost:5173' and the production superRefine does not require it. Sitemap and robots URLs come from WEB_ORIGIN while canonicals come from VITE_SITE_URL, and nothing checks that they match.
rawFindings.impact: One missed or mismatched env var ships canonical, hreflang, og:url and JSON-LD URLs pointing at localhost, or a sitemap on a different host (e.g. *.vercel.app vs the custom domain) from the canonicals. Google then ignores the sitemap or deindexes the real site. This is a production SEO blocker triggered by misconfiguration.
rawFindings.evidence: config.ts:50-52 `(import.meta.env.VITE_SITE_URL as string | undefined) || "http://localhost:3001"`. vite.config.ts has no SITE_URL check (grep empty). env.ts:47 `WEB_ORIGIN: z.string().default("http://localhost:5173")`; env.ts:138-160 production checks cover only JWT secrets. seo.routes.ts:14 `const PUBLIC_ORIGIN = env.WEB_ORIGIN`. DEPLOY.md:63,128,135 documents both separately.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Fail the web production build when VITE_SITE_URL is missing or localhost. In env.ts superRefine for production, require WEB_ORIGIN to be https and non-localhost. Add a dedicated PUBLIC_SITE_URL, or document and verify that WEB_ORIGIN === VITE_SITE_URL (e.g. a startup log or a deploy smoke test comparing the sitemap host to the canonical host).
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: intentionally blocks misconfigured deploys.

rawFindings.title: robots.txt/sitemap delivery fragile: absent on self-hosted, API-coupled on Vercel (no timeout, 5xx robots, wrong body)
rawFindings.rootCause: The self-hosted server (server/index.mjs) has no /robots.txt or /sitemap*.xml route and public/ has no robots.txt, so both fall through to the Vike 404 page. On Vercel, seo.js proxies to the API with no timeout. On a fetch error it returns 502 with a robots body, for sitemap paths too. With API_URL unset it answers /sitemap.xml with 200 and robots text.
rawFindings.impact: Self-hosted deploys have no sitemap discovery and no robots rules. On Vercel, an API outage turns robots.txt into a 5xx, which Google treats as disallow-all for a period (documented Google behaviour), pausing crawling of the whole site. A slow API can hang the function until the platform timeout.
rawFindings.evidence: server/index.mjs:99-118 only has the `app.get("/*")` SSR handler. public/ listing contains no robots.txt. seo.js:39-41 `await fetch(`${API_URL}${pathname}`, { headers })` with no signal. seo.js:52-56 returns 502 with the robots body. seo.js:30-35 returns 200 with the robots body for any allowed path when API_URL is missing.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Serve a static robots.txt from the web app, since it is not data-dependent, so it never depends on API health. Proxy only sitemaps, with AbortSignal.timeout(~8s) and a 503 plus Retry-After and an XML-appropriate content type on failure. Add the same sitemap proxy to server/index.mjs, or document that self-hosted is unsupported for SEO.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: _error head: 500 errors and article 404s get generic 'page not found' meta; hreflang emitted on error pages
rawFindings.rootCause: +Head and +title branch only on VACANCY_NOT_FOUND and COMPANY_NOT_FOUND. They never check is404 or ARTICLE_NOT_FOUND, although +Page.tsx does. HeadDefault always emits the 3 locale alternates and x-default, including on 404/500 pages.
rawFindings.impact: 500 responses carry the title and description 'Sahifa topilmadi'. Article 404s get the generic title. Error URLs emit hreflang clusters, which produce Search Console hreflang noise. Status codes themselves are correct.
rawFindings.evidence: _error/+Head.tsx:12-20 (no is404 / ARTICLE_NOT_FOUND). _error/+title.ts:9-11 `return t.meta.notFound.title`. _error/+Page.tsx:19,39-42 has both the ARTICLE_NOT_FOUND and 500 branches. HeadDefault.tsx:52-55 unconditional alternates.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add ARTICLE_NOT_FOUND and `is404 === false` (t.error.title500) branches to +Head and +title. In HeadDefault, skip alternates and x-default when pageContext.is404 !== undefined (the error page).
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: robots.txt still both Disallows and noindexes account pages; no rules for parameter crawl traps
rawFindings.rootCause: PRIVATE_PATHS (/login, /signup, /profile, /favorites...) are Disallowed while the same pages carry noindex. Crawlers blocked by robots.txt cannot see the noindex. Unbounded filter combinations on /vacancies and /companies (category x region x experience x page x q, saved=1) are not restricted.
rawFindings.impact: Externally linked account URLs can show as 'Indexed, though blocked by robots.txt'. Facet and pagination permutations burn crawl budget on a large catalogue. Low impact.
rawFindings.evidence: seo.routes.ts:28-41 PRIVATE_PATHS, 47-51 Disallow in 3 locales. login/+Head.tsx:12 and signup/+Head.tsx:12 noindex. There is no `Disallow: /*?*saved=` or similar. ISSUE-092 is marked FIXED (dead paths removed), but the Disallow + noindex duality remains.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Pick one mechanism for account pages: remove them from Disallow and rely on noindex, keeping Disallow for /admin and /api. Add targeted rules such as `Disallow: /*?*saved=`, and rely on the canonical/noindex fix for q and facet combinations.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: /pricing uses a temporary 302 although the platform is permanently free; dead indexable Head/data remain
rawFindings.rootCause: The guard comment treats monetization as 'later' and uses 302. Product rules make free the final state, with pricing outside core UX. pricing/+Head.tsx (indexable) and +data.ts (fetchPlans) are unreachable leftovers.
rawFindings.impact: Google keeps /pricing (and /ru, /en variants) as the indexed URL for a 302 instead of consolidating to /employer. It also leaves dead monetization code on a public route. Minor.
rawFindings.evidence: pricing/+guard.ts:7-11 `throw redirect(localizeHref("/employer", ...), 302)`. pricing/+Head.tsx:8 has no noindex. pricing/+data.ts:5 `fetchPlans()`. seo.routes.ts:72-81 no longer lists /pricing.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Switch to a 301 (or 410 if the page is being retired). Remove pricing/+Head.tsx and +data.ts, or keep them behind the billing flag only.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: 301s are cached by browsers; acceptable given the final product rule.

rawFindings.title: JobPosting invents FULL_TIME for legacy 'remote' employmentType and always claims directApply
rawFindings.rootCause: EMPLOYMENT_SCHEMA maps the legacy enum value remote (a workplace, not an employment type) to FULL_TIME, which the data does not state. directApply: true is hard-coded, but applying requires signing in and passing the phone-verification gate.
rawFindings.impact: Google Jobs can show 'Full-time' for vacancies whose employment type is unknown, contrary to the 'do not invent data' rule. directApply may be judged inaccurate, a quality or eligibility risk. Low impact.
rawFindings.evidence: +Head.tsx:10-15 `remote: "FULL_TIME"`. +Head.tsx:60 employmentType mapping. +Head.tsx:65 `directApply: true`. schema.prisma:64-69 enum EmploymentType includes remote. ApplyCard.tsx:142 PhoneGateNotice on apply error. VacancyDetailView.tsx:48 login link for guests.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Omit employmentType when employment is 'remote' (location is already covered by workplaceType and TELECOMMUTE). Set directApply only if the apply flow genuinely completes on the page, or drop the property.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: OG image endpoint re-renders satori+resvg on every request with no server-side cache
rawFindings.rootCause: Each GET does a DB lookup plus a full SVG layout and PNG rasterization. Only a browser/CDN Cache-Control max-age=3600 is set, and Railway has no CDN in front by default. Only the global per-IP rate limit applies.
rawFindings.impact: Social crawlers, link unfurls in large Telegram groups and scrapers iterating slugs consume API CPU on the single instance that also serves core traffic. Minor at 10k users, but avoidable.
rawFindings.evidence: og.routes.ts:10-43 findUnique then `await renderVacancyOgImage(...)` on every request. og.routes.ts:42 `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`. server.ts:129-131 global rateLimit only.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add a small LRU/TTL cache keyed by slug and the vacancy's updatedAt (or a title/salary hash). Optionally a stricter per-route rate limit, or put the endpoint behind a CDN.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Site copy in all 3 locales still offers Telegram login and sends password recovery to support/Telegram login
rawFindings.rootCause: The dictionaries were written for the old auth model: Telegram as a login provider, and no self-service recovery. The 'Forgot password?' link points to /support. None of the owner's new flows (rules A/B/H/K) have keys: phone entry, waiting for the Telegram deep link, verification temporarily unavailable, new password, manual recovery request.
rawFindings.impact: UZ, RU and EN users are told to 'Sign in with Telegram' (forbidden by rule A) and to contact support for a forgotten password, instead of the Telegram recovery flow (rule B). The underlying feature is an auth-dimension finding; this entry covers the copy and the missing keys that must change with it in all three dictionaries.
rawFindings.evidence: messages.en.ts:357-359 withTelegram 'Sign in with Telegram', tgWaiting, tgNotLinked 'Sign in with email first and link Telegram'. en:458-459 FAQ: 'Resetting a password on the site yourself isn't available yet... sign in with Telegram'. The same FAQ text is in messages.uz.ts:465 and messages.ru.ts:467. uz/en:2759 passwordHint says contact support. login/+Page.tsx:83 href={l('/support')} for t.login.forgot. SocialLogin.tsx:90,145-150 renders the Telegram button. The bot says 'Telegram orqali kirish' at telegram.service.ts:168,177.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: When auth implements rules A/B/H/K, remove the login.withTelegram/tgWaiting/tgNotLinked/tgExpired keys and the Telegram button. Add a typed recovery.* section in uz/ru/en: phone step, open-bot step, waiting, expired/invalid link, bot unavailable (rule K), new password, success with 'all sessions signed out', manual recovery request form. Rewrite the FAQ 'password' entry and the AccountSettings passwordHint. Point 'Forgot password?' to the recovery page.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: none (new auth product rules). ISSUE-010 covered the Telegram login confirmation flow

rawFindings.title: Backend notifications (in-app, bell, push, Telegram, email) are stored and sent as Uzbek text for every user
rawFindings.rootCause: Callers build final Uzbek strings for title, body, CTA and email HTML, and notify() saves them as-is. The Notification row has no type-specific params the client could translate. User has no locale field (schema grep finds none), so push, Telegram and email cannot pick a language. The email template footer is also fixed Uzbek.
rawFindings.impact: A RU/EN job seeker sees 'Ariza holati o'zgardi' / '«X» bo'yicha: Rad etildi ❌' in the notification page and bell, and gets the same text in push, Telegram and email. Alert digests say '"name" bo'yicha 3 ta yangi vakansiya'. At 10K users with hundreds of thousands of notifications, these legacy rows cannot be re-translated later.
rawFindings.evidence: applications.routes.ts:32-37 STATUS_UZ; :108-109 'Yangi ariza'; :357-366 status title, body and ctaLabel 'Arizalarimni ko'rish'. alerts.service.ts:213,220,224-225. admin.routes.ts:318-319, 388-389. notifications.service.ts:104-105 saves title/body; 133-135 Telegram; 143-145 push; 178-182 subject = title, ctaLabel 'Saytda ochish'. mailer.ts:108-109 Uzbek footer. chat.routes.ts:87 'Yangi xabar keldi'. Web shows them raw: NotificationCard.tsx:45-46, NotificationBell.tsx:142; sw.js:16.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Save a structured payload for each type: vacancyTitle, status, count, searchName, reason. Render in-app text on the client from t.notificationsPage templates, falling back to title/body for legacy rows. Add User.locale, set from the URL locale at login or on locale switch. Build push, Telegram and email text from a small server-side uz/ru/en dictionary, and add the locale prefix to links (ISSUE-103). Keep user content (vacancy titles, search names) untranslated.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-073 (R142, NOT FIXED); ISSUE-103 (links without locale prefix, NOT FIXED)

rawFindings.title: Raw server error text (Uzbek AppError, English zod defaults) shown directly in RU/EN UI in many components
rawFindings.rootCause: The API returns one pre-rendered message: Uzbek AppError text, or `${field}: ${issue.message}` with zod's English default. Most web catch blocks print err.message in every locale. errorText (useNotice.ts:30), which limits server text to uz, is used in only some places. Many schemas have no custom messages, and AuthForm's password field has no minLength.
rawFindings.impact: A RU/EN user with a wrong password sees 'Email yoki parol noto'g'ri'. A 7-character signup password shows 'password: String must contain at least 8 character(s)' in all 3 locales. The EN vacancy form shows 'Category — Kategoriyani tanlang'. Rate-limit 429 text is Uzbek everywhere. The UI mixes languages and exposes technical field names.
rawFindings.evidence: server.ts:183-187 ZodError handler; :133-137 Uzbek 429. auth.routes.ts:17-18 email()/min(8) with no message. vacancies.routes.ts:54-55 no message; 59,61 Uzbek messages. auth.service.ts:40,98,104. Raw display: login/+Page.tsx:36, signup/+Page.tsx:52, SocialLogin.tsx:60,114, TelegramConnect.tsx:85, EmployerCompanyForm.tsx:48,61,95, RatingDialog.tsx:58, SaveSearchButton.tsx:67, profile/ui.tsx:333, ResumeFile.tsx:40, EmployerApplicationsView.tsx:171-172, VacancyForm.tsx:139-143,227. grep: no minLength in AuthForm.tsx.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Use the `error` codes the API already returns. Add specific codes (INVALID_CREDENTIALS, EMAIL_TAKEN, RATE_LIMITED, BOT_OFFLINE, PHONE_NOT_VERIFIED...) and structured {field, rule, min} for VALIDATION_ERROR. Map them in the web to t.errors.* with one shared helper that replaces raw err.message everywhere, falling back to a generic localized message. Add minLength={8} to the signup password field.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-073 (R141, R144, R224, NOT FIXED; deferred in D-031)

rawFindings.title: Region and category names shown in Uzbek on RU/EN pages where the API omits the slug or the web drops it
rawFindings.rootCause: Localization depends on slug lookups (regionName(), CATEGORY_NAMES). Several API responses return only region.name: profile, candidates, chat. Several web mappers keep only the name (apiExtra mapVacancyRow, lib/api mapCompany). The salaries page renders API names directly even though slugs are present.
rawFindings.impact: RU/EN users see 'Farg'ona', 'Toshkent viloyati', 'Qoraqalpog'iston' and 'Qurilish, ko'chmas mulk' on the home cards, the /companies catalog, profile header and resume preview, the employer candidates list, chat details, saved jobs, salary tables, region select and insights, and JSON-LD. Other vacancy cards on the same pages are localized, so the site is inconsistent.
rawFindings.evidence: components/VacancyCard.tsx:49 and CompanyCard.tsx:29 (from apiExtra.ts:94-101, which reads name only). companies/CompanyCard.tsx:96-101 via lib/api.ts:265, although companies.list.ts:113 returns the slug. ProfileHeader.tsx:77 and ResumePreview.tsx:32 (profile.routes.ts:39 has no slug). candidates/+Page.tsx:233,376 (candidates.routes.ts:135). ConversationDetails.tsx:68,140,217 (chat.routes.ts:480,494,654). SalarySearch.tsx:133 label r.name; SelectedProfession.tsx:64,93; SalaryTables.tsx:106; SalaryInsights.tsx:50,55 (salary.stats.ts:156 has slug). Localized contrast: vacancies/VacancyCard.tsx:36.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Return region {slug,name} and category {slug,name} from the profile, candidates and chat endpoints. Keep slugs in mapVacancyRow and mapCompany. Render every region and category label through regionName(locale, slug, name) and categoryLabel(). In salaries, look up names by slug. Optionally pass the localized name into JSON-LD addressLocality.

rawFindings.title: Telegram bot and verification-unavailable messages are Uzbek-only; the bot has no way to know the user's locale
rawFindings.rootCause: Every bot reply and keyboard label is a hard-coded Uzbek literal. The deep-link token entry stores only {userId, expiresAt}, so the site's locale never reaches the bot, and Telegram's from.language_code is ignored. The 503 BOT_OFFLINE text is Uzbek and the web prints it raw.
rawFindings.impact: Phone verification is required to apply, post vacancies and review. A RU/EN user who starts it gets Uzbek instructions and a 'Telefon raqamni ulashish' button. When the bot is down they see 'Telegram bot hozircha ishga tushmagan' (rule K requires a clear 'temporarily unavailable' message). The new recovery and phone-change flows (rules B-G) will reuse this bot and inherit the gap.
rawFindings.evidence: telegram.service.ts:90 linkTokens Map<string,{userId,expiresAt}>; 236 contact button label; 253-258 plain /start welcome (rule C text); 264 'Havola eskirgan'; 275-280; 329, 335, 345-347 phone verified. telegram.routes.ts:27-31 503 BOT_OFFLINE Uzbek message. TelegramConnect.tsx:85 setError(err.message). auth-guard.ts:98-102 PHONE_NOT_VERIFIED Uzbek message.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Store the locale server-side with the token entry (taken from the request's page locale, never put in the payload). Fall back to msg.from.language_code, then uz. Move bot strings into a small uz/ru/en dictionary shared with the upcoming recovery flow. On the web, map BOT_OFFLINE and PHONE_NOT_VERIFIED codes to localized t.* text instead of err.message.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: none (related to ISSUE-073 generic backend text)

rawFindings.title: Numbers formatted as ru-RU in every locale (EN shows '1 207', '12 000 000 UZS')
rawFindings.rootCause: One module-level Intl.NumberFormat('ru-RU') serves every locale: formatNumber and formatSalary. grp() in types.ts is also used 16 times in messages.en.ts. The lib/salaries/format.ts comment shows ru-RU was chosen to avoid uz ICU hydration mismatches, but it was applied to EN too.
rawFindings.impact: English pages show space-grouped numbers ('1 207 jobs', '5 000 000 – 8 000 000 UZS') where readers expect '1,207'. Some EN copy hard-codes commas, so formats are inconsistent. Cosmetic only.
rawFindings.evidence: lib/format.ts:3,6,17; types.ts:2397 grp = Intl.NumberFormat('ru-RU'); CountUp.tsx:39; employer/candidates/+Page.tsx:416; api common/format.ts:3 (OG). lib/salaries/format.ts:7-13 already switches to en-US for en decimals.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Pass the locale to formatNumber, formatSalary and grp. Use en-US for en and keep ru-RU for uz/ru (both are ICU-stable, so no hydration mismatch). Replace the inline Intl calls in CountUp and the candidates page.

rawFindings.title: Date and time formatting inconsistent: toLocaleDateString() without locale; chat uses browser timezone and en-GB
rawFindings.rootCause: Ad-hoc Date calls skip the shared formatDate(iso, locale), which fixes Asia/Tashkent and en-US. The chat helpers use local-time day boundaries and a different EN tag.
rawFindings.impact: 'Last checked' on /alerts and admin table dates follow the browser's OS language, not the page locale. A RU page can show '9/15/2026'. Chat day separators and clock can disagree with dates elsewhere for users outside UTC+5. Minor.
rawFindings.evidence: alerts/+Page.tsx:134; admin/users/+Page.tsx:142; admin/reviews/+Page.tsx:135; admin/companies/+Page.tsx:125; admin/payments/+Page.tsx:138 all call toLocaleDateString() with no args. lib/messages/format.ts:6 TIME_TAG en-GB, :9-21 local startOfDay/dayKey, :25 formatClock with no timeZone. lib/format.ts:30-32 DATE_TAG en-US, TIME_ZONE Asia/Tashkent.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Use formatDate(iso, locale) in the alerts and admin pages. Pick one time policy for chat: either Asia/Tashkent in formatClock/dayKey/formatDayLabel, or document browser-local time. Unify the EN tag.

rawFindings.title: RU/EN count strings ignore plural forms ('1 кандидатов', '1 откликов', '1 candidates')
rawFindings.rootCause: Some count templates interpolate n into a fixed genitive-plural (RU) or plural (EN) noun. The ruPlural helper exists and is used elsewhere but was not applied here.
rawFindings.impact: The employer candidates header shows '1 кандидатов' / '1 candidates'. The employer vacancy rows show '1 откликов', '3 откликов' / '1 applications'. This looks unpolished to RU/EN employers.
rawFindings.evidence: messages.ru.ts:79 resultsCount `${n} кандидатов` (used at employer/candidates/+Page.tsx:197); ru:686 applicationsCount `${n} откликов` (used at VacancyRow.tsx:107,112); ru:864 favorites.count `${n} вакансий`; ru:179 companies.subtitle. messages.en.ts:78 `${n} candidates`, en:678 `${n} applications`, en:856 `${n} jobs`. The helper is at types.ts:2400 (ruPlural).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Use ruPlural(n, ...) in the RU templates and n === 1 ? singular : plural in EN. Add a quick grep/lint for `(n) => \`${n} ` in the ru/en files.

rawFindings.title: Hardcoded Uzbek/English UI fallbacks, and 'Xatolik' used as a logic sentinel
rawFindings.rootCause: Fallback strings are written inline instead of taken from t.*. ApiError defaults to the Uzbek word 'Xatolik', and components compare err.message to that literal to decide whether a server message is 'known'.
rawFindings.impact: On a network error, RU/EN users see 'Xatolik yuz berdi'. A review with no author name shows 'Nomzod' on RU/EN vacancy pages. Signup placeholders 'Aziz'/'Aliyev' and the Footer aria-label 'Footer' are the same in every locale. Changing the sentinel word would silently change error handling.
rawFindings.evidence: SocialLogin.tsx:60,114 and EmployerCompanyForm.tsx:48,61,95 'Xatolik yuz berdi'. lib/api.ts:284 authorName fallback 'Nomzod'. lib/api.ts:100,127 default messages 'Kutilmagan xatolik yuz berdi'/'Xatolik'. Sentinel checks: ResumeFile.tsx:40, profile/ui.tsx:333, EmployerApplicationsView.tsx:171. signup/+Page.tsx:92,100,122 placeholders. Footer.tsx:140 aria-label='Footer'.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Replace the inline fallbacks with t.* keys: errors.generic, reviews.anonymous, signup.firstNamePlaceholder, footer.navLabel. Give ApiError an explicit `fromServer` flag or use the code instead of comparing message text.

rawFindings.title: Vacancy OG share image is always rendered in Uzbek, including for /ru and /en pages
rawFindings.rootCause: formatSalaryLabel and the OG route hard-code Uzbek currency, suffixes, the hidden-salary label and the region fallback. The Head builds the og:image URL without a locale, so the renderer cannot localize.
rawFindings.impact: A RU/EN vacancy link shared in Telegram or other messengers previews with 'so'm dan', 'Maosh ko'rsatilmagan' and the Uzbek region name. Minor, but visible in the main sharing channel.
rawFindings.evidence: api/src/common/format.ts:2 cur 'so'm', :4 'Maosh ko'rsatilmagan', :6-7 'dan'/'gacha'. og.routes.ts:33 regionName fallback "O'zbekiston"; :35-37 salaryLabel. web pages/vacancies/@slug/+Head.tsx:121 og:image `${API_URL}/api/og/vacancy/${vacancy.slug}` with no locale.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add ?lang=uz|ru|en to the og:image URL in +Head.tsx. In og.routes, pick labels and the region name (by slug) from a small uz/ru/en map, and include lang in the cache key.

rawFindings.title: Language switcher loses the path on error pages; locale cookie helpers are dead code
rawFindings.rootCause: The switcher reads pageContext.localePathname directly. That field is missing on render(404) error pages, which pageLocale() already handles. resolveLocale and persistLocale are never imported.
rawFindings.impact: Switching language on /ru/vacancies/old-slug (404) goes to /en instead of /en/vacancies/old-slug. A returning RU visitor who lands on / gets Uzbek with no remembered preference.
rawFindings.evidence: LanguageSwitcher.tsx:19 `(pageContext.localePathname as string) || '/'`; pageLocale.ts:10-17 already has the URL fallback. config.ts:60 resolveLocale and :68 persistLocale: repo grep finds no callers outside config.ts, including server/index.mjs and api/ssr.js.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Use pageLocale(pageContext).pathname in the switcher. Either delete the cookie helpers, or call persistLocale on switch and use the stored locale (never auto-redirect crawlers) as a hint on '/'.

rawFindings.title: Uzbek suffix spacing and inconsistent terminology across dictionaries
rawFindings.rootCause: Suffixes are concatenated after a space, and there is no glossary for core terms. Each dictionary section uses its own synonyms.
rawFindings.impact: UZ salary shows '5 000 000 so'm dan' instead of 'so'mdan'. The same concept goes by different names from page to page, which weakens clarity for candidates and employers.
rawFindings.evidence: messages.uz.ts:807-808 `${v} so'm dan` / `${v} so'm gacha`; api common/format.ts:6-7 same. Term counts: uz 'ariza' 144 vs 'murojaat' 13, 'nomzod' 49 vs 'ish izlovchi' 11. en 'candidate' 55 / 'job seeker' 11 / 'applicant' 3, 'vacanc*' 144 vs 'job' 134. ru 'кандидат' 39 vs 'соискател' 11.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Fix to so'mdan / so'mgacha in both the web and API. Add a short glossary to DESIGN.md: uz ariza/nomzod/vakansiya, ru отклик/кандидат/вакансия, en application/candidate/job. Normalize the outlier strings.

rawFindings.title: Centered dialogs have no max-height or internal scroll, so action buttons can be off-screen on phones
rawFindings.rootCause: The centered dialog variant was copied without the height limit the bottom-sheet dialogs have. useDialog locks body scroll, so a panel taller than the viewport cannot be scrolled at all.
rawFindings.impact: On landscape phones or with the on-screen keyboard open, the confirm button for invite/accept/reject, the delete confirmation and the rating submit can sit below the viewport with no way to reach them. The employer cannot finish the action. WCAG 1.4.10.
rawFindings.evidence: ApplicationStatusDialog.tsx:71 overlay 'fixed inset-0 flex items-end ... p-4'; :85 panel 'w-full max-w-md animate-pop rounded-2xl ... p-5' holds icon, title, text, a textarea with min-h-[88px] plus hint, and stacked buttons. No max-h or overflow. Same gap in ConfirmDialog.tsx:55, RatingDialog.tsx:71 (StarInput + textarea) and TeamList.tsx:175 (form). useDialog.ts:28 sets body overflow hidden. ReportDialog.tsx:91 and ApplicationDetail.tsx:68 already use max-h-[92dvh] with inner scroll.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add 'max-h-[calc(100dvh-2rem)] overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain' to these panels, or use a flex-col layout with a scrollable body and a sticky footer as ReportDialog does. Extract a shared DialogPanel so the variants stop drifting apart.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-075 (R165), status PARTIAL; this part is still unfixed
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low; CSS only.

rawFindings.title: Custom Select and LanguageSwitcher: no visible focus, no arrow keys, Escape drops focus to body
rawFindings.rootCause: This is a mouse-first popover listbox. The shared useClickOutside only closes it and never restores focus. The trigger's focus:outline-none utility overrides the global :focus-visible outline and nothing replaces it.
rawFindings.impact: Keyboard users cannot see focus on the region, sort and employee-count fields (seeker profile, employer company profile, company catalogue, home search). They have to Tab through every option. After Escape, focus jumps to the start of the document. Screen readers announce listbox semantics that the widget does not implement. WCAG 2.1.1, 2.4.7, 4.1.2.
rawFindings.evidence: Select.tsx:51 trigger has 'focus:outline-none' and no focus-visible style; the border changes only when open (:40). :70-99 is ul role=listbox > li > button role=option with no onKeyDown, no aria-activedescendant and no type-ahead. useClickOutside.ts:18-20 handles Escape by calling onOutside only. The same pattern appears in LanguageSwitcher.tsx:29,47-56 (options lack a lang attribute), Header.tsx:41,170, NotificationBell.tsx:16,31-35 (no aria-haspopup or aria-controls) and SaveSearchButton.tsx:44. CompanyToolbar.tsx:54 (sort) and SearchBar.tsx:47 (region) have no label.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Replace Select with a native <select> using the FieldSelect.tsx pattern (DESIGN.md:740, with dark:[color-scheme:dark]), or implement the full WAI-ARIA listbox/combobox keyboard model. Add a focus-visible ring. Give useClickOutside an optional triggerRef so Escape returns focus to the trigger, and close popovers on focusout. Build LanguageSwitcher as links or menuitemradio with lang set per option. Add aria-labels to the sort and region selects.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-075 (R163), status PARTIAL; Select keyboard support and popover focus are still open
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low to medium: the home SearchBar posts region through the hidden input, which must be kept.

rawFindings.title: Login and signup errors are not announced and not linked to the fields
rawFindings.rootCause: The auth form components were never moved to the aria-invalid/aria-describedby convention in DESIGN.md:143,191. The error is a plain paragraph with no live region.
rawFindings.impact: A screen reader user who enters a wrong password, a duplicate email or hits the rate limit hears nothing; the button simply re-enables. WCAG 3.3.1, 4.1.3. These screens are the entry to every candidate and employer flow and will likely be reused for the Telegram recovery and phone verification screens.
rawFindings.evidence:
login/+Page.tsx:90-92 and signup/+Page.tsx:135-137 render '

{error}

' with no role=alert or aria-live. AuthField (AuthForm.tsx:74-83) and PasswordField (:116-125) take no invalid or describedBy props, so neither aria-invalid nor aria-describedby is ever set, and focus is not moved on error. Placeholders use text-dusk/80 on surface-2: 3.34:1. The correct pattern already exists in AdminStates.tsx:46-49, TelegramConnect.tsx:213, RatingDialog.tsx:128 and PhoneInput.tsx:39-40.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Give the error element role=alert (or a persistent aria-live region) and an id. Add invalid/describedBy props to AuthField and PasswordField and set them for credential errors. Move focus to the error or the first invalid field. Use placeholder:text-dusk.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Header overlays do not fit phone viewports: mobile menu has no max-height, bell popover is clipped on the left
rawFindings.rootCause: The mobile menu panel sits inside a sticky header with no height limit. Header dropdowns are positioned relative to their trigger with no viewport-aware sizing.
rawFindings.impact: On small phones and in landscape, Settings, Logout and the last account links cannot be reached unless the user scrolls to the very bottom of a long page. The left edge of the notification popover (unread dot, start of titles) is cut off. WCAG 1.4.10. This is inferred from static layout math; the earlier browser run checked page overflow with the menus closed.
rawFindings.evidence: Header.tsx:130 is 'sticky top-0 z-50 px-3 pt-3'. The :290-361 panel 'border-t px-4 py-4 lg:hidden' has no max-h or overflow. For a job seeker it holds 5 nav links, the theme/language row, 6 account links and logout: about 640px plus a 78px bar, roughly 715px, which is taller than a ~548px iPhone SE Safari viewport. A sticky box taller than the viewport keeps its bottom off-screen. NotificationBell.tsx:55 is 'absolute right-0 w-[336px] max-w-[calc(100vw-2rem)]'. On mobile only the bell and the hamburger are visible (:163-165, :274), so the bell's right edge is about 289px at 360px width and the popover's left edge lands near -39px (about -17px at 390). The hamburger has no Escape handling and no aria-controls (:269-274). On /profile a second sticky bar is added (ProfileNav.tsx:121).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Give the mobile panel 'max-h-[calc(100dvh-5rem)] overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain', or render it as a fixed sheet using useDialog. Below sm, position the bell popover as 'fixed inset-x-4 top-[4.75rem]' and keep 'sm:absolute sm:right-0'. Add Escape close and aria-controls to the menu button. Check at 360x640 and 740x360.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: none (ISSUE-074 covered only closing the menu on navigation)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Dark-mode signal token fails WCAG AA for button labels and text; hover state drops to 2.98:1
rawFindings.rootCause: One --signal value is used both as a button fill under white text and as a text color on dark surfaces. #6366F1 is too light for white text and too dark for text on #121828. In dark mode the hover token (--signal-strong) is lighter still, which lowers contrast further. The comments were not re-measured after the indigo retheme.
rawFindings.impact: In dark mode every primary CTA (apply, login, signup, save) has its 14px label below AA, down to 2.98:1 on hover. Links, active menu items and counters drawn in text-signal are hard to read. The white check glyph on green completion badges is at 2.01:1. WCAG 1.4.3, 1.4.11.
rawFindings.evidence: global.css:49 --signal #6366F1, :50 --signal-strong #818CF8. Computed ratios: white on #6366F1 4.47; white on #818CF8 2.98 (tailwind.config.js:23 maps signal.dark to signal-strong; 54 hover:bg-signal-dark uses, e.g. AuthForm.tsx:145, Header.tsx:262). text-signal (366 uses) is 3.96 on surface, 3.55 on surface-2, 3.51 on signal-soft (Header.tsx:221, Select.tsx:87). MessageBubble.tsx:73 white/80: 3.45. index/+Page.tsx:256 white/75: 3.24. Pills with bg-white/20 (ProfileNav.tsx:145): 3.18. bg-growth with text-white: 2.01 (ProfileCompletion.tsx:49, TelegramConnect.tsx:238). The comment at global.css:49 and DESIGN.md:13,57 claim 4.9:1.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Split the token into --signal-fill (dark #4F46E5, white text 6.29:1, with a darker hover such as #4338CA at 7.9:1) and --signal-text (dark about #A5B4FC, 8.9:1 on surface). Use plain text-white on signal fills. Use dark:text-paper on bg-growth badges, as VacancyChecklist.tsx:38 already does. Fix the stale comments in global.css, tailwind.config.js:18-20 and DESIGN.md. Add a small unit test that checks token contrast.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-076 (NOT FIXED, deferred by D-031); the 2.98:1 hover and the growth badges were not in the tracker
rawFindings.fixRisk: Visible dark-mode change across roughly 400 usages; needs design sign-off. Low functional risk.
