rawFindings.title: prefers-reduced-motion is still ignored; infinite animations run on home, employer and auth pages
rawFindings.rootCause: A brand decision keeps motion always on (the global.css:419-420 comment says it will not be turned off for reduced motion). There is no reduced-motion media query and no pause control.
rawFindings.impact: WCAG 2.2.2 (level A) and 2.3.3. Users with vestibular disorders see continuous large drifting blobs (up to 260px translate plus scale) and moving gradient text on the landing and login pages, with no way to stop them. It also costs GPU and battery on low-end phones.
rawFindings.evidence: Infinite animations: global.css:231-233 drift-a/b/c (11-17s), :254 particle rise, :353 text-shine 8s, :292 breathe, :411 shimmer 1.6s. Uses: HeroBackdrop.tsx:28-47 (index and employer pages), text-shine on the h1 at index/+Page.tsx:75, employer/+Page.tsx:40, login/+Page.tsx:45, signup/+Page.tsx:61, AuthShell.tsx:101, and BrandLogo.tsx:40. global.css:63 sets html scroll-behavior:smooth, and there are 18 behavior:"smooth" scroll calls. motion-reduce appears only in SalaryDistributionChart.tsx:63 and SalaryExperienceChart.tsx:61, plus a check in VacancyForm.tsx:49. pulse-ring (:281), spin-slow (:285) and float are unused.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block that sets animation:none on .drift-*, .particle, .text-shine, .breathe, .shimmer::after and the entrance animations, sets .reveal-pending to opacity:1 and transform:none, and sets html scroll-behavior:auto. Add a prefersReducedMotion() helper for scrollIntoView calls. Delete the dead keyframes. Record the owner's decision in place of the D-031 deferral.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low; only affects users who have the OS setting enabled.

rawFindings.title: Light mode: text-dusk/80 text, placeholders and tinted status badges are below 4.5:1
rawFindings.rootCause: Opacity modifiers are applied to a mid-contrast token (--dusk #5A6A85), and tinted backgrounds lower the effective contrast of the AA-tuned gold-deep and growth tokens.
rawFindings.impact: Secondary metadata (notification type, posting date, 'not filled' hints, character counter), form placeholders, and application/moderation status badges are hard to read for low-vision users. WCAG 1.4.3.
rawFindings.evidence: Computed dusk/80: 3.59 on surface, 3.45 on paper, 3.34 on surface-2. Text uses: NotificationBell.tsx:146 (11px), VacancyCard.tsx:51, ResumePreview.tsx:22, ResumeWizard.tsx:263, ProfileOverview.tsx:251, profile/ui.tsx:181. Placeholders at /80 in AuthForm.tsx:82,124, FormControls.tsx:7, profile/ui.tsx:68, ContactField.tsx:6, ReportDialog.tsx:79 and DescriptionEditor.tsx:86; /70 (2.95) in AdminArticleEditor.tsx:468. VacancyFilters.tsx:276 ink/55: 4.00. gold-deep on gold/15: 4.47 (VacancyStatusBadge.tsx:8, ApplicationStatus.tsx:20, profile/ui.tsx:397). gold/20: 4.32 (admin/vacancies/+Page.tsx:162, 10px). growth on growth/15: 4.43 (FormSteps.tsx:40).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Use text-dusk without alpha for text and placeholders (5.48:1 on surface, 4.91:1 on surface-2). Darken light --gold-deep to about #9A4A08 and --growth slightly, or switch to /10 tints. Keep dusk/50 only for disabled pagination that is aria-hidden.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Very low; color only.

rawFindings.title: StarInput exposes no selected state and relies on 1.77:1 color
rawFindings.rootCause: The rating input is five plain mouse-oriented buttons, with no radio semantics and no non-color indicator of the selection.
rawFindings.impact: Screen reader users writing a company review or giving a one-time conversation rating cannot tell which score is selected before submitting. Low-vision users can barely tell filled from empty stars in light mode. WCAG 4.1.2, 1.4.1, 1.4.11.
rawFindings.evidence: StarRating.tsx:38-51 renders five '<button aria-label={`${i}`}>' with no aria-pressed or aria-checked and no radio role; the names are bare digits. The selection is shown only by color: text-gold #F59E0B against text-line #E3EAF5 is 1.77:1, and gold on surface is 2.15:1. Hover preview uses onMouseEnter only. Used in CompanyReviews.tsx:222 (group labelled 'your rating') and RatingDialog.tsx:104 (RatingDialog text says the rating can be given only once).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Build it as a radiogroup: visually hidden native radio inputs with i18n labels such as '4 of 5 stars', or role=radio with aria-checked and a roving tabindex. Draw unselected stars as outlines in text-dusk (at least 3:1) and show a numeric 'n/5' next to the stars.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: No skip link, unlabeled primary nav, sticky bars can hide focus, two h1s on the seeker profile
rawFindings.rootCause: The layout has no bypass mechanism and no global scroll padding for the sticky header. Content components hard-code h1 while ProfileHeader already renders one.
rawFindings.impact: Keyboard users tab through the logo, 4-6 nav links, bell, theme, language and account controls on every page (WCAG 2.4.1). Duplicate unlabeled nav landmarks cannot be told apart. Focused controls can scroll under the sticky bars (WCAG 2.4.11). Two h1s blur the profile's page structure.
rawFindings.evidence: Layout.tsx:21-25 renders Header and '<main className="flex-1">' with no skip link and no id (grep finds no 'skip' anywhere in src). Header.tsx:143 and :292 <nav> have no aria-label, while :212 and :318 do; Footer.tsx:140 aria-label="Footer" is hard-coded English. The header is sticky at about 78px (Header.tsx:130) and ProfileNav is sticky at top-[78px] (ProfileNav.tsx:121); global.css sets no scroll-padding-top, only per-section scroll-mt. ProfileHeader.tsx:63 renders an h1 on every tab (profile/+Page.tsx:188), and a second h1 appears at ProfileOverview.tsx:47, ResumeWizard.tsx:69 and headingAs="h1" at profile/+Page.tsx:139,146,153.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add a focus-visible skip link to #main as the first element in Layout and give main tabIndex=-1. Set html scroll-padding-top to about 5.5rem, more on /profile. Label the primary navs through i18n and translate the footer label. Render content headings as h2 on the profile page.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-075 (R247), status PARTIAL; skip link still missing
rawFindings.fixRisk: Very low.

rawFindings.title: Weak or missing focus indicators where utilities override the global focus ring; unlabeled search inputs
rawFindings.rootCause: focus:outline-none (specificity 0,2,0) beats the global :focus-visible outline (global.css:437-440), and several replacement styles are too faint.
rawFindings.impact: Keyboard users lose track of focus in the main home search and in kebab menus. Search inputs are identified only by their placeholder.
rawFindings.evidence: 38 elements use outline-none. SearchBar.tsx:24 replaces it only with focus-within:border-ink/25, a 1.43:1 change from the line color; the input at :31 has no label or aria-label, and neither does AdminShell.tsx:216. ActionsMenu.tsx:56 items use focus:bg-surface-2, a 1.11:1 background change. ArticleCard.tsx:41 removes the link outline and the card ring at :22 is signal/50, 2.24:1 against paper. PhoneInput.tsx:29-31 keeps border-signal permanently when invalid, so focus causes no visible change and the invalid state is not shown in the danger color.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Use the VacancySearch.tsx:92 pattern (focus-within:border-signal plus ring-4 ring-signal/10). Add sr-only labels to SearchBar and the AdminShell search. Give menu items a focus-visible bg-signal-soft with an inset ring. Use an opaque ring-signal on ArticleCard. Show PhoneInput's invalid state with border-danger and keep a focus ring.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Very low.

rawFindings.title: Dark and responsive polish: no global color-scheme, 100vh sidebars, illustrations without dark variants, nowrap and long titles
rawFindings.rootCause: Dark mode is applied through token classes only. Native browser widgets need color-scheme, which is added per control instead of globally.
rawFindings.impact: Resume month pickers and admin selects show light popups and dark-on-dark indicator icons in dark mode. Minor layout polish problems on mobile browsers and in narrow columns.
rawFindings.evidence: There is no global color-scheme; it is set per control only (FormControls.tsx:126, FieldSelect.tsx:51). It is missing on ExperienceList.tsx:304,317 (type=month, via profile/ui.tsx:68), AdminShell.tsx:242 and admin/+Page.tsx:276. Scrollbars are styled for WebKit only (global.css:82-91). Illustrations without a dark variant: NotificationsHeader, ApplicationsHeader, FavoritesHeader, ArticlesHeader, CompaniesHero. 100vh is still used at vacancies/+Page.tsx:134, companies/+Page.tsx:119 and VacancyForm.tsx:544. SidebarCards.tsx:37 is whitespace-nowrap. Titles at VacancyCard.tsx:57-62 and vacancies/VacancyCard.tsx:80 have no break-words inside overflow-hidden or line-clamp, so long words are clipped (inference).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Set color-scheme globally (':root{color-scheme:light} .dark{color-scheme:dark}') and add scrollbar-color; then the per-control hacks can go. Use 100dvh. Replace whitespace-nowrap with min-w-0 and break-words. Add [overflow-wrap:anywhere] to card titles. Provide dark illustration variants or a dark:opacity treatment.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Very low; SocialLogin.tsx:130 already forces a light color-scheme on the Google container.

rawFindings.title: Filter drawers duplicate the modal focus trap and have drifted from useDialog
rawFindings.rootCause: Both drawers were written before useDialog existed and were never migrated to it.
rawFindings.impact: Low today because the close button is always focusable. Future fixes to one trap will not reach the other two, and modal behavior is already inconsistent.
rawFindings.evidence: CompanyFilterDrawer.tsx:7,46-85 and VacancyFilterDrawer.tsx:7,185-223 copy the useDialog logic with differences. Their FOCUSABLE selector matches bare 'select', so disabled selects stay in the loop, while useDialog.ts:4 uses select:not([disabled]). With no focusable items they just return, letting Tab leave the modal, while useDialog.ts:40-42 calls preventDefault. They restore focus without preventScroll (useDialog.ts:59 passes it). The panels have no tabIndex=-1.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Replace both effects with useDialog(open, panelRef, onClose), keep the matchMedia close listener, and add tabIndex={-1} to the panels.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Very low.

rawFindings.title: Verified phone is not unique and any Telegram contact share silently overwrites it
rawFindings.rootCause: User.phone is an optional free-text string with no unique or normalized form. handleContact sets phone and isPhoneVerified=true on whatever account the chat is linked to. It does not check whether another account already holds that verified number, and it does not treat a different existing phone as a phone change. Relinking a chat clears only telegramChatId on the old account, so that account keeps its verified phone. Unverified users can store any phone string through PATCH /api/profile.
rawFindings.impact: The same verified phone can sit on several accounts (rule E), so phone-based recovery (rule B) would be ambiguous or hit the wrong account. The primary phone changes with no security event, no audit entry and no session invalidation (rule G). One SIM passes the requirePhoneVerified anti-spam gate for many accounts. Scenario: account A links Telegram T and shares its contact. The same person opens a link from account B in T. A is detached but stays verified; sharing the contact again verifies B with the same number.
rawFindings.evidence: schema.prisma:163 `phone String?` has no @unique or index; :167 isPhoneVerified. telegram.service.ts:269-273 relink runs updateMany({telegramChatId, id not userId}) to set telegramChatId null, then update; the old account's phone and flag are untouched. :339-343 `phone = '+'+digits; update {phone, isPhoneVerified:true}` with no duplicate lookup. profile.routes.ts:15,65-66 saves any 30-character phone while unverified (web PersonalInfo.tsx:85). telegram.routes.ts:38-44 unlink leaves the verified phone in place.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Store phones as normalized E.164 in a dedicated collection, e.g. VerifiedPhone {phoneE164 @unique, userId, kind primary|backup, verifiedAt, telegramUserId}. Rows exist only when verified, so the unique index never collides on nulls. In handleContact, send a generic reply and stop when the number is verified on another account. When the account already has a different verified phone, route through an explicit phone-change flow: audit event, plus a tokenVersion bump if the risk policy requires it. Define and log the policy for relink and unlink. Run the read-only duplicate report (new check A1/A2) before creating the index.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: None tracks phone uniqueness. ISSUE-010 (FIXED) only added the Telegram login confirmation step.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Existing duplicates block index creation and need manual resolution. Stricter uniqueness may lock out families sharing one SIM; product decision.

rawFindings.title: Telegram identity is keyed by a non-unique chat id instead of the Telegram user id; lookups use findFirst
rawFindings.rootCause: Linking stores String(msg.chat.id) in User.telegramChatId, which has only a non-unique index. Uniqueness is left to code: a two-step, non-transactional updateMany then update. There is no private-chat check, and msg.from.id is never stored. Login confirmation, contact verification and support attribution all resolve the account with an unordered findFirst({telegramChatId}). The Telegram login endpoints are still live.
rawFindings.impact: Rule F (one Telegram identity per account) cannot be enforced at the DB level. Any duplicate (a cross-instance race or a manual edit) makes login and phone verification pick an arbitrary account. Inference: a /start <token> sent in a group where the bot is present links the group chat; after that, any member who posts their own contact sets their number as the account's verified phone. Telegram also remains a login channel, against rule A.
rawFindings.evidence: schema.prisma:172-176,201: telegramChatId String? with a plain @@index; the comment says code enforces uniqueness. telegram.service.ts:217 chat type has only an id; :244 chatId=String(msg.chat.id); :269-273 updateMany then update, no transaction; :162 handleLoginStart findFirst; :328 checks only contact.user_id===from.id; :333 handleContact findFirst; :364 support findFirst. auth.routes.ts:137-158 /api/auth/telegram/start and /poll; web lib/api.ts:147,157 still call them.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add TelegramIdentity {telegramUserId String @unique, userId @unique @db.ObjectId, chatId, linkedAt}. A row exists only while linked, so there is no null collision. Accept /start and contacts only from private chats, bound to from.id. Link inside a transaction that fails on conflict, or offer an explicit audited re-link instead of silently taking over. Resolve accounts only by unique keys, never findFirst. Remove the Telegram login endpoints and UI (rule A).
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-010 (FIXED: confirmation step added; the login channel still exists); ISSUE-122 (NOT FIXED: no test for the Telegram login state machine); D-039
rawFindings.fixRisk: Existing links need a telegramUserId backfill; chat id equals user id only for private chats, so group-linked rows must be reset. Removing Telegram login changes UX.

rawFindings.title: An owner can re-activate an admin-archived vacancy; admin approval skips placement and block checks
rawFindings.rootCause: A vacancy has a single status with no record of who closed it. The owner PATCH allows archived to active, so an admin archive can be undone by the owner. The admin moderate route writes active, rejected or archived from any state without assertVacancyPlacement and without checking the owner's isBlocked. Blocking archives only active vacancies, so the owner's moderation and draft vacancies stay approvable.
rawFindings.impact: Moderation bypass, against the product rule: an archived spam vacancy comes back without review. Admin approval can publish a legacy vacancy with no category or workplaceType. It can also publish a blocked employer's vacancy, whose public page then collects applications for an account that cannot log in.
rawFindings.evidence: admin.routes.ts:287-309: status enum [active,rejected,archived]; no placement or owner checks. admin.routes.ts:203-208: block archives only status 'active'. vacancies.routes.ts:240-243: `allowedFrom = {active:['archived','draft'], archived:['active']}`. Web admin/vacancies/+Page.tsx:185-188 offers Archive on active rows of the moderation table. schema.prisma:424-427 has only status and rejectionReason; no closedBy or moderatedAt.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Record provenance, e.g. closedBy: owner|admin|block, moderatedBy, moderatedAt. Forbid owner re-activation when closedBy is admin or block, and send the vacancy to moderation instead. Run assertVacancyPlacement and an owner-not-blocked check in the admin approve path. On block, also take moderation and draft vacancies out of the approvable queue. Log admin moderation events.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-024 and ISSUE-059 (FIXED for the owner PATCH path only); D-015
rawFindings.fixRisk: Legacy archived rows have no provenance; default them to owner-closed so employers are not locked out. That admin Archive is meant as a moderation action is inferred from the admin UI.

rawFindings.title: No persistent data model for the new auth rules (recovery tokens, backup phone, manual recovery, security audit log)
rawFindings.rootCause: The schema has no collections for recovery or verification challenges, manual recovery requests, security events or verified backup phones. Telegram link and login tokens live in process memory as raw Map keys. The only backup-phone field is JobSeekerProfile.additionalPhone: free text, unverified, and absent for employers. Password recovery does not exist.
rawFindings.impact: Rules B, F, H, I, J and L cannot be implemented. One-time, replay-protected, hashed-at-rest tokens and revocation after a reset all need persistent state. Restarts drop tokens and a second API instance splits them. Phone verification, phone change, Telegram link/unlink and admin recovery leave no audit trail. The backup phone cannot be used for recovery or uniqueness.
rawFindings.evidence: schema.prisma:160-807 has no recovery, audit or identity model; only StaffInvite has tokenHash (702-720). schema.prisma:217 additionalPhone String?; profile.routes.ts:16,74,83 accepts any string; web PersonalInfo.tsx:86. telegram.service.ts:90 linkTokens Map and :131 loginTokens Map (raw token keys, 30/5 min TTL). ISSUES.md:46 ISSUE-012 NOT FIXED; DECISIONS.md:106-112 D-010.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add AuthChallenge {purpose link|verify_phone|recovery|phone_change, tokenHash @unique, userId?, expiresAt with a TTL index, usedAt, attempts}. Consume it with a conditional update (usedAt null to now). Add RecoveryRequest {userId, status, reviewedBy, decidedAt, note} and SecurityEvent {userId, type from the rule L list, actorId, ip, createdAt, allowlisted meta}. Keep backup phones in VerifiedPhone with kind=backup. After a reset, bump tokenVersion and revoke open challenges. Reuse the StaffInvite hash pattern.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Prisma cannot declare MongoDB TTL or partial indexes, so they need a raw createIndexes step. Audit meta needs a key allowlist so secrets are never stored.

rawFindings.title: Google sign-in merges into an existing account with the same email without proof of ownership
rawFindings.rootCause: googleLogin looks the user up by email and issues tokens if one exists. Password registrations never verify email (isEmailVerified stays false), so that account may belong to someone else. No provider-link record exists, so a merge can be neither distinguished nor audited.
rawFindings.impact: Pre-account takeover: an attacker registers victim@gmail.com with a password. The victim later signs in with Google and ends up using the attacker's account (CV, applications, chats), while the attacker's password keeps working. This violates the session policy against unsafe automatic Google merges.
rawFindings.evidence: auth.service.ts:37-60 registerUser creates the user without setting isEmailVerified. :222-226 `existing = findUnique({email}); if (existing) { assertNotBlocked; return issueTokens(...) }`. :235-241 Google-created users get a random hash and isEmailVerified:true. No provider or identity model exists. ISSUES.md:76 ISSUE-042 PARTIAL; DECISIONS.md:117-122 D-011 kept the merge.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Do not auto-merge when existing.isEmailVerified is false. Return a conflict asking the user to log in with their password and link Google from settings. Store AuthIdentity {provider, subject @unique, userId}. On a verified link, bump tokenVersion to drop sessions created before it, and emit a Google-linked security event.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Password users who forgot their password lose the Google shortcut until Telegram recovery exists.

rawFindings.title: Admin role change leaves invalid cross-role data
rawFindings.rootCause: PATCH /api/admin/users/:id/role only writes role and revokes sessions. It does not check the target's current role, so staff can be moved too. It does not handle owned companies, vacancies, applications, conversations, StaffProfile or authored articles. Ownership helpers resolve by ownerUserId regardless of role.
rawFindings.impact: employer to job_seeker: the company and its active vacancies stay public, and new applications notify a user who can no longer reach /api/employer/*. That user can also apply to and review their own company. job_seeker to employer: applications and seeker-side conversations remain under an employer. content_editor to job_seeker: StaffProfile and published articles keep a non-staff author. These states are exactly the role-mismatch checks that returned 0 only on dev data.
rawFindings.evidence: admin.routes.ts:217-226 calls user.update({data:{role}}) and revokeUserSessions; nothing else. ownership.ts:10-12,23-25 filter by ownerUserId only. companies.routes.ts:84-96 requireRole('employer'). reviews.routes.ts:27-37 eligibility is any application to the company. DATA_INTEGRITY.md:118,135,142-143,164 role-mismatch checks.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Refuse role changes that would orphan data (409 with counts), or run an explicit transition: archive the vacancies and remove them from search, block self-apply and self-review, keep history read-only. Restrict this route to job_seeker and employer targets and leave staff roles to team.routes. Record a role_changed SecurityEvent.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low; admins need a clear error explaining what blocks the change.

rawFindings.title: Blocking an account leaves its dependent data live and reachable
rawFindings.rootCause: Blocking archives only the employer's active vacancies. Apart from /api/candidates, the sitemap and the alert sweep, no read or write path checks the counterparty's isBlocked. Unblocking restores nothing, and nothing records which vacancies the block archived.
rawFindings.impact: Job seekers can start conversations with, and message, a blocked employer whose company stays in the catalog with ratings. Employers still get a blocked seeker's email, phone and resume in application lists. Approved reviews and peer ratings from blocked users keep affecting ratings. After unblock, the vacancies closed by the block cannot be told apart from ones the owner closed.
rawFindings.evidence: admin.routes.ts:197-211 archives only status 'active'. chat.routes.ts:342-347 creates a seeker-to-company conversation without an owner block check; deliverMessage at :62-91 has none either. applications.routes.ts:169-221 and :259-303 do not filter isBlocked, unlike candidates.routes.ts:48 `isBlocked:false`. seo.routes.ts:116 excludes blocked owners, but companies.list.ts has no owner or isBlocked filter (grep). companies.routes.ts:221-225 review aggregate includes every user.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Define one block policy and apply it everywhere. Exclude blocked owners' companies from the catalog, company page and chat start. Mark or hide blocked seekers in employer application lists. Exclude blocked users' reviews and ratings from aggregates. Set closedBy='block' on vacancies archived by a block so unblock can restore them. Add check A9.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-035 / ISSUE-108 (FIXED: sessions only); D-012 (candidates list excludes blocked accounts)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Hiding applications may hurt employer record-keeping; marking is safer.

rawFindings.title: Legacy and seeded vacancies still lack workplaceType; schema keeps category and workplace optional; remote/office contradictions accepted
rawFindings.rootCause: Neither seed writes workplaceType, no backfill exists, and Vacancy.categoryId and workplaceType are optional in the schema. Correct behaviour relies on the effectiveWorkplaceType fallback (employmentType 'remote'). createSchema does not reject employmentType 'remote' combined with workplaceType office or hybrid.
rawFindings.impact: DI-1 (83/83 dev vacancies without workplace_type) comes back on every demo rebuild, breaking the demo-coverage and required-workplace rules. Legacy non-remote rows need an edit before they can be re-published, while admin approve skips the rule entirely. Contradictory remote+office rows distort filters and facets.
rawFindings.evidence: demo-seed.ts:1689-1715 vacancy.create without workplaceType; the word does not appear in the file. seed.ts:292-330 upsert omits it too. schema.prisma:402 `categoryId String?`; :411-412 `workplaceType WorkplaceType?` (legacy comment). vacancies.rules.ts:27-30 fallback. vacancies.routes.ts:62-63 has no cross-field refine. DATA_INTEGRITY.md:13,127 DI-1=83. ISSUES.md:123 ISSUE-089 NOT FIXED.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Write workplaceType in both seeds. Add an idempotent backfill: set remote where employmentType is remote, and flag other rows for the owner to edit rather than guessing. Refine the schema so employmentType 'remote' requires workplaceType 'remote', or deprecate 'remote' as an employment type. After the backfill, make categoryId and workplaceType required. Enforce placement in admin approve.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: DI-1, DI-R4, ISSUE-089 (NOT FIXED), ISSUE-059 / ISSUE-129 (FIXED), D-028
rawFindings.fixRisk: Report the rows read-only first; guessing 'office' for unknown rows would publish wrong data.

rawFindings.title: Admin hard delete of a vacancy cascades applications and history and leaves dangling references
rawFindings.rootCause: The 409 VACANCY_HAS_APPLICATIONS guard applies only to non-admins. Prisma's emulated onDelete Cascade then removes applications, status history and favorites. Notification.payload stores applicationId and vacancyId as untyped JSON, and reviews stay even when the application that made them eligible is gone.
rawFindings.impact: Candidates silently lose their application record: the data loss ISSUE-025 fixed for employers still happens on the admin path. Notifications keep ids of deleted rows. Company reviews remain with no supporting application.
rawFindings.evidence: vacancies.routes.ts:279-289: `if (role !== 'admin') { count; 409 }`, then vacancy.delete. schema.prisma:465 Application.vacancy onDelete Cascade; :489 history Cascade; :572 Favorite Cascade; :620 payload Json?. applications.routes.ts:111 payload {applicationId, vacancyId}. DECISIONS.md:163 D-015 allows admin delete.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: When applications exist, make admin removal a soft state (archived, closedBy admin, hidden from search). Allow hard delete only with zero applications, or behind an explicit confirm flag plus an audit event. Consumers should tolerate missing notification targets.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Application status accepts any transition, and applying writes no initial history row
rawFindings.rootCause: statusSchema allows viewed, invited, rejected or accepted from any current status; the only guard is a no-op for the same status. Status can also change after the vacancy is archived or rejected. The apply path creates the application with no initial 'sent' history row, while the demo seed writes one.
rawFindings.impact: Candidates can get 'Accepted' followed by 'Viewed', or 'Rejected' followed by 'Invited' notifications. UI timelines start at an arbitrary change. The check 'status == last history newStatus' cannot be applied uniformly because real and seeded rows have different shapes.
rawFindings.evidence: applications.routes.ts:20-23 z.enum([viewed,invited,rejected,accepted]); :315-319 no vacancy status check; :326-345 only `if (!changed && !reasonText) return current`; :82-90 create without history. demo-seed.ts:1433-1449 history starts with oldStatus null and newStatus sent. DECISIONS.md:207 D-019 says no state machine was implemented.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Define allowed transitions, e.g. sent to viewed to invited to accepted or rejected, with terminal states changed only through an explicit reopen; return 409 otherwise. Write the initial history row in the same transaction as the apply. Tolerate legacy rows without it in integrity checks.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Employers correcting mistakes need a reopen path.

rawFindings.title: DATA_INTEGRITY.md baseline is stale and its script is not in the repo: checks to re-run
rawFindings.rootCause: The 103 read-only checks ran once, against the 61-user dev database, from a script in a temporary session scratchpad outside the repo. The doc claims the indexes fully match the schema. The code has changed since: new indexes, role/block/delete paths, and DI-R2 is now fixed in code.
rawFindings.impact: There is no reproducible way to verify production invariants at 10k users before adding unique indexes for phone and Telegram identity. The documented index table is already wrong.
rawFindings.evidence: DATA_INTEGRITY.md:4 script under AppData/Local/Temp/.../scratchpad; :37 claims a full match. Missing from the index table: :74 users created_at (schema.prisma:203); :84 vacancies [status,is_premium,published_at] and [company_id,status] (:442,:444); :85 applications created_at and [vacancy_id,status] (:476-477); :89 messages [conversation_id,is_read] (:557); :93 notifications [user_id,created_at] (:628). DI-R2 fixed: vacancies.service.ts:662 `salaryMin ?? null`, :315 isSet:false.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Commit a strictly read-only script, e.g. apps/api/scripts/data-integrity.mjs using findRaw, count and listIndexes. Re-run on a staging copy or prod secondary: (1) all orphan-reference checks, :106-169; (2) role-mismatch checks :118, :135, :142-143, :164 (because of the role-change route); (3) multiple companies per owner, :119 (race); (4) DI-1 and business rules :126-131, plus salary_min $exists:false; (5) duplicate application and conversation pairs and telegramChatId duplicates, :136 and :183; (6) email duplicate and lowercase checks, :180-182; (7) the enum table, :186-212; (8) listIndexes against the current schema. Regenerate the index table from the results.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Run off-peak or on a secondary; never add write operations.

rawFindings.title: No integrity checks exist for the new auth rules (phone and Telegram identity uniqueness, block and history consistency)
rawFindings.rootCause: The check set predates the new auth rules. On users it covers only email and telegramChatId duplicates; nothing checks phone, verification flags, backup phone, recovery state or block consistency. e2e marks every user phone-verified directly, so no test exercises these invariants.
rawFindings.impact: Unique indexes for rules E and F would fail at deploy, or duplicates would stay hidden and recovery could target the wrong account.
rawFindings.evidence: DATA_INTEGRITY.md:180-183: user checks cover email and telegramChatId only; no phone or isPhoneVerified check among :106-184. The code creates duplicates at telegram.service.ts:269-273 and :339-343, and profile.routes.ts:65-66. e2e-check.mjs:244,341,1254 run updateMany isPhoneVerified=true for all users. App code cannot yield isPhoneVerified=true with a null phone (handleContact writes both), but those e2e updates can.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add read-only checks. A1: duplicate digits-only phone among isPhoneVerified=true. A2: the same across all users, to size the migration. A3: isPhoneVerified=true with phone null, missing or empty. A4: verified phone not matching ^\+\d{9,15}$. A5: telegramChatId duplicates and negative (group/channel) chat ids. A6: isPhoneVerified=true with telegramChatId null. A7: additionalPhone equal to the user's own phone or another user's phone. A8, once the new models exist: duplicate telegramUserId, users with more than one identity, unused challenges past expiresAt, more than one active challenge per user and purpose, challenges older than the user's last tokenVersion bump, audit meta containing password or token keys. A9: blocked owners with active or moderation vacancies. A10: company owner not an employer. A11: application.status differs from the last history newStatus.
rawFindings.fixRisk: None; read-only.

rawFindings.title: One company per owner and one resume per profile are check-then-create without unique indexes
rawFindings.rootCause: Four paths look up before creating: POST /api/companies, PUT /api/employer/company, registration with companyName, and PUT /api/resume. Company.ownerUserId and Resume.jobSeekerId have only non-unique indexes.
rawFindings.impact: Concurrent requests (a double submit, or registration racing a profile save) create a second company or resume. primaryCompany and findFirst return the oldest, so the duplicate is invisible in the UI. ownedCompanyIds still counts it for candidates and applications, and the catalog and sitemap expose it.
rawFindings.evidence: companies.routes.ts:251-259 `if (await primaryCompany()) 409`, then create; :105-139 same pattern. auth.service.ts:63-67. schema.prisma:337 @@index([ownerUserId]); :252 @@index([jobSeekerId]). resume.routes.ts:96-104 findFirst, then create. ownership.ts:7-8 comment accepts multiple companies.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: If one company per owner is final, run the duplicate report (DATA_INTEGRITY.md:119), then add @@unique([ownerUserId]) and map P2002 to the existing 409. Do the same for resumes with @@unique([jobSeekerId]), or turn the resume save into an upsert keyed by profile.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-037 (FIXED: 409 check added; race remains); DI-R1
rawFindings.fixRisk: Index creation fails if duplicates already exist. Prisma requires User.ownedCompanies to become an optional one-to-one relation.

rawFindings.title: Demo HR account shows 'Premium tarif faollashtirildi' notification with 100-vacancy cap and paywalled candidate base
rawFindings.rootCause: The HR row in NOTIFICATIONS still has pre-free copy: title 'Premium tarif faollashtirildi', body 'Obuna 30 kunga faol: 100 tagacha vakansiya va nomzodlar bazasi ochiq.', url '/pricing'. seedNotifications (1515-1524) writes it verbatim into payload.url for the NextBrain owner (1917). D-014 moved production notification URLs to /profile but the seed was never updated. The console also prints '(NextBrain, Premium)' at 1927.
rawFindings.impact: hr@demo.ish.top is the demo employer account. Its /notifications page and bell say vacancies are capped and candidate search needs a paid Premium plan. That contradicts the free, no-limit product rule. The link goes adapter.ts:86 ('/pricing' -> employer target) -> 302 -> /employer.
rawFindings.evidence: demo-seed.ts:1296 ["hr","system","Premium tarif faollashtirildi","Obuna 30 kunga faol: 100 tagacha vakansiya va nomzodlar bazasi ochiq.","/pricing",144,true]; demo-seed.ts:1917 seedNotifications(NOTIFICATIONS, hr->ownerId.nextbrain); lib/notifications/adapter.ts:85-86; pages/pricing/+guard.ts:10-12; demo-seed.ts:1927.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Replace the row with a message that fits a free platform (for example company verified -> /employer) or delete it. Remove 'Premium' from the console line at 1927. Re-run db:demo, passing --for again.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-080 (PARTIAL, merged R238); ISSUE-064 (FIXED, merged R148 flagged this demo notification) - still present
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: seed data only; the demo DB must be re-seeded.

rawFindings.title: Demo seed bypasses BILLING_ENABLED: seeds priced plans, paid company subscriptions and 11 payments
rawFindings.rootCause: createDemo() always calls ensurePlans() (1620) and loads plan ids (1624-1625). COMPANIES carry plan 'premium'/'standard' with planDaysLeft (92, 120-121, 183-184). company.create sets subscriptionPlanId/subscriptionExpiresAt (1672-1673). The payments loop seeds 9 paid, 1 pending and 1 failed (1821-1850). Admin notifications about payments sit at 1299-1300. The server gates ensurePlans behind features.billing (server.ts:270); the seed does not.
rawFindings.impact: Demo/dev data looks like a paid platform. subscription_plans hold 490 000 / 1 290 000 so'm and a free plan of '3 ta faol vakansiya'. Admin overview shows non-zero 'Tushum' revenue, the admin companies list shows Premium/Standart with expiry dates, and /admin/payments has a pending row whose confirm sends a tariff notification. Production is not affected (seed refuses production without --force, :2049).
rawFindings.evidence: demo-seed.ts:54 import ensurePlans; :1620 await ensurePlans(); :1672-1673 subscriptionPlanId/subscriptionExpiresAt; :1822-1834 payments array (grandbuild pending, registon failed); :1837 prisma.payment.create; :1299-1300 admin 'To'lov kutilmoqda' / 'To'lov amalga oshmadi'; server.ts:270 if (features.billing) await ensurePlans().
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Drop plan and payment seeding, and the plan fields in COMPANIES, or wrap them in features.billing. Remove the admin payment notifications. Keep the reset cleanup (1571) so existing demo payments are deleted.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: the admin payments page then shows its empty state and revenue shows 0 (see the admin gating finding).

rawFindings.title: Admin payment confirm and billing admin UI are not gated by BILLING_ENABLED; confirm notifies employer that a tariff was activated
rawFindings.rootCause: adminRoutes is registered unconditionally (server.ts:254). /api/admin/payments (461-499) and POST /api/admin/payments/:transactionId/confirm (502-520) call markPaymentPaid (import :17) with no features.billing check. The overview always aggregates payments (99-101, 127) and the companies list includes subscriptionPlan (347, 361-362). Web always shows the 'To'lovlar' nav (AdminShell.tsx:50), an accent 'Tushum' revenue card (admin/+Page.tsx:107-112) and a 'Tarif' column (admin/companies/+Page.tsx:112,121-127).
rawFindings.impact: With monetization off, an admin can confirm any legacy pending payment. That writes subscriptionPlanId/expiry to the company (unlocks nothing) and sends the employer 'To'lov tasdiqlandi' / '"Standart" tarifi faollashtirildi.', a tariff message on a free platform. Admins also see revenue and tariff UI for a feature that does not exist.
rawFindings.evidence: admin.routes.ts:502-520 (notify title 'To'lov tasdiqlandi', body `"${payment.plan.name}" tarifi faollashtirildi.`); server.ts:253 billing gated vs :254 adminRoutes ungated; AdminShell.tsx:50; admin/+Page.tsx:107-112; messages.uz.ts:1808 'To'lovlar', :1823 'Tushum', :1879 'Tarif'. No e2e check hits /api/admin/payments.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Return 404/409 from confirm when !features.billing, or register the payment admin routes only with the flag. Add a billing flag to /api/admin/overview and hide the revenue card, tariff column and nav item when it is off. Keep a read-only legacy list if records must stay visible.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: admin-only. Make sure the admin payments page handles 404 cleanly.

rawFindings.title: Candidate-facing 'Premium' badge, 'premium vacancies only' filter and premium-first default sort imply a paid tier
rawFindings.rootCause: Vacancy.isPremium (schema.prisma:426) can only be set by an admin (admin.routes.ts:287-307); employer vacancy schemas do not accept it. The public UI still labels it 'Premium': gold badge (vacancies/VacancyCard.tsx:64-68, components/VacancyCard.tsx:64-66, VacancyDetailHeader.tsx:45-47), filter switch (VacancyFilters.tsx:242-244), chip (VacancyToolbar.tsx:130). i18n: uz 151/1103/1120/1128 'Faqat premium vakansiyalar'; ru 'Премиум'; en 'Premium jobs only'. Default 'Eng dolzarb' sorts isPremium first (vacancies.service.ts:276-284,325; search.service.ts:261).
rawFindings.impact: On a free platform the main job search shows a Premium tier and a premium-only filter, which suggests employers pay for visibility. That conflicts with 'premium is not core UX'. No payment path exists, so the impact is perception and consistency. Earlier audit kept the flag and noted only the naming.
rawFindings.evidence: VacancyFilters.tsx:242 <Switch checked={value.premium}>{f.premium}</Switch>; VacancyCard.tsx:66-68 {v.card.premium}; messages.uz.ts:1103 premium: "Faqat premium vakansiyalar"; vacancies.service.ts:276-283 DATE_ORDER [{isPremium:"desc"},...] used for relevance; alerts.service.ts:94 qs.set("premium","1"); FINAL_AUDIT.md:271.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Keep the admin highlight but give it a neutral label (uz 'Tavsiya etiladi', ru 'Рекомендуем', en 'Featured'). Consider removing the public premium-only filter and chip. Keep the premium URL/API param for backward compatibility and update DESIGN.md:798.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: labels/i18n only if the param name stays. e2e-check.mjs:292 uses premium=1 and is unaffected.

rawFindings.title: /pricing page, billing client API/types and pricing i18n remain as dead code with conflicting static prices
rawFindings.rootCause: +guard.ts:10-12 always returns 302 -> /employer, so +Page.tsx (checkout, Payme/Click picker, payment history), +data.ts (fetchPlans), +Head.tsx and +title.ts never run. Also dead: apiExtra.ts:287-316, types.ts:471-521, api.ts:34 unused import, and i18n uz pricing 561-590 ('Biznes' 499 000 so'm, '1 ta faol vakansiya'), pricingExtra 1772-1798, footer.employersPricing 406, open.pricing 1592, support.categories.payments 432 (hidden, faq.ts:76), meta.pricing 47. ru/en and i18n/types.ts have the same keys.
rawFindings.impact: Adds maintenance load and leaves a misleading source of truth. The i18n catalogue ('Biznes' 499 000) conflicts with DEFAULT_PLANS ('Standart' 490 000), and its limit text contradicts the free rule. Deleting the guard would instantly expose a checkout UI. Admin pages depend on pricingExtra.status* labels (admin/payments/+Page.tsx:59-62, admin/+Page.tsx:110).
rawFindings.evidence: pages/pricing/+guard.ts:11 throw redirect(localizeHref("/employer"...),302); +Page.tsx:55 startCheckout(...); apiExtra.ts:292 fetchPlans -> /api/plans (404 when flag off, e2e-check.mjs:191-196); messages.uz.ts:575 price "499 000 so'm" vs billing.service.ts:32 price 490_000; Footer.tsx:65-68 never uses employersPricing; adapter.ts:86 never returns 'pricing'.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Keep only +guard.ts (consider 301) and delete the other pricing page files, billing fetchers and types. Move the payment status labels to admin.payments. Remove the pricing, pricingExtra, footer.employersPricing, open.pricing, meta.pricing and support payments keys (plus the SUPPORT_CATEGORIES/SupportCategoryCard 'payments' entries) in uz/ru/en/types.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium: the Messages type must stay consistent across 3 locales; web typecheck catches misses.

rawFindings.title: Billing module unsafe to re-enable: plans encode vacancy cap and paid candidate search; webhook marks paid on any signed call
rawFindings.rootCause: DEFAULT_PLANS (17-62): free plan maxActiveVacancies 3, canSearchCandidates false, '3 ta faol vakansiya'. Paid plans sell 'Nomzodlar bazasidan qidiruv' and 'Tasdiqlangan kompaniya belgisi'. assertCanSearchCandidates (170-180) still throws 402 PLAN_FEATURE_LOCKED with no caller, and canPostMore stays (163). The webhook (billing.routes.ts:121-160) marks any signed request paid, ignoring Payme method and amount; comparisons are not timing-safe (312,326). createCheckout creates unbounded pending payments (198-218). env.ts:83 still describes a 'qo'lda tasdiqlash' mode.
rawFindings.impact: Inert today because routes are not registered (server.ts:253). README.md:142 and DEPLOY.md:72 document BILLING_ENABLED=true as a supported switch. Turning it on would publish /api/plans with a 3-vacancy free cap and paid candidate search that contradict the rules and the code. A signed Payme pre-check could activate a plan without payment.
rawFindings.evidence: billing.service.ts:22-27 maxActiveVacancies: 3 / canSearchCandidates: false / "3 ta faol vakansiya"; :174-178 AppError(402,"PLAN_FEATURE_LOCKED"); billing.routes.ts:142 await markPaymentPaid(transactionId) with no method/amount check; :159 {result:{state:2}}; env.ts:83; grep: assertCanSearchCandidates has no caller.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Preferred: delete the billing module and keep the schema per architecture §14. If it stays: remove the gating plan copy, assertCanSearchCandidates and canPostMore; implement provider state machines with method, amount and timingSafeEqual checks; reuse pending payments; mark the flag 'do not enable' in README/.env.example.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-064 (FIXED via flag only; merged R147 webhook and R239 DEFAULT_PLANS still true in code)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low when deleting: e2e expects /api/plans 404, which still holds. admin.routes.ts:17 imports markPaymentPaid and must change too.

Pre-deploy question 2 (651-652) asks for a provider contract and says 'kalit yo'q bo'lsa tizim admin tasdig'i rejimida ishlaydi'. No version mentions removing the 402 (D-012), BILLING_ENABLED (D-014), the /pricing redirect or unlimited vacancies. A grep of CHANGELOG for BILLING_ENABLED or bepul finds nothing.

rawFindings.title: Audit maps still present /api/candidates 402 gate and open billing routes as current, with no snapshot banner
rawFindings.rootCause: The PHASE-1 maps (dated 2026-09-14) were not updated after the fixes. API_MAP.md:116/:285 describe '402 PLAN_FEATURE_LOCKED'; :179-183 list billing routes as registered; :260/:272 ditto. ROUTE_MAP.md:117/:141 cite /pricing notification URLs at admin.routes.ts:483 and billing.routes.ts:155 (now url '/profile' at admin.routes.ts:517 and billing.routes.ts:155). DB_MAP.md:199 notes the 402 conflict. ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT.md:23,83,127 quote README monetization claims that have since been fixed. No 'snapshot/stale' note in the headers.
rawFindings.impact: These maps are named as audit references but contradict FINAL_AUDIT.md:258-271 and the current code. Readers may assume candidate search is paywalled or billing is exposed, or redo fixes that are already done.
rawFindings.evidence: API_MAP.md:116 'admin bo'lmasa assertCanSearchCandidates(company) -> 402 PLAN_FEATURE_LOCKED'; API_MAP.md:179 'GET /api/plans ... ochiq qolgan'; ROUTE_MAP.md:117 '/pricing | admin.routes.ts:483, billing.routes.ts:155'; current admin.routes.ts:517 url "/profile"; candidates.routes.ts:24 '402 ... olib tashlandi'; server.ts:253.

rawFindings.fixRisk: None (docs).

rawFindings.title: Telegram is still a login channel (login button, API, bot confirm flow, FAQ)
rawFindings.rootCause: The ISSUE-010 fix hardened Telegram login with a bot confirm button instead of removing it. The new owner rule says Telegram is only for verification, recovery and linking.
rawFindings.impact: Violates rule A. A linked Telegram account can open a full session. Once Telegram recovery exists, the same identity would be both a login and a recovery factor. Users are told to rely on it in place of password recovery.
rawFindings.evidence: auth.routes.ts:137-158 /api/auth/telegram/start and /poll issue tokens via telegramLogin. telegram.service.ts:112-190 and 283-321 run the lg payload and lgok/lgno callbacks. SocialLogin.tsx:145-154 renders the Telegram button on /login. FAQ: messages.uz.ts:465, ru.ts:467 and en.ts:459 say 'sign in with Telegram on the sign-in page'. Bot not_linked text (telegram.service.ts:165-169) says linking lets you log in via Telegram.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Remove /api/auth/telegram/start and /poll, telegramLogin, the loginTokens map, handleLoginStart and handleCallbackQuery lg*. Remove the showTelegram button and tg* i18n strings. Rewrite the password FAQ in all 3 locales to describe Telegram-based recovery.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-010 (FIXED as phishing hardening, now contradicts rule A); ISSUE-122/D-039
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low. Only accounts that used Telegram login are affected, and they still have email+password or Google.

rawFindings.title: No password recovery or change flow; 'Forgot password' and settings point to /support
rawFindings.rootCause: Recovery was deferred (D-010) and has not been built. No reset challenge, token model, bot payload handler or change-password endpoint exists.
rawFindings.impact: Rule B is not implemented, so rules I and J are moot. A candidate who forgets a password loses resume, applications and chats unless support intervenes by hand. There is no in-app password change after a suspected compromise.
rawFindings.evidence: login/+Page.tsx:82-87 links 'Parolni unutdingizmi?' to /support. AccountSettings.tsx:88 password row links to /support. auth.routes.ts only has register, login, refresh, logout, me, telegram/start, telegram/poll and google; there is no reset or change route. telegram.service.ts handleStart (243-281) knows only link and login payloads. ISSUE-012 still NOT FIXED.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: No new pages. Add a recover mode on /login (AuthShell, ?mode=recover): phone -> POST /api/auth/recovery/start (rate limited, generic response). Create a hashed, one-time, 10-minute challenge in the DB and return a t.me link with a random rc payload. Bot checks that from.id matches the linked chat/phone, then issues a one-time site return link. Set the new password, bump tokenVersion, revoke all challenges, audit. Put change-password in the /profile?tab=settings security group.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium. Needs a new persisted challenge collection. In-memory maps (current bot tokens) do not survive restarts or multiple replicas.

rawFindings.title: Telegram link deep link binds on click with no confirmation: attacker gets victim's verified phone, victim's link is silently removed
rawFindings.rootCause: The link token is a bearer token for the attacker's account. The bot links whichever Telegram chat opens it and offers phone sharing without saying which site account is being linked (the confirmation added for ISSUE-010 covers login only).
rawFindings.impact: One-click phishing ('verify your ISH BOR! phone'). The victim's Telegram and phone become the verified identity of the attacker's account, which bypasses the anti-spam gate and shows the victim's number to employers on fake applications. The victim's own account is silently unlinked. This breaks rules D, E and F and would undermine Telegram-based recovery.
rawFindings.evidence: telegram.routes.ts:33 creates a link token for any logged-in user. telegram.service.ts:262-273: verifyLinkToken, then updateMany clears telegramChatId on other accounts, sets it on the token owner, and replies 'Hisobingiz bog'landi' with the contact keyboard (275-280). No account is shown and nothing is confirmed. handleContact 333-343 writes phone and isPhoneVerified=true to the account linked to the chat. Compare the login flow at 174-189, which shows the email and asks to confirm.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: In the bot, show a masked account identifier with Confirm/Deny inline buttons before linking. Refuse, rather than steal, when the Telegram identity is already linked to another account. Confirm phone sharing again on that screen. Write security events for link and phone verification.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-010 (same class fixed only for login)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low. Adds one bot round-trip to linking.

rawFindings.title: Verified phone is not unique and survives unlink/relink, so one phone can verify many accounts
rawFindings.rootCause: Phone verification is a boolean on User with no uniqueness claim. Unlinking or moving a Telegram chat never clears phone or isPhoneVerified on the account it came from.
rawFindings.impact: Rule E (unique primary phone) and rule F (one Telegram identity per account) are not enforced. Multiple candidate or spam accounts can carry the same verified phone, which defeats the anti-fake-application purpose. Phone-based recovery would be ambiguous: which account does a phone recover?
rawFindings.evidence: handleContact telegram.service.ts:339-343 saves the phone with no lookup for other users holding it. schema.prisma:163 phone String? has no unique index. telegram.routes.ts:38-44 DELETE /api/telegram/link clears only telegramChatId. Relink (telegram.service.ts:269-272) nulls the old account's chat but leaves its isPhoneVerified=true and phone. Path: verify on account A, unlink or relink to B, share contact on B, and both are verified with the same number.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Store a normalized phone in a separate claim collection with a unique key (Mongo nulls rule out a plain unique index on User.phone). Reject verification when the phone is claimed by another account, and route that user to manual recovery. Define unlink policy: keep the claim, or clear verification plus audit. Add a migration check for existing duplicates.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium. Existing duplicate phones need a data review before enforcing.

rawFindings.title: No phone change or backup phone flow; verified phone is locked forever and 'additionalPhone' is unverified free text
rawFindings.rootCause: The profile API only lets an unverified user write the phone. Nothing ever resets verification. The backup number is a plain profile string.
rawFindings.impact: A candidate who changes number cannot update the verified primary phone (rule G), and there is no verified, unique backup phone usable for recovery (rule F). The only real way to change the phone is uncontrolled: link another Telegram account and share its contact, which overwrites the phone with no security event, audit or session policy.
rawFindings.evidence: profile.routes.ts:59-67 writes phone only when !isPhoneVerified. PersonalInfo.tsx:167-175 renders the verified phone as a locked field with no change action. additionalPhone is free text: profile.routes.ts:16,74, PersonalInfo.tsx:191-203, schema.prisma:217. admin.routes.ts only reads isPhoneVerified (176). telegram.service.ts:339-343 overwrites the phone on any contact share.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: No new pages. In the /profile?tab=telegram panel (TelegramConnect variant=panel) add 'Change primary phone' and 'Add backup phone'. Each starts a Telegram challenge (one-time payload) and becomes active only after contact share from the linked identity. Enforce uniqueness, write audit events, and bump tokenVersion if the risk policy requires. Relabel additionalPhone as contact-only or migrate it to a verified backup.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium. Touches the verification model shared with the apply gate.

rawFindings.title: Manual recovery (rule H) impossible: only a Telegram-relayed contact form, no persisted request, no admin action
rawFindings.rootCause: Account recovery was never modeled. Support is a fire-and-forget Telegram message, and the admin panel has no ownership-verification or phone-reset tooling.
rawFindings.impact: A candidate who has lost password, phone and Telegram has no path the admin panel can act on. If the Telegram bot or admin chat is down or unconfigured, the request cannot be sent at all (503), which also contradicts rule K. Admins cannot trigger a verified phone reset or forced session invalidation with audit.
rawFindings.evidence: support.routes.ts:19-29 subjects have no account-recovery option. Lines 121-147 only send to TELEGRAM_ADMIN_CHAT_ID: nothing is stored, and it returns 503 SUPPORT_OFFLINE when unconfigured and 502 on send failure. admin.routes.ts only has block (revokeUserSessions at 200) and role change (223); there is no recovery or phone reset endpoint. FAQ messages.uz.ts:465 sends users to /contact.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add an 'account_recovery' subject that always persists a RecoveryRequest (status, contact email, evidence text, IP hash), independent of Telegram. List requests in the existing /admin/users area with an approve action. Approval clears the phone claim and Telegram link, bumps tokenVersion and writes an audit event. Admins never see or set passwords or tokens.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low to medium. New collection and admin UI section inside existing pages.

rawFindings.title: No security audit log for phone verification, Telegram link/unlink or session invalidation
rawFindings.rootCause: No audit or security event model or writer exists. Security-relevant state changes are plain Prisma updates.
rawFindings.impact: Rule L is violated. Phishing-driven links, silent phone overwrites and session revocations cannot be investigated or shown to the user, and manual recovery has no trail.
rawFindings.evidence: A grep for 'audit|security|recovery' in schema.prisma finds nothing. The model list (User ... PushSubscription) has no event model. Phone verified: telegram.service.ts:340-343. Link and silent unlink: 269-273. Unlink: telegram.routes.ts:38-44. Session revoke on logout, block and role (auth.service.ts:166-173, admin.routes.ts:200,223). All are unlogged apart from occasional logger warnings.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add a SecurityEvent collection {userId, type, actorUserId, createdAt, ipHash, meta} indexed by [userId, createdAt]. Write it at phone_verified, backup_phone_added, phone_changed, telegram_linked/unlinked, recovery_started/completed, sessions_invalidated and manual_recovery_approved. Never store passwords, tokens or message bodies. Show recent events in /profile?tab=settings.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low. Additive.

rawFindings.title: Google login auto-merges into an existing email account that was never verified (pre-account takeover)
rawFindings.rootCause: googleLogin trusts the email match and issues tokens for the existing user, even though password signups never verify email.
rawFindings.impact: An attacker registers victim@gmail.com with a password. The victim later uses 'Continue with Google' on /login or /signup, fills in resume and applies. The attacker's password still works, exposing resume, applications and chats. This breaks the owner rule on unsafe Google merge.
rawFindings.evidence: auth.service.ts:222-226: an existing email leads to assertNotBlocked and issueTokens, with no check of isEmailVerified or any link consent. registerUser (37-73) creates accounts with isEmailVerified false and no verification flow. signup/+Page.tsx:143 passes a role, but an existing account wins regardless. Documented as accepted risk in D-011; ISSUE-042 PARTIAL.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: If the existing account has isEmailVerified=false and a password, do not auto-merge. Either require a password login and then explicit linking, or on first Google sign-in invalidate the password, bump tokenVersion, set isEmailVerified=true and write an audit event. Store googleSub and match on it afterwards.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium. Legitimate users who registered with a password and later use Google may need to reset a password, which depends on the Telegram recovery flow being built.

rawFindings.title: Candidates are listed to every employer by default: any resume save publishes it, open-to-work defaults true, and no employer phone gate
rawFindings.rootCause: Publication is a side effect of saving, and visibility defaults to discoverable. D-012 hid contacts but left names and full resumes open to any employer with a company.
rawFindings.impact: A candidate who only wants to apply privately is still exposed: full name, headline, region, desired salary and complete work and education history can be paged by any self-registered employer who has not verified a phone (up to 200x50 profiles). Whether this counts as 'private data' is an owner decision (inference).
rawFindings.evidence: resume.routes.ts:140 sets status 'published' on every PUT, including saving one skill. schema.prisma:219 isOpenToWork defaults to true. candidates.routes.ts:34 preHandler is only requireAuth plus role employer/admin (company required at 37), with no requirePhoneVerified. Lines 47-51 filter published and open-to-work; 122-160 return name, headline, region, desiredSalary, experience and education. The only UI hint is 'Ish beruvchilar sizni topa olishi uchun' (messages.uz.ts:601).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Make discoverability an explicit opt-in (isOpenToWork default false, or a consent step in ResumeWizard showing 'visible to employers'). Separate 'resume saved' from 'published'. Require requirePhoneVerified, or a verified company, for /api/candidates.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium. Changing defaults shrinks the employer candidate pool; existing profiles need a migration decision.

rawFindings.title: Telegram outage or missing bot token dead-ends applying; UI never says verification is temporarily unavailable
rawFindings.rootCause: Core candidate actions hard-require a Telegram-verified phone. Bot availability is exposed but ignored by the UI, and the bot token is optional with no production warning.
rawFindings.impact: When the bot is down or unconfigured, unverified candidates cannot apply, message companies or review. They are sent to a Telegram panel whose button fails with a raw Uzbek 503 message in RU/EN. A misconfigured deploy blocks the main candidate funnel silently.
rawFindings.evidence: requirePhoneVerified (auth-guard.ts:90-103) is used by applications.routes.ts:43, chat.routes.ts:294 and reviews.routes.ts:19. env.ts:57 has TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN optional with default ''. server.ts warns only for UPLOAD_DIR (278). telegram.routes.ts:20 returns botUsername null, but TelegramConnect.tsx never checks it: connect is enabled and line 85 shows the API message. ApplyCard.tsx:142 shows PhoneGateNotice with no unavailability state.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Return verificationAvailable in /api/telegram/status. TelegramConnect and PhoneGateNotice show a localized 'verification temporarily unavailable' and disable connect. Warn or fail startup in production when the Telegram token is missing. No email fallback.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-115 (FIXED, related status-failure handling); ISSUE-073 for untranslated API messages
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Plain /start does not send a link to the ISH BOR! site
rawFindings.rootCause: The welcome text was written for the link-from-profile flow and has no site URL or button.
rawFindings.impact: Rule C violation, low risk. Users who open the bot directly get no way back to the site and are told to press a profile button they cannot reach from Telegram.
rawFindings.evidence: telegram.service.ts:252-259: an empty payload sends only 'profil sahifasidan «Telegram orqali tasdiqlash» tugmasini bosing' and a support note. No WEB_ORIGIN URL and no inline url button.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add an inline keyboard url button to env.WEB_ORIGIN (plus a short text link). Keep the generic reply for invalid payloads (already safe).
rawFindings.fixRisk: Very low.

rawFindings.title: Guest login from vacancy detail (Apply/Save) and save-search loses the return target and lands on home
rawFindings.rootCause: Apply-card and save links are built with plain l('/login') instead of loginHrefWithReturn. Signup has no returnTo handling at all.
rawFindings.impact: The highest-intent guest flow (open vacancy, click Apply, log in or sign up) drops the user on / or /profile, so they have to find the vacancy again. This breaks the apply funnel.
rawFindings.evidence: VacancyDetailView.tsx:48 login: l('/login') and 49 signup: l('/signup'). These are used by the guest CTA (ApplyCard.tsx:84), save (VacancyDetailView.tsx:74) and useApplication 401 redirects (useApplication.ts:65,79). SaveSearchButton.tsx:80 l('/login'). login/+Page.tsx:34 returnTargetOr(l('/')) falls back to /. signup/+Page.tsx:34 always goes to /profile or /employer.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Use loginHrefWithReturn for the login and signup links on the detail page, save-search and the useApplication redirect. Honour returnTo in signup's done(), and carry it into Google signup.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Very low.

rawFindings.title: Candidate PDF resume is publicly downloadable without auth and never revoked
rawFindings.rootCause: Resumes share the public static /uploads/ mount with logos and covers. Access control relies only on an unguessable filename.
rawFindings.impact: Once a resume URL reaches an employer, it can be forwarded or scraped and stays valid for anyone even after rejection, a closed vacancy or the candidate turning off open-to-work. PDFs often contain phone and address.
rawFindings.evidence: server.ts:174 registers fastifyStatic at /uploads/ with no auth hook (the onSend hook at 163-172 only adds CSP and nosniff). profile.routes.ts:109 stores /uploads/resume-<32hex>.pdf. applications.routes.ts:294 returns resumeUrl to the employer. The file is removed only when replaced or deleted (119,133).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Serve resumes through an authenticated endpoint: the candidate themself, an employer with an application to their vacancy, or an admin. Use short-lived signed URLs and keep the resume- prefix out of the public static root.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium. Existing resume URLs stored in profiles need a migration or compatibility redirect.

rawFindings.title: Phone gate discovered only after clicking Apply; gate link goes to profile overview and loses the vacancy
rawFindings.rootCause: Session user data has no phone-verification flag. The apply hook does not load it, and the gate notice links to the generic /profile.
rawFindings.impact: The candidate sees an enabled Apply button, gets a 403 notice, lands on profile overview (not the Telegram tab), and after verifying has no path back to the vacancy.
rawFindings.evidence: getMe (auth.service.ts:112-129) returns no isPhoneVerified. useApplication.ts:47 loads only applications and resume, so the phase is 'ready'. The PHONE_NOT_VERIFIED 403 is mapped at useApplication.ts:78. PhoneGateNotice.tsx:13 href is l('/profile') with no ?tab=telegram and no returnTo.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Load /api/telegram/status (or add phoneVerified to /api/auth/me) in useApplication and show the gate before submit. Link to /profile?tab=telegram with returnTo, and offer 'back to vacancy' after verification.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Very low.

rawFindings.title: Vacancy detail downloads all of the candidate's applications to find one; GET /api/applications is unbounded
rawFindings.rootCause: There is no per-vacancy 'my application' endpoint, and the candidate list query has no limit.
rawFindings.impact: An active candidate with hundreds of applications downloads the full list with status history on every vacancy page view. Payload and DB work grow with activity.
rawFindings.evidence: applications.routes.ts:129-155 findMany with no take, including statusHistory, vacancy, region and company. useApplication.ts:47-49 calls fetchMyApplications on each vacancy detail mount and runs .find() for the current vacancy id.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add GET /api/vacancies/:id/my-application (indexed by the [vacancyId, jobSeekerId] unique index). Add take plus a cursor to /api/applications.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Notification center can only reach the latest 100 notifications
rawFindings.rootCause: The API has a max limit and no cursor. The web client paginates in memory over the single 100-item response.
rawFindings.impact: With alerts and status changes, active candidates exceed 100 quickly, and older notifications become unreachable (only disclosed as 'truncated').
rawFindings.evidence: notifications.routes.ts:20-23 limit max 100; 58-63 findMany with take only. lib/notifications/api.ts:4-5,22 fixed limit=100 'sahifalash yo'q'. NotificationsView.tsx:183 shows the truncated note.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add cursor pagination on (createdAt, id) using the existing [userId, createdAt] index, and page from the server in the notifications UI.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Login 'Remember me' checkbox does nothing; Apple button is a non-functional placeholder
rawFindings.rootCause: UI controls were added without backend or session support.
rawFindings.impact: Misleading security UI: unchecking 'remember' still gives a 30-day refresh cookie. A visible Apple sign-in button only says 'not connected'.
rawFindings.evidence: login/+Page.tsx:22 remember state and 73-81 checkbox are never used in handleSubmit (26-40). The refresh cookie is always maxAge 30 days (auth.routes.ts setRefreshCookie). SocialLogin.tsx:139-144 Apple button onClick only sets the 'soon' note.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Either implement (session cookie without maxAge when unchecked) or remove the checkbox. Remove the Apple button until it is supported.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Very low.

rawFindings.title: Admin takedown via 'archive' can be re-activated by the employer (moderation bypass)
rawFindings.rootCause: PATCH /api/vacancies/:id/status lets a non-admin set active from 'archived' or 'draft'. Admin moderation writes the same plain 'archived' status (admin.routes.ts:289,301-309), and blocking a user also archives. No field records who archived the vacancy or why, so an admin removal looks exactly like the owner closing it.
rawFindings.impact: An admin removes an active vacancy with the Archive button, which sits next to Reject on every active row. The employer undoes it with one Activate click, and only phone, category and location are re-checked. The admin gets no signal. This breaks the rule 'moderation bypass must be impossible'.
rawFindings.evidence: vacancies.routes.ts:240-243 allowedFrom; 245-254 only phone and placement checks; admin.routes.ts:289 moderate enum includes archived, 301-309 no moderation marker; admin/vacancies/+Page.tsx:185-186 Archive button for active rows; web lib/employer/vacancies/adapter.ts:101 activate allowed for archived; e2e-check.mjs has no admin-archive-then-employer-activate case.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Store moderation provenance (e.g. closedBy/moderatedAt, or a separate moderationState), or make admin removals use 'rejected' and drop 'archived' from /moderate. In PATCH /status, refuse non-admin activation of an admin-archived vacancy (409). Write admin moderation actions to the audit log and add an e2e test.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-024 (state machine fixed for rejected/moderation; the admin-archived path is not covered)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium: one new optional field (no Mongo migration). Existing archived rows default to employer-closed.

rawFindings.title: Verified badge survives company rename and logo change (impersonation)
rawFindings.rootCause: PUT /api/employer/company updates name, description, website, industry and region, and the logo endpoint replaces the logo, without touching isVerified. Verification is one boolean that is not tied to the identity the admin checked: no snapshot of the verified name or STIR, and no re-review when those fields change.
rawFindings.impact: An employer gets verified as a small real firm, then renames the company to a well-known brand and uploads that brand's logo. The badge stays on the company page, on vacancy cards (PUBLIC_COMPANY_CARD_SELECT.isVerified) and in the verified=1 search filter. Fake vacancies under a 'verified' brand can then collect candidate data, and the admin is never told.
rawFindings.evidence: companies.routes.ts:107-120 update data (name: body.name ...) has no isVerified handling; 146-166 logo upload does not reset it; vacancies.service.ts:44-51 cards expose isVerified; admin.routes.ts:374-394 verify only flips the boolean; admin/companies/+Page.tsx:132-133 toggle only.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: When a verified company changes name, website or logo, either reset isVerified=false (notify the owner and queue it for admin review) or hold the change as pending until approved. Snapshot the verified name and STIR. Audit-log verify and unverify.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: verified employers who rename must re-verify, so UI copy is needed.

rawFindings.title: Applications workspace limited to newest 2000 with full resumes; filters, counts and search are client-side
rawFindings.rootCause: GET /api/employer/applications returns the newest 2000 rows, each with the full resume (experience, education, skills), status history and email/phone. It has no server-side filter, search or pagination. The web page fetches once and filters, counts and paginates in memory. The per-vacancy endpoint (/api/vacancies/:id/applications, limit 500) exists but the web never calls it.
rawFindings.impact: An employer with more than 2000 applications cannot open, search or change the status of older ones. The ?vacancy= link from Vakansiyalarim and the status tab counts cover only that subset, with just a generic 'capped' note. The tracker benchmark for 5000 applications is about 3.5 s p50 and 2.6 MB, which is worse on mobile networks.
rawFindings.evidence: applications.routes.ts:29 EMPLOYER_LIST_LIMIT=2000, 194-216 full resume include, 219 take; EmployerApplicationsView.tsx:96-113 one fetch then filterApplications/statusCounts in memory, 200-202 capped note; lib/employer/applications/adapter.ts:199-227; web only calls /api/employer/applications (lib/employer/applications/api.ts:21, lib/api.ts:883).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add server-side status/vacancyId/q/period/sort parameters with cursor pagination (page size 50 or less) and a lightweight row select. Load resume, history and contacts on demand via GET /api/applications/:id with an owner check. Compute status counts with groupBy on [vacancyId, status].
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: the response shape changes, so URL state handling and e2e checks must be updated.

rawFindings.title: /api/employer/vacancies silently capped at 1000 full documents with per-row _count; edit page downloads the whole list
rawFindings.rootCause: The endpoint returns full documents (description up to 20k chars, requirements and conditions up to 10k each) for up to 1000 rows. Each row has _count.applications and the response has no total. There is no owner GET for a single vacancy, so the edit form downloads the whole list and searches it in the browser.
rawFindings.impact: With no active-vacancy limit, archived rows pile up. Past 1000, the oldest silently drop out of the dashboard and stats, and their edit page shows 'not found'. The per-row _count pattern is the one measured at about 3 s in applications.routes.ts (comment at 223-224) and replaced there, but not here. Each dashboard or edit open downloads several MB.
rawFindings.evidence: vacancies.routes.ts:93 LIMIT 1000; 126-137 include with _count and take, returns { items } only; VacancyFormView.tsx:79 fetchEmployerVacancyRecords, 87 records.find(id) then not_found; EmployerVacanciesView.tsx:81; applications.routes.ts:223-226 groupBy replacement.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add GET /api/employer/vacancies/:id using ownedVacancy. Make the list use a card select with server pagination, a status filter and a total. Get application counts via application.groupBy by vacancyId.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium: dashboard stats and filters need server totals.

rawFindings.title: Admin role change away from employer leaves vacancies live and applications orphaned
rawFindings.rootCause: PATCH /api/admin/users/:id/role updates the role and revokes sessions only. Unlike the block path (203-211), it does not archive the user's active vacancies or remove them from the search index.
rawFindings.impact: After an employer is changed to job_seeker or a staff role, their vacancies stay public and keep accepting applications. New-application notifications go to a user who can no longer reach /api/employer/* (requireRole employer/admin), so candidates wait forever. As a job_seeker, that user could even apply to their own vacancy and then review their own company.
rawFindings.evidence: admin.routes.ts:217-226 role update + revokeUserSessions only; 203-211 block path archives and calls syncVacancyIndex; applications.routes.ts:106 notify ownerUserId, 164 requireRole('employer','admin'); reviews.routes.ts:28-37 review gate is 'has applied'.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: When the role leaves employer, archive active and moderation vacancies (reuse the block logic), sync the index and call bumpDataVersion. Alternatively refuse the change while the user owns live vacancies. Audit-log role changes.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-035 / ISSUE-108 (session side fixed, data side not)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Vacancy rejection is not binding: delete and re-post goes live, and approved-after-rejection vacancies can be edited freely
rawFindings.rootCause: New vacancies publish immediately. Only a PUT on a 'rejected' vacancy sends it to 'moderation'. A PUT on an active vacancy, including one an admin just approved after resubmission, replaces title and description with no re-review. A rejected vacancy without applications can be deleted and posted again as a new, immediately active vacancy.
rawFindings.impact: An admin rejection can be undone in two requests (DELETE then POST with the same content), or by waiting for approval and then PUTting the rejected text back. There is no rejection counter or company-level flag. This conflicts with 'moderation bypass must be impossible' unless the owner explicitly accepts post-moderation.
rawFindings.evidence: vacancies.routes.ts:154-166 POST without moderation; 186 resubmit only when status==='rejected'; 188-216 edits applied directly to active rows; 279-289 delete allowed without applications; vacancies.service.ts:646-670 status active + publishedAt; DECISIONS.md:273 notes vacancies publish immediately.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Owner decision needed. Options: pre-moderate new or edited vacancies for companies with past rejections or no verification; send material edits (title/description/requirements) of previously rejected vacancies back to 'moderation'; keep a per-company rejection count and throttle re-posting the same content.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: adds admin workload and changes the employer publishing flow.

rawFindings.title: Candidates database open to any employer with a name-only company; returns full names and full resumes
rawFindings.rootCause: /api/candidates requires only the employer role and any company row (primaryCompany). It has no requirePhoneVerified, no company verification and no per-user quota. It returns first and last name, headline, region and the full latest published resume (experience with descriptions, education) for every open-to-work seeker, up to page 200 x 50.
rawFindings.impact: Anyone can sign up as an employer, create a company with just a name via PUT /api/employer/company, and page through essentially all ~10k candidates within the 600 req/min per-IP global limit. Contacts stay hidden (D-012), but names and work histories reach unvetted accounts. Whether this breaks 'candidate private data only to authorized employers' depends on the owner's definition of authorized (inference).
