rawFindings.evidence: candidates.routes.ts:34 preHandler is requireAuth + requireRole only; 37-40 company existence check; 11 MAX_PAGE=200, 68-69 skip/take up to 50; 122-161 names + resume returned; companies.routes.ts:39-47 PUT needs only name; env.ts:56 RATE_LIMIT_MAX default 600; by contrast chat.routes.ts:294 conversation start requires phone verification.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add requirePhoneVerified (same gate as chat), a per-user rate limit or daily view quota, and an audit of profile views. Consider showing only the surname initial until the candidate applies or replies, and requiring a verified company for bulk browsing.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: the page already renders PhoneGateNotice for phone-gate errors.

rawFindings.title: Public company reviews expose the reviewer's full name and userId, revealing that they applied
rawFindings.rootCause: Posting a review requires a prior application to that company. The public GET /api/companies/:slug returns each review's userId and the author's first and last name, and the UI renders the full name.
rawFindings.impact: Anyone, including the employer, learns that a named candidate applied to this company. The employer can match the reviewer to its applications list and retaliate. The stable userId links the same person across companies. Candidates have no anonymous option.
rawFindings.evidence: reviews.routes.ts:28-37 hasApplied gate; companies.routes.ts:191-203 selects userId and jobSeekerProfile names; web CompanyReviews.tsx:176 name = review.authorName; DECISIONS.md:183-186 (D-017) kept userId to detect 'my review'.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Compute 'mine' on the server from optional auth (or a separate mine endpoint) instead of returning userId. Show authors as first name + initial (or 'Nomzod') by default, with opt-in to the full name.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: 'mine' detection moves server-side.

rawFindings.title: Employer conversation list is unbounded and aggregates the whole message history on every load
rawFindings.rootCause: GET /api/conversations has no take or cursor. It loads every conversation with the company description, finds each last message by aggregating over all messages of all conversations ($match $in, $sort, $group), then loads every vacancy ID of the involved companies and every application of every involved seeker.
rawFindings.impact: An active employer with thousands of conversations and around 100k messages scans the full history on every /messages open or reconnect. Response size and latency grow as the platform ages.
rawFindings.evidence: chat.routes.ts:358-381 findMany without take; 122-139 lastMessages pipeline over all messages of all ids; 396-433 vacancy and application findMany without limits; 500 in-memory sort.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Store lastMessageAt and a preview on Conversation (updated in deliverMessage), index [employerUserId,lastMessageAt] and [seekerUserId,lastMessageAt], add cursor pagination, compute vacancy context only for the returned page, and drop company.description from list rows.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: denormalized fields must be kept consistent, and the client needs infinite scroll.

rawFindings.title: Candidate search uses relation filters ($lookup) and offset paging across all seeker profiles
rawFindings.rootCause: The query filters on the to-one relation user {role, isBlocked}, the to-many resumes {some: published}, and nested resumes.some.skills.some for text search. Prisma on MongoDB runs these as $lookup per JobSeekerProfile. Paging is offset-based up to page 200, and each row includes the full resume.
rawFindings.impact: Every candidates page or search runs lookups across all ~10k seeker profiles before skip/take, and deeper pages cost more. It is the same pattern the team replaced for vacancies after measuring 1.5 s dropping to 9 ms. Not benchmarked here (inference).
rawFindings.evidence: candidates.routes.ts:47-63 where with relation filters; 66-85 findMany with skip/take and nested includes; DECISIONS.md:368 benchmark for replacing relation filters.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Denormalize an isDiscoverable flag (open to work + published resume + not blocked) plus search text and skills on JobSeekerProfile, index [isDiscoverable, regionId, updatedAt], use keyset pagination, and return a summary per row with the resume loaded on demand.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: the flag must be updated on resume publish, block and open-to-work changes.

rawFindings.title: Vacancies never expire: expiresAt is never set and no job archives stale listings
rawFindings.rootCause: Vacancy.expiresAt exists in the schema but is never written by createVacancy, PUT or PATCH, and no job archives old vacancies. A vacancy stays active until the employer closes it.
rawFindings.impact: With tens of thousands of vacancies, abandoned listings stay searchable, keep collecting applications nobody reads, inflate public counts and facets, and JobPosting has no validThrough.
rawFindings.evidence: schema.prisma:429 expiresAt; vacancies.service.ts:647-671 create data has no expiresAt; the field is only read in VACANCY_CARD_SELECT (vacancies.service.ts:92); no sweep in the alerts or admin modules.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Set expiresAt on publish and re-activation (e.g. +30/60 days). Add a daily sweep, reusing the alerts timer, that archives expired vacancies. Warn the employer before expiry with a one-click extend, and emit validThrough.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium: currently active vacancies need a backfill policy.

rawFindings.title: Admin vacancy moderation search uses a company relation filter and per-row _count
rawFindings.rootCause: Admin text search is OR [title contains, company {name contains}]. The company relation filter runs as $lookup over all vacancies, both in findMany and in count, and each row adds _count.applications.
rawFindings.impact: Moderation searches slow down as vacancies grow into tens of thousands, with two full lookup scans per search. Admin-only; not benchmarked (inference).
rawFindings.evidence: admin.routes.ts:239-259 where with company relation filter, findMany + count, _count at 255; the fixed pattern for public search is vacancies.service.ts:169-198 resolveFilterIds.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Resolve company names to IDs first (as resolveFilterIds does), filter with companyId in, and replace _count with groupBy.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Application status changes are unrestricted, and the reason message skips the phone-verification gate
rawFindings.rootCause: PATCH /api/applications/:id/status accepts viewed/invited/rejected/accepted from any current status; only an identical repeat is skipped. A reason is delivered as a chat message via getOrCreateConversation + deliverMessage without the requirePhoneVerified check that /api/conversations/start enforces.
rawFindings.impact: A candidate can receive 'Qabul qilindingiz' followed by 'Ko'rildi', or repeated rejected/accepted flips, each with a notification or email. An employer without a verified phone can open a chat with any applicant through the reason field.
rawFindings.evidence: applications.routes.ts:20-23 status enum; 311 preHandler has no phone gate; 328-330 only equality check; 350-354 conversation + message; chat.routes.ts:294 start requires requirePhoneVerified; ApplicationSidebar.tsx:83-90 offers every status.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Define allowed transitions (no going back to 'viewed'; confirm before reversing a final state). Apply requirePhoneVerified when a reason is sent.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Admin approval skips placement rules, can publish private drafts, and does not notify the employer
rawFindings.rootCause: /api/admin/vacancies/:id/moderate sets status 'active' from any state, including an employer's draft, without calling assertVacancyPlacement. It notifies the owner only on rejection.
rawFindings.impact: An admin can publish incomplete legacy vacancies (no category or workplaceType) or unfinished drafts. An employer whose resubmitted vacancy is approved is never told it went live.
rawFindings.evidence: admin.routes.ts:289 status enum; 301-309 update with no placement check; 314-322 notify only when rejected; admin/vacancies/+Page.tsx:175-178 Activate shown for every non-active row, drafts included.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Run assertVacancyPlacement on admin activation, block or confirm draft-to-active, and notify the owner on approval and archive with the reason.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Rejected or moderation vacancies with applications cannot be closed or deleted by the employer; delete check is not atomic
rawFindings.rootCause: The owner can archive only from 'active', and DELETE is refused when applications exist. A vacancy that collected applications while active and was then rejected (or resubmitted to moderation) can therefore be neither closed nor deleted. DELETE counts applications and then deletes without a transaction.
rawFindings.impact: The vacancy stays stuck in the dashboard until an admin acts. In a rare race, an application created between the count and the delete is cascade-deleted.
rawFindings.evidence: vacancies.routes.ts:240 archived allowed only from active; 279-289 count then delete; web lib/employer/vacancies/adapter.ts:97-104 close offered only for active.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Allow owners to move rejected or moderation vacancies to archived. Make delete conditional, either inside a transaction or by re-checking after marking the vacancy as deleting.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: PUT /api/vacancies/:id has no phone-verification gate while POST and re-activation do
rawFindings.rootCause: The PUT preHandler is requireAuth + requireRole only. POST (156) and PATCH to active (249) call requirePhoneVerified.
rawFindings.impact: An account whose phone is not verified, or no longer verified (for example during the new phone-change flow in rule G), can rewrite the content of a live vacancy.
rawFindings.evidence: vacancies.routes.ts:156 POST gate; 171 PUT without gate; 249 PATCH gate; the web form already handles PHONE_NOT_VERIFIED (VacancyForm.tsx:224).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add requirePhoneVerified to PUT, at least when the vacancy is active.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Remote vacancies can never keep a location, and API still accepts employmentType 'remote' with any workplaceType
rawFindings.rootCause: toVacancyPayload sends regionId null on edit and undefined on create when the vacancy is remote, and the form hides the region field. The API createSchema still accepts employmentType 'remote' together with office or hybrid.
rawFindings.impact: The rule makes location optional for remote, but the web makes it impossible and erases a stored region on any edit. API clients can store contradictory office + employmentType remote rows, which the remote filter and facets count as remote.
rawFindings.evidence: form.ts:34 isRegionRequired, 209 regionId null/undefined; vacancies.routes.ts:63 employmentType enum includes remote; vacancies.service.ts:128-131 employmentWhere ORs employmentType and workplaceType.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Show an optional region field for remote and omit regionId when unchanged. Reject employmentType 'remote' unless workplaceType is remote on new or updated rows.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Company verification has no evidence data, request flow or unverify notice
rawFindings.rootCause: The web saves companies through PUT /api/employer/company, whose schema has no legalName or STIR. POST /api/companies accepts them but the web never calls it. The admin list shows name, owner email and legacy plan only. Employers have no 'request verification' state, and unverify sends no notice or reason.
rawFindings.impact: Admins verify on the name alone, employers cannot ask for verification, and legacy billing columns still show in the admin companies list.
rawFindings.evidence: companies.routes.ts:30-37 POST schema with legalName/stir vs 39-47 PUT schema; no POST /api/companies call in apps/web/src/lib; admin.routes.ts:346-366 list fields incl. subscriptionPlan; 384-392 notify only on verify.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Capture legalName and STIR in PUT (or a verification-request endpoint with a pending state), show them to admins, notify on unverify with a reason, and audit-log changes.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Company form offers SVG logos that the API rejects; PUT accepts whitespace-only company name
rawFindings.rootCause: The file input's accept list includes image/svg+xml although the API accepts only PNG, JPG and WebP. The PUT schema's name is z.string().min(1) without trim, while POST uses trim().min(2).
rawFindings.impact: Users can pick an SVG and then get a server error after uploading. API clients can save a blank-looking company name that appears on vacancy cards.
rawFindings.evidence: EmployerCompanyForm.tsx:154 accept includes image/svg+xml; companies.routes.ts:158 saveUpload allows png/jpg/webp; companies.routes.ts:40 name min(1) vs 31 trim().min(2).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Remove image/svg+xml from accept, and use trim().min(2) for the PUT name.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Very low

rawFindings.title: Application 'source' is client-controlled, so the 'via Telegram' chip can be spoofed
rawFindings.rootCause: applySchema lets the candidate send source 'telegram'. No Telegram flow creates applications; the only application.create is in this route.
rawFindings.impact: The 'via Telegram' chip in the employer workspace and any source statistics are unreliable. Low impact.
rawFindings.evidence: applications.routes.ts:17 source enum from body, 88 stored; ApplicationDetail.tsx:213-218 renders the chip; web lib/api.ts:206 always sends 'site'.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Drop source from the request body and set it on the server per channel.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Very low

rawFindings.title: /employer/@slug still permanently redirects any unknown segment to /companies/<segment>
rawFindings.rootCause: The guard throws redirect(301) for any /employer/<x> that is not a static employer page.
rawFindings.impact: Typos and future employer sections (e.g. /employer/company) get a cached 301 to a 404 company page.
rawFindings.evidence: +guard.ts:12-16 unconditional redirect(localizeHref('/companies/'+slug), 301).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Return 404 for reserved employer segments, or use 302 and check that the slug exists.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: All SSR API calls share one per-IP rate-limit bucket (600/min), so crawling 20k public pages or moderate traffic produces 429s
rawFindings.rootCause: @fastify/rate-limit is global, max RATE_LIMIT_MAX (default 600/min), keyed on req.ip. It has no keyGenerator, allowList or route exemption. Web SSR loaders call the API with plain fetch and forward no client identity. Every render therefore counts against the web server's egress IP: home 4 calls, /vacancies 2, vacancy or company detail 2. The traffic figures are an inference from code, not a measurement.
rawFindings.impact: Self-hosted web has a single egress IP, so the budget is about 10 API calls/s for all visitors and crawlers combined, i.e. roughly 2.5-5 page views/s. A crawler working through the ~16k vacancy and company URLs, or modest peak traffic, gets 429s. Loaders turn those into failed pages (200 + noindex per ISSUE-070). On Vercel it depends on how function instances share egress IPs (inference).
rawFindings.evidence: server.ts:129-139 rateLimit({max: env.RATE_LIMIT_MAX, timeWindow:'1 minute'}), no keyGenerator or allowList (grep). env.ts:56 default 600; .env.example:47. web lib/api.ts:75,339,359,376,390,483 fetch(`${API_URL}...`) with no forwarded headers. pages/index/+data.ts:10-21 makes 4 calls; pages/vacancies/+data.ts:15-18 and pages/vacancies/@slug/+data.ts:13 make 2 each; pages/companies/@slug/+data.ts:13-22.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Give SSR its own budget. Send a server-only secret header from SSR and in keyGenerator either key by a validated forwarded client IP or apply a much higher limit to that key. Keep strict per-IP limits on auth, apply, upload and recovery routes. Add CDN caching (s-maxage + stale-while-revalidate) for anonymous vacancy and company detail HTML to cut origin calls per crawl.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-011 (rate limit and TRUST_PROXY, PARTIAL); ISSUE-070 (API error renders 200 + noindex, NOT FIXED); ISSUE-100
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium. The SSR secret must never reach browsers, and a bad keyGenerator could let clients bypass per-IP limits.

rawFindings.title: Employer applications list still returns 2000 rows with full resumes: 3.5 s and 2.6 MB at 5000 applications
rawFindings.rootCause: One response carries up to 2000 applications, each with coverLetter, statusHistory, applicant profile and the full resume (experience, education, skills). Prisma resolves each include as a separate query with $in lists of up to 2000 IDs. There is no [vacancyId, createdAt] index (DB_MAP I4 was never added), so sorting createdAt desc over a vacancyId $in likely happens in memory (inference). Filtering and paging happen in the browser.
rawFindings.impact: Measured p50 3497 ms, cold 4085 ms, 2609 KB, with no improvement after PHASE 6. Applications older than the newest 2000 cannot be reached in the UI. GET /api/vacancies/:id/applications has the same shape with 500 rows.
rawFindings.evidence: applications.routes.ts:29 EMPLOYER_LIST_LIMIT=2000. :171-220 findMany {vacancyId in} with include vacancy/statusHistory/jobSeeker/resume{experience,education,skills}, orderBy createdAt desc, take 2000. :221 count; :225 groupBy. :259-303 per-vacancy list, take 500, full resume. schema.prisma:472-477 Application indexes, none on [vacancyId, createdAt]. FINAL_AUDIT.md 10K table.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Paginate on the server: page or cursor, pageSize up to 50, status and vacancyId filters, return items/total/hasMore. List rows should carry only id, status, createdAt, vacancy card, applicant name/avatar/headline and resume {id,title}. Add GET /api/employer/applications/:id (owner check) for resume, cover letter and history. Add @@index([vacancyId, createdAt]). Compute per-vacancy counts only for vacancies on the current page.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium. The response shape and the client-side filtering on the employer applications page change, and the e2e checks must be updated.

rawFindings.title: Candidate database runs relation-filter $lookup over every job seeker profile (p50 1972 ms at 8000 seekers)
rawFindings.rootCause: The where clause filters through relations: user {role, isBlocked} and resumes {some published}. Text search adds resumes.some.title and resumes.some.skills.some.skillName. On MongoDB, Prisma runs these as $lookup stages for every profile before $match, then sorts by userId and applies skip (up to 199x50). Includes load the full resume sections. The cause is read from the query shape; no explain was run.
rawFindings.impact: Page 1 without text measured p50 1972 ms. Cost follows the total number of seekers, not the page size. The text variant adds a nested $lookup into resume_skills and was not benchmarked, so it is likely slower (inference). Every employer search and every 'show more' click waits about 2 s or more.
rawFindings.evidence: candidates.routes.ts:47-63 where uses user and resumes relation filters and an OR over resumes.some(title|skills.some). :66-85 findMany with skip/take, orderBy userId, include resumes{skills,experience,education}. :16 page max 200. schema.prisma:207-225 JobSeekerProfile indexes: [regionId] and unique userId only, no isOpenToWork index. FINAL_AUDIT.md Performance: open heavy point, cause unconfirmed.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Resolve IDs first: distinct jobSeekerId from published resumes (Resume [status] index), plus the small set of blocked job-seeker userIds. Then query profiles by id in [...] with isOpenToWork and regionId, using keyset pagination on userId. Longer term, denormalize JobSeekerProfile.isSearchable (updated on resume publish/hide/delete and user block) with @@index([isSearchable, isOpenToWork, userId]). For text, resolve matching jobSeekerIds from resumes and skills first and cap the set.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: None (listed in FINAL_AUDIT Performance without an ID); privacy rules from ISSUE-007/008 must stay
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium. The denormalized flag can drift and needs a backfill. The contactable/privacy logic must not change.

rawFindings.title: Filtered and text facets are uncached: 7 aggregations on every /vacancies filter change, one of them over all active vacancies (not benchmarked)
rawFindings.rootCause: Only facets with no filters at all are cached. Any filtered request runs resolveFilterIds plus 5 groupBy and 2 count queries. Each dimension drops its own filter, so the groupBy for the filtered dimension scans every active vacancy. With text, all 7 queries repeat the regex OR over title, description and requirements.
rawFindings.impact: /vacancies SSR fetches list and facets together on every filter, sort, page or text change. The cold unfiltered facets took 602 ms at 14,427 active vacancies. A one-filter request includes at least one full-set groupBy, so similar cost is likely, and text facets could be several times the 306 ms text list (inference; not measured). Crawlers following filter URLs hit the same path.
rawFindings.evidence: vacancies.service.ts:430-447 computeFacets runs Promise.all of 5 groupBy + 2 count using where(except). :249-272 regex contains on description. :508 cached() only for the unfiltered case; :528-530 isUnfilteredQuery switch. web pages/vacancies/+data.ts:15-18 fetches page and facets in parallel. FINAL_AUDIT.md benchmarks only /api/vacancies/facets with no params (602 ms cold, 2 ms p50).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add a keyedCache for facets keyed by normalized filter params (e.g. 60 s, 500 keys) with stale-while-revalidate. Collapse the 7 round trips into one aggregateRaw $facet pipeline behind a shared first $match. On the client, reuse existing facets when only page or sort changed. For text, compute facets from a capped set of matched IDs, or use Meilisearch facets when it is enabled.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-048 (PARTIAL); ISSUE-138 (unfiltered facets cache, FIXED); D-033
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low for the cache (counts up to 60 s stale). Medium for the $facet rewrite, which must keep the exclude-own-dimension semantics covered by e2e.

rawFindings.title: One global cache version: every vacancy, company or review write clears the catalog, facets, salary and home caches
rawFindings.rootCause: All in-process caches check a single global version. bumpDataVersion() is called on vacancy create (active), every PUT including draft edits, status change, delete, company profile or logo save, company create, review create/delete, and admin block/moderate/verify/review actions. One write invalidates all 200 catalog keys, unfiltered facets, the 5-minute salary dataset and home stats together.
rawFindings.impact: With about 2000 employers editing during the day, the caches will often be cold. The next visitor then pays the benchmark's cold times: catalog ~0.75 s, facets ~0.6 s, salary dataset ~0.57 s. The 1-9 ms p50 values assume repeated identical requests with no writes in between. Draft edits clear public caches even though nothing public changed. The write rate is an inference.
rawFindings.evidence: cache.ts:14-17 single `version` and bumpDataVersion; :24-44 keyedCache and :46-60 cached both compare against it. Callers: vacancies.routes.ts:219 (PUT, unconditional), :265, :291; vacancies.service.ts:675-678; companies.routes.ts:122,140,162,177,260; reviews.routes.ts:65,94; admin.routes.ts:210,312,382,447,454. FINAL_AUDIT.md 'Keyin cold' column vs p50.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Keep separate versions per dependency (active vacancy fields, company profile, reviews). Bump only when a public field of an active record changes, so PUT on a draft or moderation vacancy does not bump. Serve stale values while refreshing in the background once per key, so writes never force a synchronous cold load. With more than one API instance, use a shared store or accept TTL-only staleness.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-125 (application writes no longer bump, FIXED); ISSUE-049; ISSUE-051; ISSUE-052; D-034
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium. Staleness windows grow slightly, and a missed dependency leaves a stale catalog after a rename.

rawFindings.title: Conversation list is unpaginated: 523 ms p50, 1148 ms p95, 498 KB at 500 conversations; the seeker path can build very large vacancy-ID $in lists
rawFindings.rootCause: All of the user's conversations are loaded with the company's full description (up to 2000 chars) and region. The last message and unread counts are then aggregated over all of them. For vacancy context, every vacancy ID of every involved company is loaded, then applications for those seekers x vacancies. The result is sorted in Node. There is no limit or cursor, and Conversation has no lastMessageAt field to sort or page by.
rawFindings.impact: Measured 523 ms p50, 1148 ms p95, 498 KB for an employer with 500 conversations; the employer's own company description repeats in every row. A seeker talking to large companies can produce thousands of IDs in the $in (not benchmarked). The web refetches the whole list on WS reconnect and whenever a message arrives for a conversation not yet in the list.
rawFindings.evidence: chat.routes.ts:358-381 findMany OR employer/seeker, include company{description,region}. :384 and :122-139 lastMessages aggregate over all IDs. :385-391 unread groupBy. :398-405 vacancy.findMany {companyId in all companies}. :406-433 applications. :500 in-memory sort. web lib/messages/useMessenger.ts:175, :221 reloadList(true). FINAL_AUDIT.md /api/conversations row.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Denormalize Conversation.lastMessageAt and a last-message preview/sender, written in deliverMessage. Add @@index([employerUserId, lastMessageAt]) and [seekerUserId, lastMessageAt], and return take 30 with a keyset cursor. Drop company.description from list rows (the side panel already has /api/users/:id/summary). For vacancy context, query applications by jobSeekerId (indexed) and match companyId in memory. Compute unread counts only for the returned page.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium. Needs a schema field plus backfill, and the messenger must support 'load more' while still bumping new conversations to the top.

rawFindings.title: Header counters poll every 20 s and 45 s per tab even though WebSocket already pushes; the employer summary re-reads all owned vacancy IDs each time
rawFindings.rootCause: Each logged-in tab polls /api/inbox/summary every 20 s plus on focus and INBOX_CHANGED. It also polls /api/notifications?limit=30 every 45 s plus on focus, although the socket delivers messages and notifications. For employers, each summary call re-resolves owned companies, all owned vacancy IDs and a count of 'sent' applications. The bell fetches a 30-item list plus count instead of the existing unread-count endpoint.
rawFindings.impact: Roughly 4-5 authenticated requests per open tab per minute, each with an extra requireAuth user read. The employer summary measured 125 ms p50 and 735 ms cold with 500 vacancies. This constant background load grows with open tabs and with vacancies per employer (traffic figures are inference). The notification list is about 8 KB per poll.
rawFindings.evidence: web lib/useInboxSummary.ts:45 setInterval(refresh, 20000); :47-49 focus and INBOX_CHANGED listeners. lib/useNotifications.ts:48,68 fetchNotificationsStrict every 45_000 ms. lib/apiExtra.ts:192-195 fetchUnreadCount exists. API chat.routes.ts:676-693 conversation findMany + message.count + ownedVacancyIds + application.count. ownership.ts:10-19; auth-guard.ts:52 findUnique per request. FINAL_AUDIT.md inbox summary row.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Push counter deltas over the existing WebSocket (new message, application, notification) and resync on reconnect. Poll only while the socket is closed, with backoff, and pause while document.hidden. Use /api/notifications/unread-count for the bell and load the list only when the menu opens. Cache an employer's owned vacancy IDs for about 60 s (invalidated on vacancy create/delete) or keep a per-company newApplications counter.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium. Counters can drift if events are missed, so keep a slow fallback poll and a refresh on focus.

rawFindings.title: Companies catalog $lookup pipeline still runs on every cold request, every cursor page and every company page (/similar is never cached)
rawFindings.rootCause: Two $lookup sub-pipelines (approved reviews; active vacancies grouped) run for every company matching the base filter, before $sort/$limit, because the sort key is built from them. Only the exact query string is cached for 60 s. A cursor page re-runs the full pipeline and then applies $match on the cursor. /api/companies/:slug/similar calls listCompanies directly with no cache, and saved=1 is never cached.
rawFindings.impact: First catalog page cold: 754-767 ms with 2000 companies and 20k vacancies. Each 'load more', and every company page SSR (which fetches /similar in parallel), pays a similar cost for an industry group or region that can include most companies (not benchmarked). Cost grows linearly with companies and vacancies.
rawFindings.evidence: companies.list.ts:274-318 computed $lookup on company_reviews and vacancies. :330-337 order is computed -> $set _sort -> $sort/$limit. :342-347 cursor branch. :381-397 similarCompanies -> listCompanies. companies.routes.ts:20 catalogCache; :73-80 cache used only when saved is not set; :239-243 /similar uncached. web pages/companies/@slug/+data.ts:13-22. FINAL_AUDIT.md catalog rows.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Denormalize Company.activeVacancyCount, activeVacancyViews, ratingAvg, reviewCount and hasRemote/hasOffice. Update them on vacancy create/status/delete and review writes, with a periodic reconcile job, and index the sort keys together with _id. Until then, cache /similar per slug (e.g. 10 min) and include cursor pages in the keyed cache.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium for denormalization (counter drift, backfill). Low for caching /similar.

rawFindings.title: Message history returns 1000 messages without a cursor, and its sort tiebreaker is not in the index
rawFindings.rootCause: The newest 1000 messages with full bodies come back in one response, with no before-cursor. orderBy is [createdAt desc, id desc], but the index is [conversationId, createdAt]; id is not in it, so MongoDB likely runs a blocking top-k sort over every message in the conversation (inference; no explain for this query). Each open also runs an updateMany for read marks.
rawFindings.impact: Measured 45 ms p50 and 252 KB for a 5000-message conversation. Cost and memory grow linearly with conversation length and body size: bodies can be up to 4000 chars, so 1000 rows can reach ~4 MB. The client keeps every opened thread in memory.
rawFindings.evidence: chat.routes.ts:158 MESSAGES_LIMIT=1000. :523-527 findMany where conversationId, orderBy [{createdAt:'desc'},{id:'desc'}], take 1000. :512-515 updateMany isRead. :70 body.slice(0,4000). schema.prisma:554 @@index([conversationId, createdAt]). FINAL_AUDIT.md row 'suhbat tarixi (5000 xabar)'.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Sort by id alone (effectively time-ordered) or add @@index([conversationId, createdAt, id]). Page with take 50 and ?before=<messageId>, loading older pages on scroll. Skip the read updateMany when the list already shows 0 unread for the conversation.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium. The client must merge pages with optimistic unsent messages.

rawFindings.title: Vacancy text search scans descriptions twice with regex (list + count); sort orders and deep pages are not covered by indexes
rawFindings.rootCause: Without Meilisearch (MEILI_HOST defaults to empty), each search term is a case-insensitive regex OR over title, description and requirements across all active vacancies, and count() runs the same filter again. resolveFilterIds also runs a regex over all company and category names per term. Every sort ends with id, which no Vacancy index includes. Popular and salary sorts have no index. skip can reach 49,950.
rawFindings.impact: Text search measured p50 306 ms (down from 3505). Both scans read full descriptions (up to 20k chars) of ~14k active vacancies, so latency grows with active count and description length. Deep pages, popular, salary_asc and multi-term text were not benchmarked. The alerts sweep calls listVacancies for each saved search.
rawFindings.evidence: vacancies.service.ts:249-272 contains/insensitive on description and requirements. :180-188 company/category name regex per term. :276-289 DATE_ORDER and SORT_ORDERS end with id. :318 and :401-412 findMany and count in parallel. :325 salary order. vacancies.routes.ts:45 page capped at 1000. schema.prisma:440-446 Vacancy indexes. env.ts:79 MEILI_HOST default ''.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Turn on Meilisearch in production (already implemented), or add a normalized searchText field (as articles have) with a text index instead of regex on description. Add indexes that match the sorts: [status,isPremium,publishedAt,id], [status,publishedAt,id], [status,viewsCount,publishedAt,id], [status,isPremium,salaryMin,id]. Cap anonymous pages at about 100, and reuse page 1's total instead of recounting on later pages.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low for indexes (watch build time on first deploy). Medium for replacing regex, since substring vs word matching changes results.

rawFindings.title: Similar vacancies (fetched on every vacancy detail SSR) only has a [categoryId] index, so it sorts all vacancies in the category in memory
rawFindings.rootCause: The query filters {status:'active', id != base, categoryId}, sorts by publishedAt desc then id desc, take 40. The only index containing categoryId is [categoryId], so MongoDB fetches every vacancy in the category (any status, full document) and top-k sorts them. The company fallback query also sorts in memory on [companyId, status].
rawFindings.impact: Every detail SSR calls /similar alongside the detail. With 20k vacancies and a small category catalog, one category can hold thousands of documents, all read on each view and on each crawler hit (inference; /similar is not in the benchmark, while the detail itself measured 9 ms).
rawFindings.evidence: vacancies.service.ts:592-598 findMany where status/id not/categoryId, orderBy publishedAt desc, id desc, take 40. :610-615 companyId fallback. schema.prisma:445 @@index([categoryId]); :444 [companyId, status]. web pages/vacancies/@slug/+data.ts:13; lib/api.ts:390.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add @@index([categoryId, status, publishedAt]) and [companyId, status, publishedAt] so only about 40 documents are fetched. Cache similar results per slug for 5-10 minutes on TTL.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low. Indexes are additive, and a cached list may show a just-closed vacancy briefly (its detail still returns 404).

rawFindings.title: Admin vacancy and user search use relation filters ($lookup per document); no createdAt index for admin sorts (not benchmarked)
rawFindings.rootCause: Vacancy search is OR [title contains, company.name contains]. The company relation filter makes Prisma run a $lookup per vacancy, the same pattern that made public text search take 3.5 s before D-033. User search filters on jobSeekerProfile.firstName/lastName relations. Both queries run twice (findMany + count). Vacancy and Company have no createdAt index, so orderBy createdAt sorts every match. page is allowed up to 10,000 with skip.
rawFindings.impact: Moderation and support searches over 20k vacancies or 10k users will probably take seconds (inference by analogy with the 3505 ms pre-D-033 measurement). The default vacancies list with no status filter scans and sorts 20k documents on each load. Only /api/admin/users?page=200 without text was benchmarked (16 ms).
rawFindings.evidence: admin.routes.ts:239-259 where OR title/company.name, orderBy createdAt desc, skip/take, plus count. :140-167 users OR email/phone/jobSeekerProfile.firstName/lastName, plus count. :29 page max 10_000. :340-351 companies orderBy createdAt. schema.prisma:440-446 no Vacancy createdAt index; :337-339 no Company createdAt index. FINAL_AUDIT.md admin rows.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Resolve company IDs by name and profile userIds by name first (capped, e.g. 500), then filter on companyId in / id in, the same way resolveFilterIds does. Add @@index([createdAt]) and [status, createdAt] on Vacancy and [createdAt] on Company. Skip the count on later pages when a text filter is set.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-052 (admin part); DB_MAP I7 (recommended, not added)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low. Very common terms produce long ID lists, so cap them.

rawFindings.title: Employer vacancy dashboard returns 1000 full documents (987 KB at 500 vacancies); the edit form downloads the whole list to find one record
rawFindings.rootCause: GET /api/employer/vacancies has no select: it returns full documents (description, requirements, conditions) with region, category, company and a per-row _count of applications, take 1000. There is no single-vacancy owner endpoint, so the edit form fetches the entire list and picks one record.
rawFindings.impact: Measured 180 ms p50 and 987 KB for an employer with 500 vacancies. Every dashboard load and every edit-page open transfers the full payload. Vacancies beyond the newest 1000 cannot be edited from the UI.
rawFindings.evidence: vacancies.routes.ts:93 EMPLOYER_VACANCIES_LIMIT=1000; :126-136 findMany include region/category/company/_count, take 1000, no select. web components/employer/vacancies/VacancyFormView.tsx:79 fetchEmployerVacancyRecords and :87 records.find(r => r.id === vacancyId). lib/employer/vacancies/api.ts:24-28 calls /api/employer/vacancies. FINAL_AUDIT.md row 'ish beruvchi vakansiyalari (500)'.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add GET /api/employer/vacancies/:id with the ownedVacancy check for the edit form. Change the list to card fields only, a status filter and pageSize up to 50, one application.groupBy for the page's counts, and @@index([companyId, createdAt]).
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium. The dashboard view-model mapping and e2e checks expect full rows.

rawFindings.title: User.phone and backup phone have no index or uniqueness, but the new Telegram recovery rules make phone the lookup key
rawFindings.rootCause: User.phone and JobSeekerProfile.additionalPhone have no index. Telegram contact sharing writes phone with no duplicate check. Recovery by phone (rule B), backup phone (F) and a unique primary phone (E) all need an indexed lookup and a DB-level unique constraint. MongoDB treats null and missing values as equal in unique indexes, so a plain @unique would fail for users without a phone.
rawFindings.impact: Once recovery by phone exists, every recovery request (public, attacker-reachable) would scan 10k+ user documents. Duplicate phones may already exist, so recovery could match several accounts or the wrong one. Code-only uniqueness checks without an index are racy.
rawFindings.evidence: schema.prisma:160-205 User: phone String?, indexes only on telegramChatId, role, createdAt; :217 additionalPhone has no index. telegram.service.ts:333-343 findFirst by telegramChatId then update {phone, isPhoneVerified:true} with no duplicate check. profile.routes.ts:65-66 writes phone for unverified users. No where-by-phone lookup exists today (grep).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Normalize phones to E.164, backfill and resolve duplicates. Then create partial unique indexes via $runCommandRaw: {phone:1} unique with partialFilterExpression {isPhoneVerified:true, phone:{$type:'string'}}, and the same for a dedicated verified backup-phone field. Recovery should look up only by the normalized indexed value and never reveal whether a phone exists.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-012 (password recovery missing, NOT FIXED); auth rules B, E, F
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium. Existing duplicates block index creation, so a data-integrity pass and an ownership rule for contested phones are needed first.

rawFindings.title: Notifications have no retention or TTL; the center is capped at 100 with no pagination; the unreadOnly variant lacks a compound index
rawFindings.rootCause: Notifications are never deleted. Every broadcast inserts one document per user. The list accepts only limit up to 100 with no cursor, and the notification center always asks for 100. unreadOnly filters on isRead and sorts by createdAt, but the only indexes are [userId,isRead] and [userId,createdAt].
rawFindings.impact: The collection grows by ~10k documents per broadcast plus every application, status change and alert. Per-user reads stay fast (list and unread-count both measured 6 ms), but storage and index size grow without bound, and users cannot see anything older than the newest 100. A 10k-user broadcast takes at least ~400 s at the 40 ms gap.
rawFindings.evidence: notifications.routes.ts:20-23 limit max 100; :54-65 findMany take limit ?? 30 plus count. web lib/notifications/api.ts:5,22 NOTIFICATIONS_LIMIT=100. schema.prisma:626 [userId,isRead], :628 [userId,createdAt]; no TTL anywhere. admin.routes.ts:53,58,564-578 broadcast loop. notifications.service.ts:100-108 one create per notify.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add retention: a batched daily deleteMany for read notifications older than 90 days and all older than 180 days, or a partial TTL index created via $runCommandRaw. Add keyset pagination (?before=id) to the list and the center. Add @@index([userId, isRead, createdAt]).
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-053 (retention recommendation not implemented); ISSUE-054; ISSUE-112
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium. Old history disappears by design, and the TTL filter must not remove unread items.

rawFindings.title: Vacancy sitemap is one 7.2 MB file rebuilt per request at the origin; employer sitemap uses relation filters; hard 50k cap
rawFindings.rootCause: sitemap-vacancy.xml loads up to 50,000 active vacancies and builds one XML string with 3 locale links plus x-default per URL, on every request, with no API-side Cache-Control. Only the Vercel proxy caches it (1 h); the self-hosted server has no sitemap route. sitemap-employer filters on owner.isBlocked and vacancies.some, both relation filters that run $lookup for every company.
rawFindings.impact: Measured 240 ms and 7189 KB at ~14k active vacancies. At the 50k cap the file would be ~25 MB (linear estimate), and anything beyond the cap is silently dropped. The employer sitemap was not benchmarked; its shape resembles the uncached catalog (~0.7 s, inference).
rawFindings.evidence: seo.routes.ts:97-109 vacancy findMany take 50000 then buildUrlSet. :111-131 company where NOT owner.isBlocked, OR vacancies.some active. :150-164 buildUrlSet. web api/seo.js:50 s-maxage=3600 (Vercel only). web server/index.mjs has no sitemap handling (grep). FINAL_AUDIT.md sitemap row.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Split into sitemap-vacancy-N.xml chunks of 10k using _id keyset, listed in sitemap.xml. Cache the generated XML in-process for 1 h and send Cache-Control from the API. For the employer sitemap, resolve blocked owner IDs and distinct active-vacancy companyIds first instead of relation filters.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low. vercel.json rewrites and robots.txt must cover the new chunk names.

rawFindings.title: Admin overview pulls 14 days of user and application rows into Node and counts unindexed boolean fields
rawFindings.rootCause: The overview runs 14 parallel counts, including user.count({isBlocked:true}) and company.count({isVerified:true}) with no index. It then loads every user and application created in the last 14 days and buckets them by day in JavaScript.
rawFindings.impact: Measured 112 ms at the synthetic volume. The 14-day transfer grows with real activity: a busy fortnight with tens of thousands of applications means tens of thousands of rows per overview load.
rawFindings.evidence: admin.routes.ts:87-102 Promise.all of counts, including isBlocked and isVerified. :107-113 user.findMany and application.findMany with createdAt >= since, select createdAt. :42-49 countByDay. schema.prisma:201-203 User indexes, none on isBlocked. FINAL_AUDIT.md admin overview row.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Aggregate in MongoDB with $group on $dateToString using timezone 'Asia/Tashkent'. Cache the overview for 60 s. Use a partial index on is_blocked:true.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low. Day boundaries must match startOfTashkentDay.

rawFindings.title: Salary statistics silently ignore active vacancies beyond 20,000 and reload ~20k rows on every cache miss
rawFindings.rootCause: The cached dataset takes at most 20,000 active vacancies ordered by publishedAt desc and keeps title, salary, category and region in memory. Above that count, older active vacancies drop out of every statistic and the market median, with no signal.
rawFindings.impact: Nothing is dropped at 14,427 active vacancies. Past 20k active, /salaries numbers become partial without anyone noticing. Each miss (5 min TTL, or any global version bump) reloads the set; cold measured 573 ms.
rawFindings.evidence: salary.stats.ts:76 MAX_ROWS = 20_000. :166-181 cached(5*60_000) findMany {status:'active'} with title/salary/category/region select, take MAX_ROWS. :199-262 all statistics computed over those rows. FINAL_AUDIT.md /api/stats/salary row.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Load only salaried, non-hidden UZS rows (with vacancyCount computed separately), log a warning when the cap is hit or remove it, and precompute per-category, per-region and per-experience aggregates on a schedule.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low. vacancyCount currently includes hidden-salary vacancies and must stay consistent.

rawFindings.title: 10K benchmark cannot be re-run from the repo, and several hot or heavy endpoints are not measured
rawFindings.rootCause: scale_bench.mjs and explain_queries.mjs are cited as evidence, but neither they nor the synthetic data generator are in the repository. The benchmark table covers 25 endpoint variants and leaves out several paths reviewed here.
rawFindings.impact: Changes to unmeasured paths cannot be verified. Not measured: filtered and text facets, /api/vacancies/:slug/similar, /api/companies/:slug/similar and catalog cursor pages, candidates with text, admin vacancy list and text searches, sitemap-employer.xml, notification center (limit=100, unreadOnly), seeker conversation lists, popular / salary_asc / deep text pages, articles, alerts sweep and broadcast duration.
rawFindings.evidence: FINAL_AUDIT.md:111 'TEST: explain_queries.mjs, scale_bench.mjs'. FINAL_AUDIT.md:169 onward: the 10K table rows. A find for scale_bench* / explain_queries* in the repo returns nothing. apps/api/scripts contains only e2e-check.mjs and generate-vapid.mjs.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Commit the generator, benchmark and explain scripts under apps/api/scripts/scale, with a guard that refuses non-test database names. Add the unmeasured endpoints above and record the explain stage plus keysExamined/docsExamined, so each scale fix has a before and after number.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-101 (test scripts not reproducible, NOT FIXED); D-032
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low, provided the scripts hard-fail against dev, demo or production databases.

rawFindings.title: No persisted audit log for admin/staff actions or security events
rawFindings.rootCause: The schema has no AuditLog/SecurityEvent model (model list schema.prisma:160-805). None of these handlers writes any record: block (190-215), role (217-226), vacancy moderate (285-325), company verify (374-394), review status/delete (443-456), payment confirm (502-521), broadcast (534-591), team PATCH/invites (team.routes.ts:125-216), article delete (articles.admin.routes.ts:442-452), admin delete of a vacancy with applications (vacancies.routes.ts:279-289). The only trace is a pino line with the broadcast delivered count (admin.routes.ts:582).
rawFindings.impact: A compromised or rogue admin can grant admin, block users, delete reviews or cascade-delete applications with no forensic trace. Rule L events (sessions invalidated, manual recovery approved, Telegram linked/unlinked, phone verified/changed) have nowhere to be recorded.
rawFindings.evidence: grep for auditLog/securityEvent/adminAction over apps/api/src and apps/web/src returns nothing; schema.prisma model list has no audit model; admin.routes.ts:195-225 updates then returns; team.routes.ts:189-215 same.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add an append-only AuditEvent model (actorId, action enum, targetType, targetId, allowlisted metadata such as old/new role or status, ip hash, createdAt; indexes [targetId, createdAt] and [action, createdAt]). Add a recordAudit() helper and call it after every admin/team/article-delete mutation and from future auth security flows. Never store bodies, tokens, passwords or message text. Show a read-only per-user history in the existing /admin/users row later.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low. Additive collection and helper calls; one extra write per admin action.

rawFindings.title: Manual account recovery (rule H) has no workflow; admin cannot reset phone or revoke sessions
rawFindings.rootCause: User administration offers only block (190-215) and role (217-226). There is no endpoint to reset or replace a verified phone, unlink Telegram, or invalidate sessions without blocking. The login page's forgot link goes to /support (login/+Page.tsx:83-86). The support form has no recovery subject (support.routes.ts:19). Messages are only forwarded to the Telegram admin chat and never stored (support.routes.ts:140). The bot relay (telegram.service.ts:352-374) needs Telegram, which the rule H user has lost.
rawFindings.impact: A user who lost their password, phone and Telegram has no path back. Admins would improvise (role/block hacks or direct DB edits) with no ownership verification, no forced session invalidation and no audit. Rule H is unmet.
rawFindings.evidence: Existing surfaces that can host this without a new page: /admin/users already searches by email and phone (admin.routes.ts:142-151), shows isPhoneVerified/telegramLinked tags (users/+Page.tsx:133-138), has a row-action pattern with confirm, busy state and notice (users/+Page.tsx:45-58,143-166) and an AdminSelect filter (80-93). The overview already shows pending counters (admin.routes.ts:99, reviews.pending). POST /api/support is public and rate-limited (support.routes.ts:121-123).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Intake: add an 'account_recovery' subject to POST /api/support that also persists an AccountRecoveryRequest (status pending/approved/rejected, contact email, claimed phone stored as a hash or last digits, reviewer, notes; no secrets). Admin: add a 'Recovery requests' filter on /admin/users plus a pending counter on the overview. Approve action: clear phone/isPhoneVerified/telegramChatId (or set an admin-verified new phone pending Telegram re-verification), call revokeUserSessions and closeUserSockets, write an audit event, notify the user. Admins never set or see passwords; the user then re-verifies via Telegram and uses Telegram recovery.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium. New model and endpoints; the approval must be one-time and race-safe (conditional update on status=pending).

rawFindings.title: ensure-admin auto-promotes any account registered with ADMIN_EMAIL on every boot
rawFindings.rootCause: On every boot (server.ts:267-271), ensureAdminUser promotes any existing user whose email equals ADMIN_EMAIL (ensure-admin.ts:23-29). If ADMIN_PASSWORD is missing or short, no admin is created and the email stays free (32-37). Public registration accepts any email without an ownership check (auth.service.ts:37-60; roles job_seeker/employer at auth.routes.ts:19), and login ignores isEmailVerified (auth.service.ts:90-110). The code comment tells operators to delete the admin from the DB to recover a lost password (ensure-admin.ts:12-14).
rawFindings.impact: If ADMIN_EMAIL is set but no account exists yet (no password configured, or during the 'delete and restart' recovery the comment suggests), anyone who registers that often guessable address becomes super admin at the next deploy or restart. A panel demotion of that account is also reverted on restart.
rawFindings.evidence: ensure-admin.ts:23-29 `if (existing) { if (existing.role !== "admin") await prisma.user.update(... role: "admin")`; server.ts:271 `await ensureAdminUser(app.log)`; auth.service.ts:44-60 creates the user with no email verification; loginUser has no isEmailVerified check.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Only create the admin when the email is absent. Never promote an existing account automatically, or promote only when it is isEmailVerified, no active admin exists, and an explicit one-shot flag (e.g. ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_PROMOTE=1) is set; otherwise log a warning. Replace the 'delete the account' advice with the manual recovery flow, since deleting a user cascades its data (schema onDelete: Cascade).
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low. Bootstrap-only code path.

rawFindings.title: Telegram login issues admin/staff sessions without a password (rule A)
rawFindings.rootCause: POST /api/auth/telegram/start and /poll (auth.routes.ts:137-158) let any account with a linked telegramChatId log in after a bot button confirmation (telegram.service.ts:248-249, 310-315). telegramLogin (auth.service.ts:176-181) has no role check, so admin and staff accounts qualify.
rawFindings.impact: Taking over the Telegram account or chat that is linked to an admin gives a full super-admin session with no password. It also directly violates rule A (Telegram is not a login channel).
rawFindings.evidence: auth.service.ts:176-181 `export async function telegramLogin(userId)` only checks assertNotBlocked and then issueTokens; auth.routes.ts:155-157 sets the refresh cookie and returns accessToken.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Remove the Telegram login endpoints and the bot login branch, keeping Telegram only for verification, linking and recovery. As an interim guard, refuse telegramLogin for roles in STAFF_ROLES.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low to medium. The web login UI button and its i18n strings must be removed too.

rawFindings.title: Privilege changes lack safeguards: no last-admin guard, no step-up, generic confirm
rawFindings.rootCause: PATCH /api/admin/users/:id/role and /block only forbid acting on yourself (193, 220). Team PATCH does the same (team.routes.ts:182-184). Any admin can grant admin to any user, or demote or block every other admin. No re-authentication is required. The web 'Make admin' button uses the generic 'Ishonchingiz komilmi?' confirm without naming the user or role (users/+Page.tsx:151-154; messages.uz.ts:1909).
rawFindings.impact: One stolen admin session can lock out all other admins; ensure-admin restores only the role, not isBlocked (ensure-admin.ts:24-29), so recovery needs DB access. Accidental admin grants expose all candidates' email and phone (candidates.routes.ts:36,72).
rawFindings.evidence: admin.routes.ts:217-226 has no admin-count check; team.routes.ts:189-215 same; users/+Page.tsx:45-47 `window.confirm(t.admin.common.confirmAction)`.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Reject demoting or blocking the last active admin (count role=admin, isBlocked=false). Require password re-entry for granting admin. Use a role-specific confirm naming the user, as TeamList.tsx:43 does. Audit every change (see the audit finding).
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-035 / ISSUE-108 (FIXED: DB role check; this gap is separate)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Admin vacancy moderation can publish drafts and skips category/workplace/location rules
rawFindings.rootCause: PATCH /api/admin/vacancies/:id/moderate sets status 'active' from any state (287-309). It does not call assertVacancyPlacement, does not reject drafts, and does not check whether the owner is blocked. The employer/admin status route does run placement checks (vacancies.routes.ts:245-255). The admin list includes drafts when unfiltered (239-244), and the UI shows Approve on every non-active row (vacancies/+Page.tsx:175-178), with an untranslated 'draft' label (71).
rawFindings.impact: An employer's unfinished private draft can go public without consent (breaks draft visibility). Legacy vacancies missing category or workplaceType or location become active (breaks required-field rules). Vacancies archived when their owner was blocked (admin.routes.ts:203-211) can be reactivated.
rawFindings.evidence: admin.routes.ts:304-306 `...(status ? { status } : {})`, `...(status === "active" ? { rejectionReason: null, publishedAt: ... } : {})` with no validation; vacancies.routes.ts:250-254 assertVacancyPlacement exists only on the other route.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: In moderate, allow 'active' only from moderation, rejected or archived; return 409 for draft. Call assertVacancyPlacement with effectiveWorkplaceType. Refuse when the company owner isBlocked. Hide Approve on draft rows and translate the draft label.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Admin role change leaves inconsistent state (orphaned active vacancies, staff roles unmodelled)
rawFindings.rootCause: The role route only updates the role and revokes sessions (217-226). Unlike block (203-211), it does not archive the owner's active vacancies, so an employer changed to job_seeker keeps live vacancies they can no longer manage (requireRole('employer','admin') at applications.routes.ts:310, vacancies.routes.ts:273). The users route enums exclude content_editor/content_author (137, 219). The table shows raw staff role names and offers make-seeker/employer buttons on staff rows (users/+Page.tsx:60-64,140,151-165), bypassing the team page.
rawFindings.impact: Candidates keep applying to vacancies with no reachable owner. Staff can be silently turned into seekers or employers outside the team workflow, leaving staffProfile and article authorship stale.
rawFindings.evidence: admin.routes.ts:221-225 `prisma.user.update({ data: { role } }); await revokeUserSessions(id)` with no vacancy handling; admin.routes.ts:137 `role: z.enum(["job_seeker","employer","admin"])`.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: When leaving the employer role, archive active vacancies and sync the index (reuse the block branch), or refuse while active vacancies exist. Exclude staff rows from the users-route role actions (point to /admin/team) and add staff roles to the filter and labels.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Staff and bootstrap admin accounts have no phone, so Telegram-only recovery can never work for them
rawFindings.rootCause: Invite accept creates the account with email, password and isEmailVerified: true but no phone and no Telegram (team.routes.ts:250-257). ensure-admin does the same (ensure-admin.ts:40-46). The admin and staff guards never require isPhoneVerified (admin.routes.ts:25; articles.admin.routes.ts:38-39). The only documented admin recovery is deleting the account (ensure-admin.ts:12-14).
rawFindings.impact: Under rules B/E, the most privileged accounts cannot recover a password at all, and the suggested DB deletion cascades their invites and profile (schema.prisma:697,715) and can trigger the ensure-admin promotion race.
rawFindings.evidence: team.routes.ts:250-257 user.create without phone; ensure-admin.ts:40-46 same; ensure-admin.ts:14 'avval hisobni bazadan o'chiring'.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Require staff to verify a primary phone via Telegram on first /admin visit (gate AdminShell and requireStaff('admin') on isPhoneVerified, with a grace path to the verification screen). Include staff in the manual recovery flow and remove the delete-from-DB guidance.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium. Existing admins must be onboarded before the gate is enforced.

rawFindings.title: Telegram admin-chat support relay is controlled by chat membership, not panel RBAC
rawFindings.rootCause: Support messages (with the sender's email and role) go to TELEGRAM_ADMIN_CHAT_ID (352-373). Any reply in that chat to a message containing #u<chatId> is relayed to the user as the official 'Support javobi' (377-386). Authorization is only `chatId === env.TELEGRAM_ADMIN_CHAT_ID` (406). Nothing is persisted or audited.
rawFindings.impact: Removing or blocking someone in /admin/team does not remove their access to support traffic or their ability to answer users as support. If recovery requests are routed through support, identity data and recovery conversations sit outside RBAC and audit.
rawFindings.evidence: telegram.service.ts:369-372 forwards `Kimdan: ${user.email} (${user.role})` plus message text; 384 relays the admin reply; 406-407 has no per-sender check.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Store support tickets in the DB and handle them from the admin panel (a recovery-requests filter on /admin/users, see the manual recovery finding). If the Telegram relay stays, restrict replies to linked telegramChatIds of active admin/staff users (msg.from.id lookup) and audit relayed replies.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low to medium

rawFindings.title: Broadcast is fire-and-forget in process memory: no durable record, progress or resume
rawFindings.rootCause: The lock is a module variable (52) and the send loop is a detached async IIFE (557-588). Nothing about the broadcast (actor, content, audience, cursor, delivered, failed) is stored. The response returns the target count as `sent` (549, 590), and the UI reports it as sent (admin/+Page.tsx:224-225). Each user awaits external channels with a 40 ms minimum gap (574-577).
rawFindings.impact: At 10k users a run takes at least 400 s, and likely much longer with SMTP/Telegram latency (inference). A Railway redeploy or crash mid-run silently truncates delivery. Admins cannot see progress, and re-sending duplicates messages to users who already got it. With more than one replica the lock does not hold.
rawFindings.evidence: admin.routes.ts:51-53 `let broadcastRunning = false`; 582 only `log.info({ delivered })`; 590 `reply.status(202).send({ sent: total })`.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Persist a Broadcast document (actorId, title, body, audience, status, lastId, delivered, failed, timestamps). Take the lock with a conditional DB update, resume from lastId on boot, show status and progress on the overview, label the UI count as 'queued', and audit the send.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-054 / ISSUE-112 (FIXED: moved to background and throttled; durability still missing)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low to medium

rawFindings.title: Admin list search uses relation filters and unanchored regex, run twice per request
rawFindings.rootCause: User search ORs email/phone `contains` with jobSeekerProfile.firstName/lastName relation filters (142-151). Vacancy search uses company.name as a relation filter (241-243). Each where clause runs for both findMany and count (154-167, 246-259). On MongoDB, Prisma turns relation filters into $lookup pipelines over every document (the repo notes this at ownership.ts:3-5, ISSUE-045). The vacancy list sorts by createdAt with no index (schema.prisma:440-446). The overview loads 14 days of application rows into memory on each view (107-113).
rawFindings.impact: With 10k users and tens of thousands of vacancies, each admin search does two full collection scans with per-document lookups (inferred multi-second latency and DB load). Deep skip pages are also slow.
rawFindings.evidence: admin.routes.ts:147-148 `{ jobSeekerProfile: { firstName: like(query.text) } }`; 242 `{ company: { name: like(query.text) } }`; articles.admin.routes.ts:216-229 already uses a two-step search to avoid this.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Use a two-step search like articles.admin.routes.ts: resolve profile userIds and company ids first with a bounded query, then filter by id `in`. Add an exact-match fast path for normalized email and phone. Order vacancies by id or add a createdAt index. Build the overview chart with a $group aggregation.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Impactful admin actions have missing or generic confirmations
rawFindings.rootCause: Company unverify has no confirm (companies/+Page.tsx:44-56,132). Vacancy archive and premium toggles have no confirm (vacancies/+Page.tsx:185-192). Review approve/reject have no confirm, and delete uses a generic prompt without the review or company (reviews/+Page.tsx:140-152). Role grants use a generic prompt (users/+Page.tsx:151-165). Reindex and alert sweep run with no confirm (admin/+Page.tsx:156-171). RowButton has no disabled state (AdminShell.tsx:254-277).
rawFindings.impact: Misclicks silently unverify companies, archive live vacancies or hard-delete reviews, with no audit to reconstruct what happened.
rawFindings.evidence: companies/+Page.tsx:44-48 toggleVerify calls verifyCompany directly; reviews/+Page.tsx:150 `act(row, deleteAdminReview, true)` with t.admin.common.confirmAction; contrast TeamList.tsx:43,48 and AdminArticleList.tsx:67-69, which name the item.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Use name-specific confirms for unverify, archive, review delete and role grant, following the TeamList/AdminArticleList pattern. Add a disabled prop to RowButton driven by busyId.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Search reindex runs inline with no lock; concurrent run or publish can drop fresh docs
rawFindings.rootCause: POST /api/admin/search/reindex awaits reindexAll inside the HTTP request (admin.routes.ts:528) with no running flag, unlike runAlertSweep (alerts.service.ts:113-120). reindexAll snapshots active ids and then deletes every index doc not in that snapshot (search.service.ts:186-211).
rawFindings.impact: A vacancy published and synced during the scan, or a second concurrent reindex from another admin or tab, can be removed from Meilisearch until its next sync (race inferred). Large reindexes can also outlive proxy request timeouts.
rawFindings.evidence: search.service.ts:205-211 builds `stale` from activeIds and calls index.deleteDocuments(stale); admin.routes.ts:528 `async () => reindexAll()`.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add a single-flight lock. Re-check DB status before deleting stale ids (or delete only ids whose vacancy is not active). Run as a background job returning 202 with status on the overview.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Legacy payments admin surface is not behind the billing flag
rawFindings.rootCause: server.ts:253 gates only billingRoutes on features.billing. adminRoutes always registers GET /api/admin/payments and POST /api/admin/payments/:transactionId/confirm (461-521), and confirm activates a plan via markPaymentPaid (504). The web nav always shows Payments (AdminShell.tsx:50) and the overview always shows a Revenue card (admin/+Page.tsx:107-112).
rawFindings.impact: Monetization UI persists in the core admin experience of a fully free platform, and an admin can still activate paid plans while billing is disabled.
rawFindings.evidence: server.ts:253-254 `if (features.billing) await app.register(billingRoutes); await app.register(adminRoutes);`
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Gate payment routes, the nav tab and the revenue card on features.billing (expose the flag in the overview response).
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: E2E has no negative authz checks for admin.routes mutations
rawFindings.rootCause: The guest/seeker/employer 401/403 loop covers only /api/admin/articles, /api/admin/team and /api/admin/articles/authors (930-937). admin.routes endpoints are exercised only with the admin token (558-566, 1416, 1679, 1762). Role change, broadcast, moderation, review delete and company verify are never tested with non-admin or content_editor tokens.
rawFindings.impact: A regression that swaps requireStaff('admin') for a broader guard would pass CI.
rawFindings.evidence: grep '/api/admin' in e2e-check.mjs shows no seekerToken/employerToken/staffEditorToken use on admin.routes paths.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Extend the loop to admin.routes GET and PATCH/POST paths with seeker, employer, content_editor and content_author tokens (expect 403) and guest (expect 401).
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Docs and comments still say admin routes use token-based requireRole
rawFindings.rootCause: AdminShell.tsx:11-13 says /api/admin/* is guarded by requireRole("admin"), and API_MAP.md:154 says admin routes trust the token role. The code actually uses requireAuth + requireStaff("admin") with the role read from the DB (admin.routes.ts:25; auth-guard.ts:52-59,76-84).
rawFindings.impact: Misleads future authorization reviews and fixes.
rawFindings.evidence: docs/audit/maps/API_MAP.md:154 '(**tokendagi** rol; requireStaff emas)'; admin.routes.ts:25 `requireStaff("admin")`.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Update the AdminShell comment and the API_MAP section 12 header.
rawFindings.fixRisk: None

rawFindings.title: Uzbek apostrophe variants (o' oʻ o‘ o’ `) are not normalized in vacancy, company, candidate and admin search
rawFindings.rootCause: searchTerms (137-143) only trims and splits on whitespace. Terms go into Prisma contains/insensitive (172, 253), a literal substring match. Stored title, description, company and category text is saved as typed (vacancies.routes.ts:55, trim only). Neither side maps ʻ ʼ ’ ‘ ` to one form. The normalizer already exists in articles.content.ts:40-41, salary.stats.ts:97-100 and web lib/list.ts:40-41, but it is not used here, in companies.list.ts:247-249, in candidates.routes.ts:43-61 or in admin.routes.ts:39.
rawFindings.impact: A query and a vacancy that spell o'/g' with different characters never match, and the user sees an empty page. Uzbek job words with o'/g' are very common (o'qituvchi, qo'riqchi, ko'chmas mulk, Farg'ona). iOS Smart Punctuation turns ' into ’ by default, and official Latin Uzbek uses ʻ (U+02BB), so mismatches go both ways (prevalence is an inference). Meili tokenizer behaviour may differ (inference), which adds driver divergence.
rawFindings.evidence: Demo data uses ASCII ' only: demo-seed.ts:499,525,607,673,759,799,807, with 0 occurrences of ʻ or ’ in demo-seed.ts. The seed category is "Qurilish, ko'chmas mulk" (seed.ts:49). On the Mongo driver, GET /api/vacancies?text=ko’chmas (U+2019) gives terms ["ko’chmas"], nothing contains it, and total is 0. text=ko'chmas returns "Ko'chmas mulk bo'yicha sotuv menejeri" (demo-seed.ts:759) plus every vacancy in that category. /api/companies?q=, /api/candidates?text= and the admin ?text= searches behave the same way.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add a shared common normalizeSearch (lowercase, map [ʻʼ’‘`´] to ') and apply it to query terms. For stored text, either add a normalized searchText to Vacancy and Company (like Article.searchText, filled on write, with a backfill), or build per-term regexes that accept any apostrophe variant (with escaping). Normalize the same fields in the Meili toDoc. Add e2e cases for ’ and ʻ.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: None for vacancies/companies/candidates. ISSUE-048 covers only regex performance. Articles already solved this (articles.content.ts:40).
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: a stored normalized field needs a backfill and a reindex; the regex-variant approach keeps the current scan cost.

rawFindings.title: Terms under 4 characters still substring-match titles and company/category names (false hits) but skip requirements (missed hits)
rawFindings.rootCause: For short terms, textFilter (263-270) drops description and requirements but still uses unanchored substrings: title contains (268), company name contains (183), category name contains (184). The comment's example ("sHaHRi") is excluded only from descriptions, not from titles or company names. Skill tokens (PHP, SQL, 1C, Go, C++) usually appear only in requirements, which short terms never search.
rawFindings.impact: The product's own popular chip "HR" (web lib/salaries/query.ts:107) and queries like "IT" or "QA" return unrelated vacancies and miss relevant ones. A company-name substring hit pulls in every vacancy of that company. Meili matches whole words in all fields, so the two drivers return different sets.
rawFindings.evidence: Demo on Mongo: GET /api/vacancies?text=IT, term "IT" (<4 chars), title contains "it". It returns "Kredit mutaxassisi" (demo-seed.ts:563, kred-IT) next to "IT stajyor" (demo-seed.ts:491). GET ?text=PHP does not return a vacancy titled "Backend dasturchi" whose PHP mention is only in requirements. D-033 kept this rule for performance reasons.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Match short terms on word boundaries with an escaped regex such as (^|[^\p{L}\p{N}])term($|[^\p{L}\p{N}]), including requirements. Use the same word-boundary rule when resolving company and category names to IDs.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low-medium: result counts change; e2e text=DASTURCHI react still passes.

rawFindings.title: Meilisearch and MongoDB return different result sets for the same query, and the driver switches with sort, filters, facets and alerts
rawFindings.rootCause: Meili runs only when text is set, sort is relevance and there is no company/verified/premium/date filter (352-354). Facets (computeFacets 430-447) and alerts (alerts.service.ts:185-195, publishedAfter set) always use Mongo. Mongo requires every term as a substring (AND, 255). Meili does word/prefix matching with typo tolerance and default matchingStrategy "last", which drops trailing terms (not overridden, search.service.ts:257-263; the default is inferred from Meili docs). Meili indexes only description[0..4000] and requirements[0..2000] (toDoc 122-123); Mongo searches full fields up to 20k/10k characters (vacancies.routes.ts:56-57).
rawFindings.impact: With MEILI_HOST set, the result count changes when the user only changes the sort or ticks "verified". Facet counts disagree with the list total. A saved search that showed N results on the page may never alert, because the sweep runs the stricter Mongo query.
rawFindings.evidence: With Meili on, ?text=dasturchu (typo) with sort=relevance returns "dasturchi" vacancies, but the same query with sort=date (Mongo) returns 0. ?text=frontend dasturchi toshkent: Mongo needs "toshkent" in the text (region name is searchable in neither driver), giving about 0, while Meili drops the last word and returns all frontend vacancies (inference). A term that appears only after character 4000 of a description is found by Mongo but not Meili. The e2e suite asserts engine mongodb (e2e-check.mjs:270), so the Meili path is never tested.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Pick one semantics. Option A: set matchingStrategy "all" and tune typo tolerance, index full text, add companyId/isVerified/isPremium/publishedAt as filterable, and route other sorts, facets and alerts through the engine. Option B: use Meili only for candidate IDs and apply all filters and counts in Mongo. Add a parity test that runs one query set against both drivers.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-061 (fixed the status re-filter only, not parity)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: visible result counts change, and CI needs a Meili instance.

rawFindings.title: Meili path returns an estimated, uncorrected total, caps reachable hits at 1000 and orders differently from Mongo 'relevance'
rawFindings.rootCause: total = res.estimatedTotalHits (266) is passed through unchanged (vacancies.service.ts:380-384), even after non-active rows are dropped (368-378). updateSettings (48-62) sets no pagination.maxTotalHits, so Meili's default of 1000 applies (inference from docs). The sort ["isPremium:desc"] (261) sits after words/typo/proximity/attribute in rankingRules (61), so premium only breaks late ties, and there is no publishedAt tiebreak. Mongo 'relevance' is isPremium, then publishedAt, then id (276-284), with no text ranking at all.
rawFindings.impact: For broad queries the header count is an estimate. Pages past hit 1000 (page 51+ at 20 per page) come back empty while pageCount promises more. A page can show fewer cards than pageSize. Premium vacancies rank first in Mongo mode but not in Meili mode. In Mongo mode 'relevance' means date order: a title match ranks below a newer description-only match.
rawFindings.evidence: Example with Meili on a large dataset: ?text=menejer&page=60 gives offset 1180, past maxTotalHits 1000, so items are [] and total is at most 1000 (inference from Meili defaults). The same query with sort=date (Mongo) returns page 60. The e2e check at e2e-check.mjs:294 asserts only the item count for sort=relevance, not the order.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Raise pagination.maxTotalHits to cover the API page cap, or cap pages in Meili mode, and use page/hitsPerPage to get an exact totalHits. Position the "sort" ranking rule deliberately and add publishedAt:desc as a tiebreak. For Mongo 'relevance', rank title matches first (for example with a scored aggregateRaw) or rename the sort option.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low for the index settings; medium for Mongo text scoring.

rawFindings.title: Search does not bridge Latin and Cyrillic Uzbek, and category names shown in the ru/en UI are not searchable
rawFindings.rootCause: Term matching is literal (172, 253). Category names are stored only in Uzbek Latin (seed.ts:45-50). The web shows translated names by slug (web lib/i18n/categories.ts:23-38), but the text filter matches only the stored name (vacancies.service.ts:184). There is no transliteration step, even though slug.ts:15-22 already has a Cyrillic-to-Latin table and articles index category words in three languages (articles.content.ts:20-27).
rawFindings.impact: Uzbek users typing in Cyrillic (дастурчи, бухгалтер) and ru-locale users typing the category label they see get empty or partial results against Latin-script vacancies.
rawFindings.evidence: Demo vacancy titles are Latin Uzbek (demo-seed.ts:442-635). /ru/vacancies?q=Финансы sends text=Финансы; no category name contains it, so "Moliya, buxgalteriya" is not matched and demo data gives 0. ?text=дастурчи returns 0, while ?text=dasturchi returns the IT vacancies. By contrast, /api/articles?q=собеседование finds articles (e2e-check.mjs:1035).
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add a normalized Vacancy searchText: title, company, category words in uz/ru/en, and a Latin transliteration of Cyrillic content using the slug.ts TRANSLIT table. Transliterate Cyrillic query terms to Latin before matching. Add ru/en synonyms for category names (like CATEGORY_WORDS), and apply the same to the Meili documents or synonyms.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: needs a stored field and backfill; transliteration is lossy (x/h, ў/o').

rawFindings.title: Query tokenization silently drops 1-char terms and terms past the 6th, and keeps punctuation inside terms
rawFindings.rootCause: searchTerms splits only on whitespace, drops length < 2 and slices to 6 (138-142), with no dedupe and no punctuation stripping. The API schema only truncates to 200 characters, with no trim or minimum (vacancies.routes.ts:29,33). The web input debounces at 2 characters, but Enter submits any length (web components/vacancies/VacancySearch.tsx:9-10,53-58). Company search has no minimum at all (companies.list.ts:247), so the rules differ between pages.
rawFindings.impact: "C" or "R" returns the whole unfiltered list as if it were results for that query. A trailing comma makes the word unmatched. Long queries silently lose their most specific tail terms. Punctuation-only queries show an empty page.
