rawFindings.evidence: Mongo examples: ?text=C gives no terms, so the filters alone apply and every active vacancy is returned. ?text=dasturchi, react needs the literal "dasturchi,", so "Frontend dasturchi (React)" (demo-seed.ts:442) does not match. ?text=senior frontend react typescript redux jest toshkent ignores "toshkent". ?text=java java java java java java kotlin drops kotlin. ?text=!! needs a title containing "!!" and returns 0, while Meili treats separators-only as an empty query and returns everything (inference). /api/companies?q=a matches nearly every company.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Normalize the query once and share it across drivers and pages: strip leading and trailing punctuation per token (keep C++, C#, node.js), dedupe, and treat a query with no usable terms as no text. Handle 1-char tokens as whole-word title matches or reject them clearly. Remove the 6-term cap or tell the user. Add .trim().max(100) to listQuerySchema.text to match the web limit.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Company rename does not reindex its vacancies in Meilisearch, so stale companyName hits persist until restart
rawFindings.rootCause: Index documents copy in companyName and companySlug (search.service.ts:124-125). PUT /api/employer/company updates the name (companies.routes.ts:108-123) and only calls bumpDataVersion(). No code reindexes that company's vacancies; only warmSearchIndex at startup (server.ts:282) or the admin reindex (admin.routes.ts:528) does. Inference: sync is fire-and-forget (vacancies.routes.ts:218,264,290). removeVacancyFromIndex skips the DB read that indexVacancy does, so a quick activate-then-archive can queue the add after the delete and leave an archived document indexed.
rawFindings.impact: With Meili on, searching the new company name misses its vacancies and the old name still finds them until the next deploy. Cards re-read from the DB show the new name, so the hit looks unrelated. The Mongo driver resolves names live, so the result depends on the sort.
rawFindings.evidence: Rename "Orzubank" to "Orzu Bank". ?text=Orzu Bank (relevance, Meili) still sees companyName "Orzubank" in the index, so vacancies whose own text lacks the new name are not returned. ?text=Orzubank still returns them, shown with the card name "Orzu Bank" (vacancies.service.ts:368-378). With sort=date (Mongo) the results are correct. Company verify is fine: verified is not in the index and turns the engine off.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: When name or slug changes, reindex the company's active vacancies in the background with batched addDocuments. Make removeVacancyFromIndex re-read the vacancy status, or serialize sync per vacancy id.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Company catalog search still returns companies whose owner is blocked
rawFindings.rootCause: listCompanies base filters (242-271) never check owner.isBlocked, and neither does GET /api/companies/:slug (companies.routes.ts:184-220). Blocking a user only archives their vacancies (admin.routes.ts:203-211). The sitemap already excludes blocked-owner companies (seo.routes.ts:114-116, ISSUE-056), so the rule exists but search was not aligned.
rawFindings.impact: A blocked employer's company (name, logo, description, rating) stays findable in /companies search, in similar-company blocks and at its public URL, which works against moderation.
rawFindings.evidence: Admin runs PATCH /api/admin/users/:id/block on employer X, and X's vacancies become archived. GET /api/companies?q=<X name> still returns the card with activeVacancyCount 0, and GET /api/companies/<slug> returns 200. similarCompanies (companies.list.ts:396) can surface it on other companies' pages. Whether hiding is intended is inferred from the sitemap rule.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Resolve blocked employer IDs and add owner_user_id $nin to the base $match. Return 404 from the detail and similar endpoints for blocked owners, as the sitemap does. Bump the catalog cache on block and unblock.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Candidate and admin searches match the whole query as one substring per field, so full names and multi-skill queries find nothing
rawFindings.rootCause: q = query.text is used unsplit in contains on headline, firstName, lastName, resume title and each skillName (candidates.routes.ts:43-61). Admin users, vacancies and companies search the same way (admin.routes.ts:142-149, 241-243, 336), and pageSchema.text is not trimmed (admin.routes.ts:28). No apostrophe normalization is applied.
rawFindings.impact: An employer searching "Aziz Karimov" or "React TypeScript" gets an empty candidate list. An admin cannot find a user by full name or by an email pasted with a trailing space.
rawFindings.evidence: GET /api/candidates?text=Aziz Karimov: firstName "Aziz" does not contain "aziz karimov", and neither does lastName, so the result is 0. ?text=React TypeScript: no single skillName contains both words, so 0. GET /api/admin/users?text=aziz%20 (trailing space): email contains "aziz " fails, so 0. The e2e test (e2e-check.mjs:565) only tries "aziz".
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Split into normalized terms and require each term in some field (an AND of per-term ORs, like vacancies textFilter). Add .trim() to the admin pageSchema.text.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Unknown experience/employment values are ignored by the Mongo driver but become zero-result filters on Meili
rawFindings.rootCause: Mongo runs splitList against EXPERIENCE_VALUES/EMPLOYMENT_VALUES (vacancies.service.ts:118-122, 202-203) and drops unknown values. Meili's oneOf and employment branch (search.service.ts:240-252) put the raw values into IN [...] with no allow-list.
rawFindings.impact: A stale or edited URL shows all results on one driver and none on the other, breaking the rule that invalid URL values are ignored.
rawFindings.evidence: e2e-check.mjs:287 expects total 1 for employment=yoq on Mongo. With Meili, ?text=dasturchi&employment=yoq builds the filter employmentType IN ["yoq"] and returns 0 hits, and ?text=dasturchi&experience=senior also returns 0. The same URL without text uses Mongo and shows all vacancies.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Validate with the same allow-lists before building the Meili filter, passing already-validated arrays in EngineQuery.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-044 (ignore invalid URL values; Meili path not covered)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low.

rawFindings.title: Review moderation bypass: author deletes a rejected review and re-POSTs it, which auto-approves it
rawFindings.rootCause: ISSUE-027 fixed only the update path: an existing review that is not approved goes to pending (line 52). DELETE /api/reviews/:id lets the author hard-delete a review in any status (88-93). That frees the @@unique([companyId,userId]) slot, and the next POST takes the create branch, which always writes status 'approved' (line 61). The admin hard-delete (admin.routes.ts:451-456) is bypassed the same way.
rawFindings.impact: A seeker who applied once can republish content an admin rejected or deleted, instantly and without admin involvement. It becomes public and counts toward reviewSummary and the rating sort. This breaks the product rule that moderation bypass must be impossible.
rawFindings.evidence: reviews.routes.ts:40-44 looks up existing by companyId+userId; :52 keeps 'approved' or sets 'pending' on update; :61 creates with status 'approved'; :92 only checks review.userId === sub or admin, never status. The web UI exposes delete (CompanyReviews.tsx:114). e2e has no delete-then-recreate case.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Keep a tombstone instead of hard-deleting: soft-delete (deletedAt, keep status) for author deletes of non-approved reviews and for admin deletes. On POST, if a tombstone or rejected row exists, create or update as 'pending'. Alternatively, block authors from deleting reviews that are rejected or pending. Add e2e: reject, author delete, re-POST, expect pending.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-027 (FIXED; the fix is bypassable); D-020
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low to medium: needs a schema field or a status filter in public queries and admin lists.

rawFindings.title: Verified company badge survives a company rename, allowing brand impersonation
rawFindings.rootCause: PUT /api/employer/company updates name, description, website, industry and region on the owner's company (107-120) and never touches isVerified. Nothing in src resets isVerified; grep finds 'isVerified: false' only in seed.ts. The admin verify action (admin.routes.ts:374-381) is a one-time flag, not tied to the name that was verified.
rawFindings.impact: An employer gets 'Small LLC' verified, then renames it to a well-known brand. It keeps the checkmark, is ranked first in the catalog (companies.list.ts:174 adds is_verified × 1e12 to the popular sort) and appears under verified filters (companies.list.ts:265, vacancies.service.ts:179). Candidates then apply or chat and share phone and email with the impersonator.
rawFindings.evidence: companies.routes.ts:108-120: prisma.company.update data { name: body.name, ... }, no isVerified. updateCompanySchema:39-47 requires name. Web api.ts:718 PUTs this route from the company form.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: When a verified company changes its name (and optionally website or logo), set isVerified=false or hold the change as pending until an admin approves it. Notify admins and write an audit event. Show a 'verification reset' notice in the employer UI.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: legitimate renames lose the badge until re-verified.

rawFindings.title: Pending staff invites (including admin role) stay usable after the inviting admin is blocked or demoted
rawFindings.rootCause: findUsableInvite (88-94) checks only revokedAt, acceptedAt and expiresAt. Accept (227-261) creates a user with invite.role without checking that invitedBy is still an active admin. Blocking or demoting staff (team PATCH 211-214, admin.routes.ts:197-201 and 221-224) revokes sessions and sockets but never revokes invites; staffInvite appears only in team.routes.ts. The raw link is also returned to the creating admin (152-156).
rawFindings.impact: A compromised admin session creates a role=admin invite for an attacker's email and receives the link. Owners block the admin, but the attacker can still accept for up to 7 days and gets a fresh admin account with new tokens. Pending invites do show in /api/admin/team, but nothing revokes them automatically.
rawFindings.evidence: team.routes.ts:29 has a 7-day TTL; :30 allows role admin; :243-247 claims on PENDING only; :250-258 runs user.create with role: invite.role. grep staffInvite shows no use in admin.routes.ts, auth.service.ts or the team PATCH block branch.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: On block or role change of a staff user, run staffInvite.updateMany({ invitedById: id, ...PENDING }, revokedAt: now). In accept, re-load the inviter and require role 'admin' and !isBlocked. Use a shorter TTL for admin-role invites. Emit security audit events for invite created, accepted and revoked.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: None (ISSUE-030 covers only redaction of the token from logs)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low

rawFindings.title: Push subscriptions are not tied to sessions: logout, session revocation and blocking keep delivering pushes
rawFindings.rootCause: sendPushToUser sends to every stored subscription for the user (push.ts:37-49), and notify never checks isBlocked (notifications.service.ts:84-149). Web logout (AuthContext.tsx:163-181) never calls /api/push/unsubscribe; usePush is used only in NotificationSettings.tsx:34. revokeUserSessions (auth.service.ts:166-173) only bumps tokenVersion. Admin block and role change do not delete pushSubscription rows.
rawFindings.impact: User B logs out on a shared or public computer. That browser keeps showing B's notifications (application status '«title» bo'yicha: Rad etildi', new vacancy matches, admin broadcasts) until someone else subscribes. 'Logout all devices', blocking and a future password reset (rule J) do not stop delivery to old devices.
rawFindings.evidence: AuthContext.tsx:163-181 runs bumpSessionEpoch, setAccessToken(null) and logoutUser() with no push cleanup. usePush.ts:110-121 unsubscribes only when the user toggles it off manually. push.ts:37 is findMany({ where: { userId } }). notifications.service.ts:141-149 pushes whenever the channel is enabled.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: On logout, the client should delete the endpoint on the server (while it still has the token) and call sub.unsubscribe(). On the server, store tokenVersion on PushSubscription at subscribe time and delete rows with a stale version in sendPushToUser. Delete all rows on block, role change and password reset. Skip external channels for blocked users.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-084 (related push authz, FIXED); ISSUE-041 (session revocation)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low to medium: schema field plus client logout ordering (unsubscribe before the token is dropped).

rawFindings.title: POST /api/push/subscribe accepts any https host, so the server makes outbound requests to attacker-chosen host:port
rawFindings.rootCause: pushSubSchema only requires z.string().url() (37-40). The endpoint is stored as-is and webpush.sendNotification is called without a timeout (push.ts:46-49). web-push opens https.request to the URL's hostname and port (web-push-lib.js:360-369). Subscribe also deletes any other user's row with the same endpoint (routes:189).
rawFindings.impact: Any logged-in user registers endpoints like https://internal-host:8443/x or a tarpit, then triggers their own notifications (instant saved-search alerts). The API makes blind TLS POSTs to internal or external hosts and can hang sockets; awaited broadcasts wait up to 20 s per user. Taking over another user's row needs their secret endpoint URL (low likelihood).
rawFindings.evidence: notifications.routes.ts:38 endpoint: z.string().url().max(1000); :189 deleteMany { endpoint, userId: { not: userId } }; push.ts:46-49 has no options; web-push-lib.js:362-365 uses hostname/port from the endpoint.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Allowlist https push-service hosts (fcm.googleapis.com, updates.push.services.mozilla.com, *.notify.windows.com, web.push.apple.com). Reject other hosts and non-default ports. Pass { timeout: 10000 } to sendNotification. Consider a unique key of (userId, endpoint) plus a proof-of-ownership refresh.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-084 (takeover part FIXED by the delete-then-upsert design)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: new browser push vendors would need allowlist updates.

rawFindings.title: Chat messages bypass the phone-verification gate (WS send and application status reason)
rawFindings.rootCause: requirePhoneVerified is documented for key actions including messages (auth-guard.ts:86-89) but is applied only to POST /api/conversations/start (chat.routes.ts:294). WS message frames (244-279) check only the conversation participant and, once at connect, blocked/tokenVersion (204-224). PATCH /api/applications/:id/status (applications.routes.ts:308-354) posts a chat message via deliverMessage with no phone gate.
rawFindings.impact: A verified employer opens a chat with a discoverable seeker whose phone is unverified; discoverability needs only isOpenToWork plus a published resume. That seeker can then send messages, subject only to the WS token bucket, and each message is also relayed to the recipient's Telegram. This contradicts the documented anti-spam rule. Impact is limited because the conversation must be started by a verified party.
rawFindings.evidence: chat.routes.ts:204-206 selects only isBlocked and tokenVersion; :256-278 has no isPhoneVerified check before deliverMessage. applications.routes.ts:310 preHandler is [requireAuth, requireRole] only; :350-353 calls deliverMessage.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Select isPhoneVerified in the WS ready check and answer message frames from unverified users with an error event (reads still allowed). Add requirePhoneVerified when a status reason is given. Otherwise record an explicit product decision that replies are allowed.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-060 (recommended a phone gate on the reason message; not implemented)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low; the UI needs to show a 'verify phone to reply' state.

rawFindings.title: Malformed-id handling is inconsistent: saved-search routes pass raw params to Prisma (404 via P2023, not 500)
rawFindings.rootCause: PATCH and DELETE /api/saved-searches/:id read req.params as { id } (119, 134) and call findUnique (121, 135) without idParams or isObjectId. The suspected 500 is refuted: server.ts:201-204 maps P2023 to 404. Other routes differ: idParams gives 400 VALIDATION_ERROR; team.routes.ts:160-161/178 and articles.admin.routes.ts:128-129 return 404 via isObjectId. PATCH validates the body first (120), so the status depends on body validity.
rawFindings.impact: No crash and no ownership leak, since found.userId is checked. Clients get inconsistent 400 vs 404 for the same kind of error, and correctness hinges on one global mapping; a future raw aggregate with a user-supplied $oid would return 500. e2e 1398-1421 asserts only status < 500 and omits DELETE saved-searches, team and article malformed ids.
rawFindings.evidence: alerts.routes.ts:119 `const { id } = req.params as { id: string }`; :121 savedSearch.findUnique({ where: { id } }); server.ts:202-204 P2023 → 404 NOT_FOUND; e2e-check.mjs:1412 covers only the PATCH case.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Use idParams.parse(req.params) in both alerts handlers before parsing the body. Choose one contract for malformed ids (404 recommended, to avoid distinguishing format from existence) and apply it to idParams, team and articles. Extend the e2e malformed-id matrix to DELETE saved-searches, team invites and members, and admin articles.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Very low

rawFindings.title: Candidate resume PDFs are public bearer URLs, and resumeUrl is sent to vacancy owners by an endpoint the web never calls
rawFindings.rootCause: fastifyStatic serves all of UPLOAD_DIR at /uploads/ with no auth (server.ts:174). The onSend hook only adds nosniff/CSP (163-173). @fastify/send defaults to 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=0' (SendStream.js:874-882). There is no X-Robots-Tag, robots.txt only disallows /api and page paths (seo.routes.ts:46-51), and CORP is cross-origin (server.ts:103). The only protection is that the file name is random.
rawFindings.impact: Anyone who holds a resumeUrl can download the PDF without logging in until the candidate replaces or deletes it. That includes every employer the candidate applied to (via GET /api/vacancies/:id/applications) and anyone they forward the link to. Access cannot be revoked per employer, shared caches may keep copies, and a leaked link can be indexed. Resume PDFs usually contain phone, address and birth date.
rawFindings.evidence: applications.routes.ts:294 selects jobSeekerProfile.resumeUrl for the owner/admin. The web only calls GET /api/employer/applications (web src/lib/employer/applications/api.ts:21), whose select has no resumeUrl (applications.routes.ts:194-209). In the web, resumeUrl is used only in the candidate's own profile (components/profile/ResumeFile.tsx:84). profile.routes.ts:109 saveUpload returns /uploads/resume-<hex>.pdf. D-013 accepts the risk.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Serve resume files through an authenticated route, e.g. GET /api/applications/:id/resume-file, allowed for the vacancy owner, the candidate and admin, with 'Cache-Control: private, no-store' and 'X-Robots-Tag: noindex'. Stop serving resume-* files from fastifyStatic. Interim steps: drop the unused resumeUrl from /api/vacancies/:id/applications, add no-store and noindex headers for /uploads/resume-* in onSend, and add 'Disallow: /uploads/' to robots.txt.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low to medium. The web links resumeUrl only for the owner; an authenticated route means fetching with a Bearer token and opening a blob URL.

rawFindings.title: With SMTP unset, every notification writes the recipient's email address to stdout
rawFindings.rootCause: deliver() gates the email channel only on user preference (line 90; no preference row means enabled) and never checks features.email (env.ts:187). sendUserEmail therefore reads the user's email from the DB (170-175), and sendMail's disabled fallback logs `[mail:o'chiq] ${to} — ${subject}` (mailer.ts:35-39).
rawFindings.impact: Rule B removes email as a recovery channel, so production may run without SMTP (inference). In that case every new-application or status notification logs a user's email. One admin broadcast to about 10k users (admin.routes.ts:574, all channels) writes about 10k addresses to the Railway logs and costs about 10k extra DB reads. The preferences UI already shows email as unavailable (notifications.routes.ts:138-142).
rawFindings.evidence: notifications.service.ts:88-90: `use = (c) => wanted.includes(c) && !off.has(c)`. Lines 153-155: `if (use("email")) external.push(sendUserEmail(input, absoluteUrl)...)`. Lines 171-174: `prisma.user.findUnique({ select: { email: true } })`. mailer.ts:36-38: `if (!tx) { console.log(`[mail:o'chiq] ${input.to} — ${input.subject}`)`. env.ts:187: `email: Boolean(env.SMTP_HOST)`.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: In deliver(), skip the email channel when !features.email (and likewise skip telegram/push when their flags are off) before any DB read. In mailer.ts, never log the recipient; log a counter or a masked domain at most.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Very low

rawFindings.title: Staff invite API returns the raw invite token to the admin; the token alone creates a staff or admin account
rawFindings.rootCause: POST /api/admin/team/invites builds `${WEB_ORIGIN}/admin/invite?token=<raw>` (134, 138) and returns it in JSON even when the email was sent (152-156). The admin UI shows it in a copyable input. Accepting needs only the token and a new password (227-261); the role can be 'admin' (line 30) and the link lasts 7 days (line 29).
rawFindings.impact: A bearer secret that can mint a super-admin account ends up in the admin's DOM, clipboard, screenshots and chat copy-paste, and whoever holds it chooses the password. Nothing proves ownership of the invited email. This conflicts with the owner's rule that admins never see raw tokens (rule H wording, rule I spirit). It is deliberate as a fallback when SMTP is off, hence P3.
rawFindings.evidence: team.routes.ts:134 `token = crypto.randomBytes(32)`, :138 `link = `${env.WEB_ORIGIN}/admin/invite?token=${token}``, :152-156 `send({ invite, link, emailSent })`, :30 `staffRole = z.enum(["admin", ...])`, :250-261 user.create with invite.role and the password from the request body. Web src/lib/admin/team.ts:37 types `{ invite; link; emailSent }`; components/admin/team/TeamInvite.tsx:102 `<input readOnly value={result.link}>`.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Return the link only when emailSent is false, show it once with a warning, and audit-log invite creation and acceptance. Better: never return the token, deliver it out of band, and require the invitee to confirm ownership of the invited email (a one-time code) before creating the account. Use a short TTL (e.g. 24h) for admin-role invites.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: none (ISSUE-030 only redacts this token from request logs)
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low to medium. Without SMTP, staff onboarding needs another delivery channel.

rawFindings.title: Registration reveals to guests whether an email already has an account
rawFindings.rootCause: registerUser looks the email up and immediately throws 409 'Bu email bilan foydalanuvchi allaqachon mavjud' (37-39). loginUser deliberately runs a dummy argon2 hash so response time does not reveal whether an account exists (13-17, 91-97), and register undoes that.
rawFindings.impact: A guest can check whether a given person, such as a current employee, has an ISH BOR! account, which hints at job hunting. Only the per-IP limit of 10 per minute applies (auth.routes.ts:59-64). The planned phone-based forgot-password flow (rule B) must not repeat this for phone numbers.
rawFindings.evidence: auth.service.ts:37-39: `const existing = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email } }); if (existing) throw Errors.conflict("Bu email bilan foydalanuvchi allaqachon mavjud")`. Lines 91-97: the dummy-hash path in loginUser. auth.routes.ts:59-64: strictRateLimit {max: 10, timeWindow: '1 minute'}; lines 66-71: the register route.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Give new and existing emails the same neutral response, e.g. 'if this email is free the account was created, otherwise sign in or recover', plus a per-email throttle. Apply the same identical-response rule to the future recovery start endpoint for unknown phone numbers.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium. The signup UX currently relies on the explicit conflict message, so the web signup error handling must change.

rawFindings.title: A blocked employer's company profile stays public on every company read path except the sitemap
rawFindings.rootCause: The block handler (admin.routes.ts:197-211) archives the owner's active vacancies and revokes sessions, but sets no hidden flag on the Company row. GET /api/companies/:slug (findUnique by slug), listCompanies (companies.list.ts:241-271, whose base $match has no owner condition), similarCompanies (:381-398) and seeker POST /api/conversations/start (chat.routes.ts:345-347) never check owner.isBlocked. Only sitemap-employer filters NOT owner.isBlocked (seo.routes.ts:116), so the intent exists but covers one path.
rawFindings.impact: Scenario: admin blocks the employer "X LLC" for fraud. Its vacancies are archived, but guests still get HTTP 200 on /companies/x-llc (SSR) with logo, description, website link and approved reviews. The company still appears in the catalog, in peers' similar-companies lists and in the home top-companies block (verified companies sort first). Seekers can still save it and open a chat whose recipient is a blocked account that never reads it.
rawFindings.evidence: admin.routes.ts:203-211 updateMany({companyId in, status:active} -> archived), company untouched. companies.routes.ts:187 findUnique({ where:{slug} }) with no owner filter. companies.list.ts:242-271 base filters are only text/industry/region/size/verified/saved. chat.routes.ts:345-347 findUnique by companySlug, then getOrCreateConversation(company.ownerUserId). seo.routes.ts:113-117 excludes blocked owners. Web companies/@slug/+data.ts:13-23 renders whatever the API returns; index/+data.ts:16.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add a denormalized Company.ownerBlocked (or hiddenAt) field, set and cleared in the block/unblock handler, and backfill it for owners already blocked. Filter on it in /api/companies/:slug (404), the listCompanies base $match (indexed, no extra $lookup), similarCompanies, seeker conversations/start and sitemap-employer. Call bumpDataVersion on unblock too. Add an e2e check: block employer -> detail 404 and absent from catalog and similar.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-056 (the sitemap-only exclusion). May overlap data-integrity-7 (blocked-account data) from this round; this finding covers only company read paths.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low to medium: needs a backfill and must clear on unblock; the catalog cache is invalidated by bumpDataVersion. Existing conversations with a blocked company need a product decision (keep read-only).

rawFindings.title: The applications list and chat vacancy card show rejected and in-moderation vacancy content to applicants
rawFindings.rootCause: GET /api/applications (129-157) and the GET /api/conversations vacancy context (chat.routes.ts:398-433, 483-496) load the vacancy with no status filter and return title, salary, region and company; they only compute isClosed = status !== active. Favorites was fixed to allow only active or archived (favorites.routes.ts:28, ISSUE-038), but these sibling paths were not. PUT on a rejected vacancy saves the new title and salary and moves it to moderation with no review (vacancies.routes.ts:186-214).
rawFindings.impact: Scenario: 40 seekers applied; admin rejects the vacancy for a fake title and salary (admin.routes.ts:305). The employer PUTs the title 'Oylik 30 mln, oldindan tolov @scam' plus a new salaryMin, and the status becomes moderation. Before any admin review, all 40 applicants see the unmoderated title and salary in /applications and in the /messages vacancy card, labelled only 'closed'. Low reach, because the employer could also message these applicants directly.
rawFindings.evidence: applications.routes.ts:130 where {jobSeekerId}; vacancy select includes title, status, salaryMin/Max and company (133-146). chat.routes.ts:400-402 vacancy ids per company with no status; 485-494 returns title/salary with isClosed. favorites.routes.ts:28 status in [active, archived]. vacancies.routes.ts:186,191,204-205,214. Web: lib/api.ts:690-697; ApplicationCard.tsx:65,166 and ConversationVacancyContext.tsx:27-29,41 render the title when closed.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: In both endpoints, return a redacted card when the vacancy status is moderation or rejected (no title or salary; e.g. title null, isRemoved true). Alternatively, snapshot title, company and salary on the Application at apply time and show the snapshot for non-public statuses. Keep archived as today. Extend the e2e [ISSUE-034/038] check.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low: the web already drops links when isClosed. Redaction needs a 'vacancy removed' label in uz/ru/en; a snapshot needs a schema field and a backfill.

rawFindings.title: The public vacancy detail returns the internal rejectionReason (raw include, no field whitelist)
rawFindings.rootCause: getVacancyBySlug uses include (549-562), so every Vacancy scalar goes to guests, including rejectionReason (schema.prisma:427). Only admin moderate to active clears it (admin.routes.ts:306). Moderate to archived (304-306) and employer PATCH archived to active (vacancies.routes.ts:257-263) leave it set. List, similar and company-page reads use the VACANCY_CARD_SELECT whitelist; the detail read does not.
rawFindings.impact: Scenario: admin rejects a vacancy with the reason 'Soxta kompaniya, STIR mos emas', later sets it to archived via moderate, and the employer re-activates it with PATCH (the archive re-activation flow on the skip list). GET /api/vacancies/<slug> and the SSR data payload then show that internal moderation note to every guest. Any internal field added to Vacancy later would also be public by default.
rawFindings.evidence: vacancies.service.ts:549-563 findUnique with include {company select, region true, category true}; 575 returns the spread object. admin.routes.ts:305-306 clears the reason only on active. vacancies.routes.ts:257-263 PATCH writes only status and publishedAt. On the web, rejectionReason is read only by the employer view (VacancyRow.tsx:85, employer adapter.ts:69), so dropping it from the public detail is safe.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Replace include with an explicit VACANCY_DETAIL_SELECT (card fields plus description, conditions, contacts, images, address) that leaves out rejectionReason. Also clear rejectionReason on every transition to active or archived (moderate archived, PATCH active).
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-032 (whitelist applied to company fields, not the vacancy detail). The leak path depends on the archive re-activation finding (skip list).
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low. Check that apps/web/src/lib/vacancies/detail.ts reads only fields kept in the new select (inference: it maps named fields).

rawFindings.title: No read path applies vacancy expiry, and the JSON-LD outputs a past validThrough
rawFindings.rootCause: createVacancy (645-672), PATCH status and admin moderate never set expiresAt, and no read path filters on it: buildFilters (210-240), detail (563), similar (590-611), company page (companies.routes.ts:206), sitemap (seo.routes.ts:100), Meili (search.service.ts:238), salary stats (salary.stats.ts:168). Only demo-seed.ts:1714 writes expiresAt. +Head.tsx:59 outputs validThrough whenever expiresAt exists, even if past, while ApplyCard.tsx:51 hides a past deadline.
rawFindings.impact: Postings stay public until the employer archives them by hand. At tens of thousands of vacancies, the list, the sitemap and salary stats (built from the newest 20k rows) fill up with stale jobs. For seeded or imported rows older than 30 days, Google receives a JobPosting whose validThrough is in the past on a live page, and the UI and JSON-LD disagree.
rawFindings.evidence: Grepping expiresAt in apps/api/src finds only vacancies.service.ts:92 (select) and demo-seed.ts:1714 (publishedAt + 30 days). +Head.tsx:59 ...(vacancy.expiresAt ? { validThrough: vacancy.expiresAt } : {}). ApplyCard.tsx:51 checks expiresAt > Date.now(). ISSUES.md ISSUE-072 is PARTIAL: validThrough was not done and vacancies stay active forever.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Product decision first (ISSUE-072). Minimal fix now: in +Head.tsx, output validThrough only when it is in the future (same check as ApplyCard). If expiry is adopted: set expiresAt on activation; add an indexed 'expiresAt null or > now' condition to buildFilters, detail, similar, sitemap and company page; add a sweep that archives and de-indexes expired rows.
rawFindings.fixRisk: The Head change is trivial. An expiry sweep would close existing active vacancies, so it needs a backfill or grace period and e2e updates.

rawFindings.title: Phone-verification gate notice is silent: a blocked Apply/Publish/Message gives screen readers no feedback
rawFindings.rootCause: PhoneGateNotice renders a plain div with no role=alert/status, no aria-live and no focus target. Callers mount it only after the API returns PHONE_NOT_VERIFIED, while focus stays on the button that triggered the action. The only change a screen reader user perceives is the button's busy state ending.
rawFindings.impact: WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages (AA) failure on core flows in uz/ru/en: candidate Apply on /vacancies/:slug, employer Publish/Save draft, applications message/status actions, vacancy list actions, candidate search chat, company review/actions. Screen reader users cannot learn why nothing happened or that Telegram phone verification is required.
rawFindings.evidence:
PhoneGateNotice.tsx:9-18 `
` with no role. Mounted at ApplyCard.tsx:142 (the failed-apply `

` right below at :144 IS announced), FormSidebar.tsx:234 (VacancyForm.tsx:224 `if (isPhoneGateError(err)) return setGated(true);`), ApplicationSidebar.tsx:115, EmployerVacanciesView.tsx:180, pages/employer/candidates/+Page.tsx:138, CompanyActions.tsx:81, CompanyReviews.tsx:240. None of these call sites wraps it in a live region.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Put role="alert" on the PhoneGateNotice root (it only mounts after a failed action), or render it inside a live region that is always present. Optionally add tabIndex=-1 and focus it after gating, as NotificationsView does for its notices.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low. If a call site also shows its own alert, the message may be announced twice; check all 7 call sites.

rawFindings.title: Profile/resume editors: required fields not exposed; validation errors neither announced nor focused
rawFindings.rootCause:
The shared profile Field marks required fields with an aria-hidden `*` and no sr-only text, and inputs get no required/aria-required. On submit, editors set error text in a plain

and return early, leaving focus on Save/Next with no summary and no focus move. The vacancy form primitives already solve all of this but the profile editors do not reuse them.
rawFindings.impact: WCAG 1.3.1/3.3.2 (A) and 4.1.3 (AA) failures on /profile (resume wizard step 2, experience, education, personal) in all locales. A screen reader user presses Next or Save with an empty required field and hears nothing. SaveStatus's aria-live stays idle because validation returns before saver.run.
rawFindings.evidence:
ui.tsx:100-104 has only `*`. TextInput :136-146 sets no aria-required. The error

at :107-110 has no role. ProfessionalInfo.tsx:45-47 sets titleError and returns false (required Field at :70). ExperienceList.tsx:243-253 validates and returns early at :260 (required fields :274, :288, :300). EducationList.tsx:209-220 and :227-229 (required :243, :266). PersonalInfo.tsx:76-78 shows the phone error, then returns. ui.tsx:95 keeps hintId in aria-describedby even when the error replaces the hint (:107-115), leaving a dangling reference. The vacancy form does this correctly: FormControls.tsx:40-46 and FormSidebar.tsx:228-233.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: In ui.tsx Field, add sr-only '(required)' text and pass required through so children set aria-required. On a failed submit, render errors with role=alert or focus the first invalid input. Build aria-describedby from the elements actually rendered.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low, but the primitive is shared by many editors. Check that errors are not announced twice when SaveStatus also changes.

rawFindings.title: Resume wizard and inline resume editors drop keyboard focus to <body> on step change, save, cancel, upload or delete
rawFindings.rootCause: Step content sits in `<div key={key}>`, so goStep remounts the subtree that holds the focused Back/Next buttons. Nothing moves focus to the new step or announces it. Inline editors, skill chips and the resume file card remove the focused control the same way. pages/profile/+Page.tsx only scrolls and lib/profile/tabs.ts has no focus logic.
rawFindings.impact: WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (A) and 1.3.1 (A) on /profile?tab=resume&step=N in all locales. After each Next, keyboard and screen reader users restart from the top of the document and are not told which step loaded. The desktop stepper shows completed steps only visually, and the step number drops out of the accessible name.
rawFindings.evidence: ResumeWizard.tsx:137 `<div key={key} className="animate-fade-in ...">` wraps StepFooter (:141, :152-160, :169, :176, :183, :194); the buttons are at :221-233. The h1 at :69 has no ref or tabIndex, and the step counter at :75-77 is not live. Stepper :112-122 replaces the number with IconCheck (aria-hidden, profile/icons.tsx:21) and adds no sr-only done text (compare FormSteps.tsx:64-65). pages/profile/+Page.tsx:72-81 only calls scrollTo. ExperienceList.tsx:88, :90, :116 setEditor(null) and :54 delete; EducationList.tsx:70, :96, :157; SkillsEditor.tsx:167 chip remove button; ResumeFile.tsx:100 dropzone is replaced by the card (:73) after upload.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Give the wizard or step heading tabIndex=-1 and focus it in an effect on step change (not on first render). Add a polite live 'Step x of 6'. Add sr-only done text to the stepper. After editor close or delete, return focus to the trigger or the new card; after chip removal, to the input; after upload/remove, to the new file controls.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low to medium: the focus effects must skip the initial render so they don't steal focus on page load.

rawFindings.title: Employer applications workspace loses focus after status changes and on mobile select/back
rawFindings.rootCause: ApplicationSidebar is keyed by `${id}-${status}`, so a successful status update remounts it and destroys the focused Update button or quick-action trigger; useDialog then calls focus() on the detached trigger. Below 1024px, selecting an application hides the list without focusing the detail, and Back unmounts the detail without restoring focus. /messages handles both of these focus moves; this view does not.
rawFindings.impact: WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (A) on /employer/applications in all locales. Employers working through many applications with a keyboard or screen reader lose their place after every Invite/Accept/Reject/Update. The role=status notice is announced, but focus jumps to <body>.
rawFindings.evidence: EmployerApplicationsView.tsx:214 `key={`${selected.id}-${selected.status}`}`. applyStatus (:160-176) changes the status and closes the dialog in the same render. ApplicationSidebar.tsx:104 is the submit button; :62-65 filters quick buttons by the new status; :129 is reject. useDialog.ts:25 captures the trigger and :59 calls `trigger?.focus?.()` on a removed node. Mobile: select (:139-148) only scrolls; :204, :228, :250, :290 hide the header and list; ApplicationDetail.tsx:177-185 Back leads to :308, which clears the selection. Compare MessagesView.tsx:82-116. Minor: StatusTabs.tsx:44 aria-controls='applications-list' points to a tabpanel (ApplicationList.tsx:95) that is not rendered when there are no results or the mobile detail is open.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Key the sidebar by application id only and reset its local state in an effect when status changes, or focus the status card heading after applyStatus. On mobile select, focus the detail h2 (tabIndex=-1). On Back, refocus [data-application-row=id] as MessagesView does. Set aria-controls only when the panel exists.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Medium: dropping status from the key needs a manual reset of the `next`/`reason` state in ApplicationSidebar.

rawFindings.title: Employer company form: required name not indicated, errors and success not announced, Uzbek error text on ru/en
rawFindings.rootCause: This older form doesn't use the shared FormControls. It has bare label wrappers, no required marker, a submit button that is disabled with no explanation, and error/success text as plain elements with no live role. Error fallback strings are hardcoded in Uzbek.
rawFindings.impact: Employer /profile company setup, which employers need before posting vacancies, in uz/ru/en. 3.3.2 (A): the name is not marked required and Save is disabled with no reason. 4.1.3 (AA)/3.3.1 (A): save and logo errors appear at the bottom in brand blue with no announcement, and the 'saved' message disappears after 2.5 s unannounced. 3.1.2 (AA): 'Xatolik yuz berdi' shows on /ru and /en pages with no lang attribute.
rawFindings.evidence:
EmployerCompanyForm.tsx:167-168: label 'Kompaniya nomi' (messages.uz.ts:661) and a `required` input, with no asterisk or hint. :208 `disabled={saving || !name.trim()}`. :220 `{error &&

{error}

}`. :213 the saved has no role and is cleared at :93. :48, :61, :95 fall back to 'Xatolik yuz berdi' (api.ts:127 defaults to 'Xatolik'). Logo errors (:48, :61) also render at :220, far from the logo buttons at :132-149. The logo preview img (:113-119) has alt="", so whether a logo is set is not exposed.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Rebuild on FormControls Field/TextInput with a required marker plus sr-only text. Keep Save enabled and show a field error with focus on submit. Render errors with role=alert in danger colour next to the relevant control. Give the saved message role=status. Replace hardcoded fallbacks with t.* keys. Give the logo preview a meaningful alt.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Low to medium: replacing the custom Select changes the visuals; keep the saveMyCompany payload unchanged.

rawFindings.title: Admin list screens: search input without a label, empty action column header, rating label ignored
rawFindings.rootCause: AdminSearchInput renders an input with only a placeholder: no label, no id, no aria-label. AdminTable callers pass `<th> </th>` for the actions column. The reviews rating puts aria-label on a generic span, which ARIA does not allow. The table headers themselves (th inside thead) and the notices are fine.
rawFindings.impact: Admin users/vacancies/companies search in uz/ru/en: the field's purpose rests on a placeholder that disappears once you type (3.3.2). The empty header leaves the action buttons without a column name for screen readers. Ratings are read as star glyphs. Admin-only polish.
rawFindings.evidence: AdminShell.tsx:216-221 `<input value=... placeholder={placeholder} ...>` has no label or aria-label, while AdminSelect (:238-249) does have aria-label. Empty headers: pages/admin/users/+Page.tsx:124, vacancies :138, companies :102, reviews :112, payments :116. reviews/+Page.tsx:125 `<span ... aria-label={`${row.rating}/5`}>` containing '★'.repeat(...). AdminTable at AdminShell.tsx:133-140 uses thead/th correctly; AdminNotice (AdminStates.tsx:45-48) is a live region.
rawFindings.recommendedFix: Add aria-label={placeholder} (or a visually hidden label) and type=search to AdminSearchInput. Use `actions`. Give the rating role=img with an aria-label, or sr-only text plus aria-hidden stars. Optionally make the first cell ``.
rawFindings.fixRisk: Very low.
rawFindings.relatedExistingIssue: ISSUE-075 (PARTIAL: label added to candidate search only; admin search still has none)

gaps.checklistItem: 2G search correctness and relevance (not only performance)
gaps.whyUncovered: Every 2G finding is about performance (db-perf-3, db-perf-5, scale-10k-4/10/11). None checks result correctness. Current code: vacancies.service.ts:137-143 searchTerms only trims and splits on whitespace, drops terms shorter than 2 characters, silently caps at 6 terms, and has no apostrophe-variant or Latin/Cyrillic normalization. Matching is Prisma contains/insensitive (vacancies.service.ts:172,253). Apostrophe variants are handled only in company industry patterns (companies.list.ts:29) and slugs (common/slug.ts:28). The Meilisearch path (search.service.ts:232-258) and the Mongo fallback have never been compared.
gaps.finderPrompt: READ-ONLY audit of search correctness. Do not start Meilisearch, the DB or servers. Files: apps/api/src/modules/vacancies/vacancies.service.ts (searchTerms :137, resolveFilterIds :160-200, text where builders :172/:253), apps/api/src/modules/search/search.service.ts (index settings, document builder, searchVacancyIds :232+, sync/reindex triggers), companies/companies.list.ts:240-260, candidates/candidates.routes.ts:44, articles/articles.routes.ts:92 (searchText build in articles.content.ts), admin/admin.routes.ts:39, and the web search inputs (apps/web/src/pages/vacancies, companies). Check: (1) Uzbek apostrophe variants o' oʻ o‘ o’ ` and g' in queries vs stored text; (2) Latin vs Cyrillic Uzbek and Russian queries; (3) the silent 2-character minimum and 6-term cap, and whether the query length has a zod max; (4) whether the Meilisearch and Mongo drivers return the same result set, total and order for the same query and filters (employment=remote OR workplaceType, salary range, verified, company); (5) whether index documents are updated or removed when a vacancy changes status, a company is blocked or verified, or an owner is blocked (stale hits); (6) behaviour for an empty query with filters and for punctuation-only queries. Report only confirmed defects: severity, file:line evidence, and a concrete example query with its wrong result. Mark inferences.

gaps.checklistItem: 2C per-endpoint IDOR matrix (GET/POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE) plus malformed-id handling (2D)
gaps.whyUncovered: The authz findings cover identity binding, moderation and privacy design, but no finding records per-endpoint ownership verification. Spot checks show notifications.routes.ts:88-111, reviews.routes.ts:88-93 and alerts.routes.ts:118-138 do check ownership. However, alerts.routes.ts:120,135 read `req.params as { id: string }` with no ObjectId validation, which likely turns a malformed id into a P2023 500. No finding mentions these modules: push subscriptions, favorites/saved companies, PeerRating (schema.prisma:523), application detail/withdraw, resume, candidate detail, company logo/cover upload and delete, vacancy status and delete, support routes, staff invites. admin-staff-15 notes the E2E suite has no negative authz tests.
gaps.finderPrompt: READ-ONLY IDOR sweep. Enumerate every route in apps/api/src/modules/**/*.routes.ts, server.ts and WS frame handlers (chat.routes.ts, common/realtime.ts), with method, path and preHandler guards. For each route that takes an id, slug or token in params, query or body, verify scoping against the caller: seeker A vs seeker B; employer who owns company A vs company B; content_author vs content_editor vs admin (articles.permissions.ts); blocked user; phone-unverified user. Priority targets not covered by existing findings: push subscribe/unsubscribe (can one user delete or overwrite another user's endpoint?), favorites and saved companies, PeerRating (rating a conversation the caller is not in, or rating twice), applications by id (GET, withdraw, status PATCH, reason message), resume and candidate detail for hidden or not-open-to-work profiles, company PUT/logo/cover/delete, vacancy PUT/DELETE/status transitions, support routes, staff-invite GET and accept (a race on single use), and article cover upload/delete. Also list every handler that passes raw req.params ids to Prisma without idParams/isObjectId (e.g. alerts.routes.ts:120,135) and check the error handler (server.ts setErrorHandler) to confirm whether malformed ids return 500. Report only confirmed defects with file:line and the attacker/victim scenario. Skip issues already listed (Telegram link, Google merge, archive bypass, candidate DB exposure, public PDF URLs).

gaps.checklistItem: 2C candidate private data / 2E serialization: field-level PII exposure across API, WS and SSR outputs (rule B: nothing secret returned)
gaps.whyUncovered: Only partial slices are covered: candidate DB names and resumes (authz-idor-6, employer-flows-7), reviewer names (employer-flows-8), owner user IDs (authz-idor-10). No finding traces which responses carry email, phone, additionalPhone, telegramChatId/telegramUsername, googleId, tokenVersion or isBlocked, or to which audience. Prisma includes mostly use explicit select (e.g. alerts.service.ts:142), so any leak would sit in select objects and serializers, and none of those has been reviewed field by field. This gap is an inference: exposure has not been verified.
gaps.finderPrompt: READ-ONLY field-level exposure audit. Grep every `select:` object and response mapper in apps/api/src/modules/** and common/realtime.ts (WS payloads such as {type:'message'}, read receipts, presence). Cover chat.routes.ts (conversation list, messages, participants), applications.routes.ts (seeker and employer views), candidates.routes.ts (list and detail), companies.routes.ts and companies.list.ts (public page, owner), reviews, PeerRating, profile.routes.ts (me and any public profile), auth.routes.ts/auth.service.ts (login, refresh, me, Google, Telegram poll responses), admin.routes.ts and team.routes.ts, og.routes.ts, seo.routes.ts sitemaps, vacancy contact fields, and web JSON-LD/SSR data (apps/web/src/lib/**, pages/**/+data.ts, pageContext passToClient in pages/+config.ts). For each personal or auth field (email, phone, additionalPhone, isPhoneVerified, telegramChatId, telegramUsername, googleId, passwordHash or hasPassword, tokenVersion, isBlocked, birth date, address, resume PDF URL, vacancy contact phone/email), state which audience receives it: guest, any logged-in user, any employer, an employer with an application from that candidate, a conversation peer, or admin. Report as defects only exposures that exceed 'candidate private data only to authorized employers' or return any auth secret. Evidence: file:line. Do not repeat already-listed candidate DB, review-name or owner-ID findings unless the current scope is broader.

gaps.checklistItem: Draft/public visibility rule across all read surfaces (2C vacancies, 2M, 2Q)
gaps.whyUncovered: Existing findings cover moderation transitions (authz-idor-4, employer-flows-6/14) and blocked-account data (data-integrity-7). No finding checks every read path for non-public vacancies (draft, moderation, rejected, archived, closed) or unpublished articles. The Meilisearch filter applies status=active at query time (search.service.ts:238), but OG image, similar vacancies, favorites, chat vacancy cards, alert digests, salary stats and article public routes were not checked for status filtering.
gaps.finderPrompt: READ-ONLY visibility audit. List every path that can return a vacancy, company or article to a guest or to a user other than the owner: vacancy detail by slug and id, similar vacancies, company page vacancies and /similar, home featured lists, favorites and saved companies, the seeker's applications list, chat conversation vacancy card (chat.routes.ts), notification links, alert digests (alerts.service.ts), og.routes.ts image endpoints, seo.routes.ts sitemaps, the Meilisearch document builder and Mongo fallback, stats/salary.stats.ts, Telegram texts, articles.routes.ts public list and detail (draft, in_review, archived) and article cover files. For each, verify the filters for vacancy status (draft, moderation, rejected, archived, closed), expiry, company blocked or unverified, owner blocked, and article status. Report only paths where a non-public record's title, salary, company or content reaches a guest or another user, including via slug guessing or an old favorite/application id, and the web SSR page that renders it (apps/web/src/pages/vacancies/@slug, companies/@slug, articles). Give file:line evidence and a concrete scenario. Skip issues already listed: admin approval of drafts, archive re-activation, rejection bypass.

gaps.checklistItem: 2O accessibility of complex forms and dynamic content
gaps.whyUncovered: The a11y findings cover global components (dialogs, Select, LanguageSwitcher, header overlays, contrast, motion, StarInput, skip link) and only the login/signup forms (a11y-ui-3). None covers the largest forms or the dynamic areas: employer VacancyForm, ResumeWizard, company form, chat composer and message list, application status UI, notification notices, admin tables. The per-locale html lang attribute and image alt text are not mentioned. Whether issues exist there is an inference.
gaps.finderPrompt: READ-ONLY accessibility audit. Do not run the app. Files: apps/web/src/components/employer/vacancies/VacancyForm.tsx, components/profile/ResumeWizard.tsx and sibling profile editors, the company form component under components/employer or components/companies, components/messages/* (composer, message list, ConversationDetails), components/employer/applications/EmployerApplicationsView.tsx, components/notifications/NotificationsView.tsx, admin table components under components/admin, and the root document/Head (components/HeadDefault.tsx, renderer or +Layout) for the per-locale <html lang>. Check: label/input association and aria-describedby for validation errors; an error summary or focus move on submit failure; required-field indication; aria-live for new chat messages, send failures, toasts and notices; keyboard operation of multi-step wizard navigation and custom chips or toggles; alt text on company logos, avatars and illustrations; table headers and scope in admin lists; whether lang follows uz/ru/en on SSR and after client navigation. Report only confirmed WCAG 2.1 AA failures with file:line, the affected locale or page, and severity (P2 for blockers in core flows, P3 for polish). Do not repeat issues already listed (dialogs, Select, contrast, motion, StarInput, skip link, login/signup errors).
